  and Mather sets, establish their compactness and inclusion properties,
  and investigate their convergence as the time step tends to zero.
  We prove upper-limit results for the Mañé sets and, when the continuous
  Aubry set has finitely many static classes, for the Aubry sets. We obtain
  full Kuratowski and Hausdorff convergence of the Aubry sets when this
  set is a single equilibrium or periodic orbit, and, under additional
  assumptions, a finite union of equilibria. Every weak limit of discrete
  Mather measures is a continuous Mather measure. For equilibrium Aubry
  sets, we give sufficient conditions for exact preservation of
  Mather sets and measure families at small time steps. A mechanical
  example illustrates these results and exhibits exact preservation
  of the Aubry set as well.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Rapid stabilization for Stokes and Navier-Stokes systems with localized disturbance
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this study, we analyze the rapid stabilization of Stokes and the two- and three-dimensional Navier-Stokes systems in the presence of an unknown spatially localized disturbance. A multivalued feedback control strategy is proposed which combines the Lyapunov frequency method with the multivalued sign operator. This methodology connects Lyapunov-based stability analysis with spectral inequalities, while the inclusion of the sign operator provides robustness against disturbance. The closed-loop system is governed by a differential inclusion, for which well-posedness is proved via the theory of maximal monotone operators. This approach guarantees global rapid exponential stabilization for the Stokes system and local rapid exponential stabilization for the two- and three-dimensional Navier-Stokes systems, with arbitrarily large disturbance bounds. In three dimensions, we obtain global strong solutions and rapid exponential stabilization for initial data sufficiently small in the $L^2$-norm with a prescribed, arbitrarily large bound in the $H^1$-norm.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Collapsed translating solitons with planar wings
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study complete embedded translating solitons in R^3 with finite genus and finite entropy. We prove that such collapsed translators whose wings are all of planar type (in a weak topological sense) must be vertical flat planes.
  In particular, this implies the non-existence result for gluing and doubling constructions involving planes that was conjectured in (14) and announced in (9) as an application of the authors' techniques, under weaker assumptions than previous rigidity results by Khan and Lynch-Tinaglia in (17,19,20).
  A key ingredient is a sharp new a priori decay estimate in the exterior problem for the horizontal graphical translator equation, showing that bounded solutions to the nonlinear equation, and their gradients, are controlled by multiples of the Green's function of the linear drift Laplacian, regardless of the size of the given L^\infty data. Combined with a graphical description of the infinite ends and the Neves-Tian flux identity, this yields the main rigidity result.
  As another application, we obtain a full classification of collapsed embedded finite-genus translators of entropy lambda < 3.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Hardy spaces $\mathcal{H}^{p}_{FIO}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ for Fourier integral operators for $p<1$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We introduce the Hardy spaces $\mathcal{H}^{p}_{FIO}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ for Fourier integral operators for $0<p<1$, thereby extending earlier constructions for $1\leq p\leq \infty$. We then establish various properties of these spaces, including their behavior under complex interpolation and duality, and their invariance under Fourier integral operators. We also obtain Sobolev embeddings, equivalent characterizations, and a molecular decomposition. These spaces are used in the companion article arXiv:2502.02511 to determine the sharp $\mathcal{H}^{1}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ and $\mathrm{bmo}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ regularity of wave equations with rough coefficients.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 31 pages. Minor changes to the previous version. To appear in Journal of Fourier Analysis and Applications. Originally part of arXiv:2502.02511

Functional Analysis.title: Failure of noncommutative Rota's theorem with $L\log L$ endpoint
Functional Analysis.summary: We construct a factorizable Markov map $T$ on a hyperfinite finite von Neumann algebra and a positive element $x\in L\log L$ for which the sequence $T^n(T^*)^n x$ does not converge bilaterally almost uniformly. This answers a question of Anantharaman-Delaroche \cite{AD2006}.

Functional Analysis.title: Searching for the power rangers
Functional Analysis.summary:
We develop a method for studying centralizers of generic elements in some large Polish groups. We identify a condition which enables us to show that the range of each power map is comeager; a strengthening of this condition allows us to prove that a generic element embeds in a flow (a continuous, one-parameter subgroup).
  This approach enables us to answer the question that motivated this work : we prove that a generic isometry of the Urysohn space (or the Urysohn sphere) embeds in a flow. We also obtain information on the centralizer of a generic isometry; we show that it contains an infinite-dimensional torus and that torsion elements are dense in it. To illustrate the flexibility of our method, we apply it to two other Polish groups. The first is the group of measure-preserving automorphisms of a standard probability space, and we recover results of King and of de la Rue and de Sam Lazaro. Finally we apply our technique to the group of nonsingular automorphisms of a standard probability space, and we deduce that a generic nonsingular automorphism embeds in a flow, answering a question of Danilenko and Silva.

Functional Analysis.title: Short curves in homogeneous spaces of the unitary group for unitarily invariant norms
Functional Analysis.summary: Let A be a unital *-subalgebra of $M_n(C)$ and let $M = U(n)/U(A)$, with the quotient Finsler metric induced by a unitarily invariant norm on $u(n)$, normalized so that $||iP|| = 1$ for rank-one projections $P$. This family contains the unitary orbits of Hermitian matrices, in particular flag manifolds and Grassmann manifolds. We prove that if $z_0$ is a minimal lifting of a tangent vector $X$ with $||X||_{\infty} < π/2$, then the one-parameter group $t \mapsto e^{t z_0}\cdot o$ has minimal length among all piecewise smooth curves in $M$ joining its endpoints. The same holds in manifolds $N=SU(n)/(SU(n) \cap A)$ for every Ad-invariant Finsler norm on $su(n)$, not necessarily symmetric (i.e. the unit sphere does not need to be balanced). The proof relies on the convexity of the distance from the identity along geodesic segments, valid for all these norms. We also prove that the ball of radius $π/2$ around the identity, for the spectral norm, is convex along one-parameter segments. This extends known results for the p-Schatten norms with p even, and gives a new proof for the operator norm, where the result is due to Duran, Mata-Lorenzo and Recht.

Functional Analysis.title: A sphere obstruction for the Hilbert shift quotient
Functional Analysis.summary:
Let $\mathcal H=\ell^2(\mathbb Z)$ and let $\mathbb Z$ act by bilateral shifts. We prove that the quotient $\mathbb S(\mathcal H)/\mathbb Z$ of the unit sphere, equipped with its quotient metric, has infinite Hilbert distortion. Consequently, $\mathcal H/\mathbb Z$ does not admit a bilipschitz embedding into Hilbert space, answering a question of Cahill, Iverson, and Mixon.
  The proof first embeds every flat torus $\mathbb R^n/L$, after rescaling, into the quotient $\mathbb S\big(\ell^2(\mathbb Z^n)\big)/\mathbb Z^n$ with distortion arbitrarily close to $1$, where $\mathbb Z^n$ acts by translations. We then show that every finite subset of this quotient embeds into $\mathbb S(\mathcal H)/\mathbb Z$ with distortion arbitrarily close to $1$. The lower bounds of Khot and Naor for the Hilbert distortion of flat tori then imply the result.
Functional Analysis.comment: The proof of the main theorem was found using OpenAI's ChatGPT 5.5

Functional Analysis.title: Geometric Properties of Higher Dimensional Solenoidal Attractors
Functional Analysis.summary:
We study the skew product systems $T: \mathbb{S}^1\times\mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{S}^1 \times\mathbb{R}^d$, \begin{equation*}
  T(x,y)=(\ell x, A y+φ(x)), \end{equation*} where $\ell\geq 2,$ $A \in GL_d(\mathbb{R})$ with $ρ(A)<1$, and $φ\in C^r(\mathbb{S}^1, \mathbb{R}^d)$, with $r>(d+3)/2. We allow the fibers to have any dimension and $A$ to be non-conformal. We show that: when $|\det(A)|\ell<1$, for almost every $φ$, the Hausdorff dimension of the solenoid attractor and the SRB measure equal 1+ the affinity dimension; when $|\det(A)|\ell>1$, for almost every $φ$, the SRB measure is absolutely continuous. In the latter case we investigate the Sobolev regularity of the density of the SRB measure. We introduce a derivative dispersion condition, replacing the usual transversality condition.

Functional Analysis.title: The stability landscape in wave-packet scattering: geometric rigidity and sharp Sobolev thresholds
Functional Analysis.summary: A central problem in harmonic analysis is to understand how frequency resolution constrains stability under nonlinear changes of coordinates. Motivated by Mallat's wavelet scattering theory, we establish a sharp resolution--robustness principle for nonlinear representations built from two-dimensional wave-packet systems, showing that the transverse geometry of the frequency channels determines the critical Sobolev regularity. Whenever the channels are thinner than in the wavelet regime, arbitrarily small smooth deformations can move high-frequency mass between adjacent channels, producing instability already at the level of the linear filter bank and the first scattering layer. We match this obstruction with scale-sharp commutator estimates propagated through the full scattering cascade, obtaining Lipschitz stability at the critical regularity threshold. Together, the results provide the first intrinsic deformation-stability theory for non-wavelet Euclidean scattering transforms and identify a microlocal transport mechanism governing robustness across nonlinear multiscale representations.
Functional Analysis.comment: 52 pages; 2 figures; endpoint stability extended to the full non-wavelet parameter range; minor expository improvements

Functional Analysis.title: Bounded symbols and one-component geometry
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove that every bounded truncated Toeplitz operator on a Hardy model space admits a bounded symbol if and only if its defining inner function is one-component, meaning that it has a connected sublevel set at some level in $(0,1)$. This resolves the bounded symbol conjecture of Baranov, Chalendar, Fricain, Mashreghi and Timotin and, through known equivalences, the embedding and weak factorization conjecture of Baranov, Bessonov and Kapustin. A uniform bound $R$ for the ratio of least bounded symbol norm to operator norm on the rank-one family associated with point evaluation in the disk already forces this geometry. The corresponding bound for all bounded truncated Toeplitz operators is at most $CR\log(e+R)$, where $C$ is absolute, and the logarithmic factor is optimal. In a nonzero de Branges space, the same geometric condition characterizes when every sufficiently small equivalent change of norm preserving the de Branges structure is represented exactly by reweighting the original integral with a positive density bounded above and away from zero. This characterization remains valid when the norm changes are restricted to discrete sampling norms. Outside the one-component class, every model space admits self-adjoint trace class truncated Toeplitz operators without bounded symbols, with arbitrarily small norm and singular values satisfying any prescribed positive upper bounds.
Functional Analysis.comment: 29 pages. All results first posted 7 Oct 2026, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23214254

Functional Analysis.title: Optimal weighted sampling of positive and normal operator orbits
Functional Analysis.summary:
We study weighted sampling of operator orbit frames in infinite dimensional separable Hilbert spaces \(H\), keeping the operator and generating vectors fixed. Let $N_μ(R)$ count the sampling times in $[0,R]$. For a single orbit of a positive operator, let $m_A(R)$ count the eigenvalues in $(0,e^{-1/R}]$. Every real sampling design that preserves the frame property must satisfy the lower bound $N_μ(R)\ge m_A(R)-O_μ(1)$. Conversely, for every $η>0$, we construct an integer sampling design that preserves the frame property and satisfies $N_μ(R)\le(1+η)m_A(R)+O_η(1)$. Thus the coefficient $1$ is optimal. Under additional spectral conditions, we attain $N_μ(R)=m_A(R)+O(1)$ and characterize the weights that preserve the frame property on the constructed sets.
  For finitely or countably many orbits of a positive operator, let $P_j$, $j\ge1$, be the spectral projection corresponding to $2^{-j-1}<-\logλ\le2^{-j}$ and define $K_A(R)=\#\{j\ge1:2^j\le R,\ P_j\ne0\}$. Every real sampling design that preserves the frame property satisfies $N_μ(R)\ge c_μK_A(R)-C_μ$ for $R\ge2$, with constants $c_μ>0$ and $C_μ\ge0$. Conversely, we construct an integer sampling design that preserves the frame property and satisfies $N_μ(R)\le L K_A(R)+L$ for $R\ge2$, where $L$ depends only on the bounds of the given orbit frame.
  For normal operators of norm one, we prove that the smallest frame condition number is attained among integer sampling designs that preserve the frame property and satisfy a prescribed counting bound, whenever this class is nonempty. Finally, we construct one normal operator with two families of generating vectors for which the optimal growth orders of $N_μ(R)$ are $\log R$ and $R$, respectively, for both real and integer sampling.

Functional Analysis.title: Chaos of Caputo derivative
Functional Analysis.summary: We study bounded realizations of Caputo differentiation on coefficient Banach spaces of fractional power series. The main contribution is an explicit quantitative analysis of local approximation and periodic reconstruction. We determine the least possible simultaneous error in the initial displacement and the prescribed target. The optimal value is attained, and a minimizing perturbation is given explicitly. We also solve the exact-arrival problem and establish uniqueness of its least-norm solution. These formulas provide computable approximation times and identify the sharp threshold for hypercyclicity, mixing and Devaney chaos. Every periodic point is described by a finite block whose geometric repetition yields exact norm formulas. The resulting approximations attain any prescribed sufficiently large minimal period near any given vector. For distinct positive powers, a simultaneous block construction gives quantitative error estimates and the same sharp threshold for disjoint mixing. Compact embeddings relate the Banach realizations to the Mittag-Leffler-Caputo Fréchet space. They also exhibit dense stable invariant subspaces inside chaotic realizations. The local approximation condition is a norm formulation of classical transitivity. Its quantitative evaluation, together with explicit periodic and simultaneous reconstruction, provides the central results of the study.

Functional Analysis.title: Stable topology and stable compactness
Functional Analysis.summary: To solve a large class of noncompact problems ubiquitous in random functional analysis and its applications, most of compactness-based fundamental theorems established for normed spaces or locally convex spaces are required to be extended for random normed modules and random locally convex modules in an appropriate way of weakening compactness. To achieve this goal, in this paper we first develop stable set theory by introducing some new set-theoretic tools, then propose a class of topological spaces with a stable structure, called stable topological spaces, and in particular propose and systematically develop the theory of stably compact spaces, which is a natural generalization of that of compact spaces. The resulting theory is of independent interest from the perspective of general topology since its investigation requires an analysis of stratification structures coordinated with partitions of unity in a complete Boolean algebra. Finally, we show the power of the theory of stable compactness by establishing random Banach-Alaoglu, random James and random Banach-Bourbaki-Kakutani-Šmulian theorems.

Functional Analysis.title: An elementary proof of rational injectivity in equivariant KK-theory
Functional Analysis.summary: Antonini, Azzali and Skandalis proved that, for every countable discrete group $Γ$, the canonical map $EΓ\to\underline{E}Γ$ induces a split injection in equivariant $KK$-theory with real coefficients. In this paper, we give a more elementary proof of the corresponding rational injectivity result in ordinary equivariant $KK$-theory without using $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors.

Functional Analysis.title: Persistence of gaps in the spectrum of certain almost periodic operators
Functional Analysis.summary: It is shown that for any irrational rotation number and any admissible gap labelling number the almost Mathieu operator (also known as Harper's operator) has a gap in its spectrum with that labelling number. This answers the strong version of the so-called "Ten Martini Problem". When specialized to the particular case where the coupling constant is equal to one, it follows that the "Hofstadter butterfly" has for any quantum Hall conductance the exact number of components prescribed by the recursive scheme to build this fractal structure.
Functional Analysis.comment: The revision addresses an error in the proof of Lemma 3.2 which resulted from an invalid step in the calculations. The settings in the revision had to be changed to the effect that the assignments in (2.7) give rise to two symmetries instead of only one: An extension of the assignments to a linear antiautomorphic involution had to be included in the line of reasoning

Functional Analysis.title: Safety-constrained position tracking of a flexible transmission system
Functional Analysis.summary: We consider safety-constrained position tracking for a flexible transmission system consisting of a torsional shaft driven by a motor and connected to a gravitationally loaded inertia. The coupled PDE-ODE dynamics admit a semilinear formulation in which the linear input-output system is impedance passive and the gravitational torque enters as a bounded, globally Lipschitz perturbation. We establish an energy dissipation inequality for the nonlinear model and show that a position-funnel controller with supervised damping admits a unique global closed-loop trajectory. In particular, the motor-angle tracking error remains strictly inside a prescribed time-varying funnel, which can be chosen to enforce safety bounds on the motor angle.

Functional Analysis.title: On isoperimetric local-Bollobás-Thomason inequalities
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove the following isoperimetric-type inequality: for every convex body $K$ in $\mathbb R^n$ and some $σ\subset[n]:=\{1,\dots,n\}$ there exists a suitable Hanner polytope $B_K$ with the same volume as $K$ and such that the volume of each of its orthogonal projections onto every subspace whose basis is formed by the canonical vectors $\{e_i:i\inτ\cup([n]\setminusσ)\}$, for every $τ\subseteqσ$, bounds from below the volume of the corresponding projections of $K$.

Functional Analysis.title: Mixed Bourgain-Morrey spaces and their applications to boundedness of operators
Functional Analysis.summary: We introduce the mixed Bourgain-Morrey spaces and obtain their preduals. The boundedness of Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator, iterated maximal operator, fractional integral operator, singular integral operator on these spaces is proved. In addition, we give a description of the dual of mixed Bourgain-Morrey spaces and conclude the reflexivity of these spaces.
Functional Analysis.comment: We have divided our article `On the mixed Bourgain-Morrey spaces' (arXiv:2511.08118) into two parts; this is the first part

Functional Analysis.title: Dual medial axes in finite-dimensional normed spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We study medial axes of nonempty closed sets in finite-dimensional real normed spaces whose norms are $C^1$ away from the origin. Using the differential of the norm, we define the dual $k$-medial axis by requiring the contact covectors associated with nearest points to have affine dimension at least $k-1$. In dimension $n$, we prove that this set is $(n-k+1)$-rectifiable for every $1\le k\le n+1$, and hence has Hausdorff dimension at most $n-k+1$. We give a direct geometric proof and characterize the dual medial axes through the superdifferential of the squared distance function, obtaining an alternative proof from a theorem of Alberti, Ambrosio, and Cannarsa on singularities of semiconvex functions. Under the additional assumption of strict convexity, the ordinary and dual medial axes coincide for $k=2,3$, yielding the corresponding rectifiability results for ordinary medial axes. For $k=4$, however, the ordinary rectifiability conclusion can fail even for norms arbitrarily close to Euclidean: we construct norms on $\mathbb R^3$ with smooth positively curved unit spheres arbitrarily $C^\infty$-close to the Euclidean sphere, together with four-point sets whose ordinary $4$-medial axes contain nondegenerate line segments.

Functional Analysis.title: Functional Analysis
Functional Analysis.summary: In this second edition, I have taken the opportunity to improve the presentation in several places, to test and revise the problem sets, and to add some new material.

Functional Analysis.title: Radial Schur multipliers on trees and quantitative Fourier--Schur separation
Functional Analysis.summary: We study ordinary and completely bounded norms of radial Schur multipliers on trees. On the homogeneous tree of countably infinite degree, we show that boundedness implies complete boundedness. The argument realizes arbitrary matrix amplifications of a shifted Toeplitz symbol inside rectangular corners of the original multiplier. It also applies to some locally finite trees of unbounded degree. Consequently, the completely bounded radial multiplier theorem of González-Pérez, Parcet, Pérez García and Wang has no general counterpart with ordinary norms. We also determine the optimal order of the comparison constant for positive definite even symbols. For each $1 < p < \infty$ with $p \neq 2$, we construct radial symbols on finitely generated nonabelian free groups, supported in the ball of radius $N$, whose completely bounded Herz--Schur norms remain bounded as $N \to \infty$, whereas their ordinary Fourier multiplier norms grow at least like $N^{|1-\frac{2}{p}|}$. For each fixed $0 < \vartheta < π$, we also determine the exact order $t^{-|1-\frac{2}{p}|}$ of both the ordinary and completely bounded Fourier multiplier norms of the damped radial phases $s \mapsto \mathrm{e}^{(-t+\mathrm{i}\vartheta)|s|}$ as $t \to 0$. Finally, we compute the local amenability modulus of free balls, we bound the Fourier--Schur ratio of free balls from above and below in terms of this modulus, and we show that its restriction to radial symbols grows polynomially in the radius.

Functional Analysis.title: When are metrizable linear subspaces of topological vector spaces finite-dimensional?
Functional Analysis.summary: We study conditions that imply finite-dimensionality of metrizable or Frechet-Urysohn linear subspaces of topological vector spaces (TVS). We consider the classes $\mathscr{D}_M$ and $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$ of TVS: a space $L$ belongs to $\mathscr{D}_M$ (respectively, $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$) if every metrizable (respectively, Frechet-Urysohn) linear subspace of $L$ is finite-dimensional. Although the classes of metrizable spaces and of Frechet-Urysohn spaces differ substantially, the classes $\mathscr{D}_M$ and $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$ are much closer to each other: in the Hrusak-Ramos-Garcia model, in which Malykhin's problem is solved, $\mathscr{D}_M=\mathscr{D}_{FU}$, whereas under MA+not CH, as shown in the paper, $\mathscr{D}_M\neq\mathscr{D}_{FU}$. For a locally convex space (LCS) $L$ we denote by $L_w$ the space $L$ with its weak topology and by $L'_{w^*}$ the dual space with the weak$^*$ topology. This paper investigates which LCS $L$ have the property that $L_w$ and $L'_{w^*}$ belong to $\mathscr{D}_M$ or $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$. Although the classes are close, different methods are used to study them: topological-algebraic ones for $\mathscr{D}_M$ (a criterion is obtained) and methods of measure theory and probability for $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$ (a sufficient condition is obtained). We prove that if an LCS $L$ admits a continuous norm, then $L_w\in\mathscr{D}_{FU}$; in particular, if $L$ admits a continuous norm and $L_w$ is Frechet-Urysohn, then $L$ is finite-dimensional. If the topology of an LCS $L$ is coarser than the topology induced by some complete norm on $L$ (for example, if $L$ is Banach), then $L'_{w^*}\in\mathscr{D}_{FU}$; completeness of the norm is essential here. The methods also apply to spaces of real-analytic functions and to the space of polynomials with the topology of pointwise convergence: these also belong to $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$.

Functional Analysis.title: Schatten limits for semi-commutators in Toeplitz quantization on Fock space
Functional Analysis.summary: We solve a problem posed by Hu and Virtanen by characterizing, for every $0<p<\infty$, the bounded symbols $f$ for which $T_f^{(t)}T_g^{(t)}-T_{fg}^{(t)}$ tends to zero in the unnormalized Schatten $p$-norm or quasi-norm as $t\to0^+$ for every fixed bounded $g$. The setting is weighted Fock spaces over $\mathbb C^n$ with weights whose real Hessians are uniformly positive and bounded. Only constants satisfy the limit when $p<2n$; at $p=2n$, it is equivalent to the weak real gradient belonging to $L^{2n}(\mathbb R^{2n})$. When $p>2n$, the limit is characterized by relative weak compactness in $L^1(\mathbb R^{2n})$ of normalized local mean oscillation densities. For $p\ge2$, uniform convergence over $\|g\|_\infty\le1$ is equivalent to vanishing density mass. A continuous compactly supported counterexample for $p>2n$ shows that bounded density mass and convergence for $g=\bar f$ do not imply convergence for every fixed bounded $g$. The symbol classes are weight-independent unital algebras, yielding limits for finite Toeplitz products and commutators; quantitative Hölder estimates also give finite-rank approximation bounds. The Gaussian case transfers to anti-Wick quantization by unitary equivalence. On compact Kähler manifolds with positive line bundles, we prove a Hölder sufficient condition, including the endpoint, for each fixed bounded second symbol. A projective-line example shows that trace norm convergence can fail for a smooth first symbol and a fixed bounded second symbol. The proofs combine local holomorphic approximation, Schatten and Sobolev estimates, singular integral methods, and the Dunford--Pettis criterion.

Functional Analysis.title: Unbounded Helson Forms with a Moment Representation
Functional Analysis.summary: We study the positive Helson form $h_0[a,b]=\sum_{m,n\ge1}α(mn)a_n\overline{b_m}$ on the finitely supported sequences $c_{00}\subset\ell^2(\mathbb{N})$, where $α(n)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}n^{-s}dμ(s)<\infty$ for a finite positive Borel measure $μ$. Under the Carleman condition $\sum_{k\ge1}α(4^k)^{-1/(2k)}=\infty$, closability of $h_0$ is equivalent to $\sqrt{n}α(n)\to0$, and hence to $μ((-\infty,1/2])=0$. For measures concentrated on $(1/2,\infty)$, we identify the closure of the operator $N_0a=\sum_{n\ge1}a_nn^{-s}$, defined on $c_{00}$, with its maximal realization from $\ell^2(\mathbb{N})$ to $L^2(μ)$. We further prove that the sequences $a\in c_{00}$ satisfying $\sum_{n\ge1}a_n/\sqrt{n}=0$ form an operator core for the positive self-adjoint operator associated with the closure of $h_0$.

Functional Analysis.title: On the Geometry of Wasserstein Barycenter II: Riemannian Rigidity, Essential Non-Branching, and Finsler Models
Functional Analysis.summary:
Wasserstein barycenters provide a notion of weighted mean for probability measures on a metric space. We prove that the barycenter curvature-dimension condition ${\rm BCD}(K,N)$ is equivalent to ${\rm RCD}(K,N)$ for $K\in \mathbb R$ and $1<N<\infty$. This gives a new characterization of Riemannian curvature-dimension spaces by entropy inequalities at barycenters of finite families of measures.
  As a byproduct, we introduce an almost ${\rm BCD}$ condition that allows an additive error in the entropy inequality. It is stable under measured Gromov-Hausdorff convergence and implies essential non-branching when the error is sufficiently small. The resulting class contains non-Riemannian Finsler spaces. Within the ${\rm BCD}$ framework, this answers an open problem posed by Ambrosio in his 2018 ICM survey. We further bound the failure of the parallelogram identity for cotangent norms in terms of the entropy error.
Functional Analysis.comment: This is the continuation of our paper <On the Geometry of Wasserstein Barycenter I>

Functional Analysis.title: Weighted Power Means on Upper Triangular Matrix Groups
Functional Analysis.summary:
We study weighted power means on the Lie group $\operatorname{UT}_n$ of real upper triangular matrices with positive diagonal entries. For $t\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, the weighted power mean $P_t(\mathbf{w}; A_1,\ldots,A_m)$ is defined by \[
  X=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i(X\#_tA_i),
  \qquad
  X\#_tA:=X(X^{-1}A)^t.
  \] Using divided differences, analytic matrix functions, and the Parlett recurrence, we prove existence, uniqueness, and real-analytic dependence of $P_t$ on the data and the weights. We derive finite entrywise and block-recursive algorithms, establish structural properties of the mean, and obtain explicit formulas for the cases $\operatorname{UT}_2$ and $\operatorname{UT}_3$. We prove that $P_t$ converges to the weighted Karcher mean as $t\to 0$. We also establish a Lie--Trotter formula and derive second-order asymptotic expansions for the power, Karcher, and log-Euclidean means, showing that the parameter $t$ first enters the local behavior at second order.

Functional Analysis.title: Computable presentations of separable Lebesgue spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: For every right-c.e.\ real $p\in(1,2)$, $L^p[0,1]$ has a computable presentation. The proof combines an effective stability modulus for almost isometric embeddings with a Fraïssé-style construction in which the exponent varies. In the same range, if $\ell^p$ has a computable presentation, then $p$ is computable. Combining these with the known results gives the computable presentability classification for all separable Lebesgue spaces. We also formulate an effective Fraïssé theorem for Banach spaces and apply it to obtain a computable presentation of the Gurarij Banach space.

Functional Analysis.title: Very tight embeddings of subspaces of \(L_p\) for \(0<p<1\)
Functional Analysis.summary: For \(0<p<1\) and \(μ>1\), every \(d\)-dimensional subspace of \(L_p\) embeds linearly into \(\ell_p^{\lfloorμd\rfloor}\) with distortion at most \(C(p,μ)(\log(d+2))^{1/p}\). If its Rademacher type \(q\) constant is at most \(T\), where \(p<q\leq2\), the distortion is at most \(C(p,q,μ)T\), independently of \(d\). We also give explicit bounds as \(μ\downarrow1\). This answers the question of Johnson and Schechtman concerning the extension of their very tight embedding theorem below exponent one. The proof combines compression at a lower exponent with a change of density that preserves the number of coordinates, and applies over both scalar fields.

Functional Analysis.title: Perturbed Exponential Systems, Pattern-Dependent Shifted-Sinc Operators, and Matrix Symbols on Finite Unions of Intervals
Functional Analysis.summary:
We study perturbed exponential systems and unions of shifted frequency lattices through shifted-sinc operators and finite-dimensional fiberizations. For the auxiliary binary local-shift model, we identify the exact pattern-dependent invariant $$ ρ_{δ,s}=\|P_-T_{2δ}P_+\|, $$ which gives the optimal squared synthesis bounds $1\pmρ_{δ,s}$. For periodic patterns, the synthesis operator reduces exactly to a single constant Vandermonde-type matrix, yielding finite-dimensional basis criteria and optimal bounds. We further prove that the worst binary lower bound is the infimum of its periodic counterparts; at the critical value $δ=1/4$, a step pattern is governed by a half-shifted Hilbert matrix and has vanishing lower bound, although every fixed periodic pattern remains invertible.
  We also combine exact bounds for structured patterns with a support-independent perturbation estimate, obtaining explicit stability neighborhoods. For finite unions of bounded intervals and finitely many shifted lattices, folding modulo one yields finitely many rectangular phase matrices whose singular values and ranks give the exact bounds and complete Riesz-sequence, frame, and Riesz-basis criteria. This framework also yields finite Hadamard constraints for periodic spectra and an exact reduction of rationally commensurate multirate sampling.

Functional Analysis.title: Effective Multiplicative Ergodic Theorems for Banach Space Cocycles
Functional Analysis.summary: The multiplicative ergodic theorem (MET) describes the asymptotic growth rates of $q$-volumes under the iterates of an operator cocycle, i.e., compositions of operators driven by a stationary process, organizing the underlying space into equivariant filtrations or splittings into so called Oseledets subspaces. For operator cocycles in finite dimensions, and more generally in Hilbert spaces, one can control the geometry of the Oseledets subspaces given by the MET via the convergence rates of finite-time volume growth data. This makes the MET "effective" for matrix and Hilbert-space operator cocycles. We extend this effective theory to cocycles of Banach-space operators, obtaining quantitative angle estimates that are new even in the finite-dimensional setting. We take a sequential approach à la Raghunathan and Ruelle, allowing us to separate the geometric argument of the MET from measure-theoretic considerations. This permits weaker cocycle measurability hypotheses for the non-invertible and semi-invertible METs on a broad class of Banach spaces, including nonseparable ones. As an application, we establish the MET for transfer operator cocycles on $\operatorname{BV}[0,1]$ associated with jointly measurable random Lasota-Yorke maps.

Functional Analysis.title: Hilbert transforms on graph products of finite von Neumann algebras
Functional Analysis.summary: We study Hilbert transforms on graph products of finite von Neumann algebras, with particular interest in their boundedness on the associated noncommutative $L_p$-spaces for $1<p<\infty$. We establish a generalized Cotlar identity for Hilbert transforms, valid on operators whose lengths exceed a constant depending only on the underlying graph. We further prove that graph products of finite von Neumann algebras satisfying a Haagerup-type inequality admit $L_p$-bounded Hilbert transforms, therefore extending the corresponding result of Mei and Ricard for free products of finite von Neumann algebras. In addition, we obtain several equivalent characterizations of this Haagerup-type inequality. Our results apply, in particular, to graph products of finite groups, right-angled Hecke von Neumann algebras, and graph products of finite quantum groups. As an application, we provide a complete characterization of a compactness problem posed by Ozawa for graph products of finite groups and right-angled Hecke von Neumann algebras.

Functional Analysis.title: Positive Planar Measures for Spectral Pinching and the Corrected BMV Conjecture
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove the corrected Bessis--Moussa--Villani pinching conjecture for all symmetrized word averages. For Hermitian matrices $A,B$ and $D=E_A(B)$, we construct a positive compactly supported measure $ζ_{A,B}$ on $\mathbb R^2$ such that \[ \Tr f(xA+yB)-\Tr f(xA+yD) =y^2\int_{\mathbb R^2}f''(xa+yb)\,dζ_{A,B}(a,b). \] Its total mass is $\frac12\|B-D\|_2^2$. This representation proves the corrected conjecture, including its equality cases, and gives a positive bivariate moment representation for the coefficient differences. We also derive complete monotonicity of normalized exponential pinching defects and a comparison with Lie--Trotter approximations. A one-dimensional second-order loss measure is obtained for trace-preserving conditional expectations on finite tracial von Neumann algebras. Finally, we relate $ζ_{A,B}$ to Heinävaara's tracial joint spectral measure by an explicit positive radial transform.

Functional Analysis.title: Monotonicity properties of Hadamard weighted geometric means of bounded sets of positive kernel operators
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove new monotonicity properties for joint and generalized spectral radius and their essential versions, operator norm, Hausdorff measure of non-compactness and numerical radius of products and sums of Hadamard weighted geometric means of positive kernel operators on appropriate Banach function spaces. Our results extend recent results on weighted geometric symmetrizations of bounded sets of such operators defined on $L^2$. To our knowledge, several proved properties in this generality are new even in the finite dimensional case and also in the case of singelton sets.
Functional Analysis.comment: This preprint is the replacement of the arxiv preprints of the articles [9] and [10] (cited in the preprint). arXiv admin note: substantial text overlap with arXiv:2202.02325, arXiv:2402.04265, arXiv:1805.09680, arXiv:2107.09459, arXiv:1612.01765

Analysis of PDEs.title: Variational principles and aplications to symmetric PDEs
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we explore various equivalences of Ekeland's variational principle within the framework of group-invariant mappings. We introduce and analyze several key theorems, including the Drop theorem, the Petal theorem, Caristi-Kirk fxed-point theorem, and Takahashi's theorem, all of them within this context. Moreover, we extend the classical Drop theorem and Petal theorem to a more generalized setting. We also demonstrate the practical signifcance of these findings through numerous applications to diverse areas of mathematics. In particular, in the context of partial differential equations, we explore their implications on the solution of the Plateau problem, and in control theory. We also extend the classical Pontyargin maximum principle.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Modified scattering for the 3D Hartree equation with singular external potentials
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish modified scattering for the three-dimensional Hartree equation with Coulomb interaction and singular external potentials, including repulsive Coulomb and inverse-square potentials. In the defocusing case, the result holds for arbitrary initial data in $H^{0,1}(\mathbb R^3)\cap H^{1,0}(\mathbb R^3)$. In particular, we obtain large-data modified scattering for the flat defocusing Hartree equation. For the focusing problem with repulsive Coulomb potential $V(x)=κ|x|^{-1}$, we prove radial modified scattering under the sharp mass condition $|λ|\|u_0\|_2^2\leq 2κ$, including the endpoint, and construct standing waves at every larger mass. Our argument obtains strong $L^2$ convergence from rescaled energy and comparison with a frozen-field evolution.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A direct proof of the equivalence of the A2 and the Helson--Szego conditions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We give a direct proof of the equivalence between the Muckenhoupt $\mathcal{A}_2$ and the Helson--Szegő conditions on the unit circle $T$. A positive weight $w$ belongs to $\mathcal{A}_2(T)$ if and only if $\log w=u+Hv$, where $u,v$ are real bounded functions, $\|v\|_\infty<\fracπ{2}$, and $H$ denotes the periodic Hilbert transform. The classical proof combines the Helson--Szegő theorem with the Hunt--Muckenhoupt--Wheeden characterization of weighted boundedness of the Hilbert transform. Our proof derives the Helson--Szegő representation directly from the Muckenhoupt $\mathcal{A}_2$ condition, without using boundedness of $H$ on $L^2(w)$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Hot Spots: From Smooth to Nonsmooth Simply Connected Planar Domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Assuming the absence of interior local extrema for first positive Neumann eigenfunctions on bounded smooth simply connected planar domains, as reported in \cite{SmoothInput}, we extend the hot spots conclusion to simply connected domains of finite area with compact Sobolev embedding and simple first positive Neumann eigenvalue. The supremum and infimum are approached in arbitrarily thin boundary layers. For bounded domains and eigenfunctions continuous up to the boundary, both extrema are attained on the boundary. We also transfer polynomial Neumann heat-kernel bounds uniformly along a conformal exhaustion and construct explicit bounded and unbounded examples, including domains with cusps and a domain with infinitely many corners and bottlenecks. Some of these examples admit no polynomial Neumann heat-kernel bound.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Stationary bistable fronts on a periodic necklace graph: existence, stability and multiplicity
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study stationary fronts for a bistable reaction-diffusion equation with the McKean reaction on a periodic necklace metric graph. For profiles that agree on each pair of parallel edges, the problem reduces to a scalar equation on the real line with a periodic, piecewise constant diffusion coefficient. The diffusion contrast of the necklace is not small, so the coefficient cannot be treated as a small perturbation of a constant. Because the McKean reaction is piecewise linear, the equation is affine between threshold crossings and coefficient interfaces, and a front is determined explicitly by its crossing points. We find an explicit interval of reaction thresholds, the pinning interval, such that stationary fronts, monotone or not, exist exactly for thresholds in this interval. Up to translations by the spatial period, there are exactly two decreasing fronts at each interior threshold and one front at each endpoint. For each fixed interior threshold, one decreasing front is Lyapunov stable and the other is unstable in the $W^{1,\infty}(\mathbb{R})$ norm, among mild solutions with one continuously moving threshold crossing. The crossing phases of the two decreasing fronts also determine nonmonotone fronts. For each interior threshold and odd $m\geq3$, choose $m$ periods of the coefficient that are sufficiently far apart. There are then exactly $2^m$ fronts with one threshold crossing in each chosen period and none elsewhere. Varying the chosen periods gives infinitely many inequivalent fronts with $m$ crossings.

Analysis of PDEs.title: From entropy waves to vortex sheets for the Euler equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct piecewise smooth solutions of the full compressible Euler equations that evolve from entropy waves into vortex sheets while retaining a strictly positive Taylor jump. For every integer $κ\geq1$, we obtain solutions satisfying initial material compatibility for pressure and velocity through order $κ$, whose tangential velocity jump has a nonzero leading term of order $t^{κ+1}$. These solutions are periodic in the tangential variables and admit a smooth realization in a slab with impermeable walls. We also construct solutions on a local nonperiodic tangential patch that satisfy initial material compatibility at every order, yet have a tangential velocity jump that is nonzero for every sufficiently small positive time and flat at $t=0$. The finite-order construction uses a normal Cauchy-Kowalevski problem for velocity potentials, whereas the all-order construction uses a homogeneous reduction to a smooth hyperbolic Cauchy problem.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Minimizers for the Cahn-Hilliard energy functional with the Flory-Huggins potential under strong anchoring conditions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we theoretically and numerically study the minimizers for the Cahn-Hilliard energy with the Flory-Huggins potential under the strong anchoring condition, i.e., the Dirichlet boundary condition. We reveal bifurcation phenomena mediated by the boundary condition, the transition layer thickness, and the temperature of the system. Numerical simulations are also presented to approximate the minimizers of this energy by solving a gradient-flow equation, namely the Allen-Cahn equation constrained with strong anchoring conditions and random initial data. The effects of varying the transition layer thickness and temperature are presented to confirm the theoretical analysis.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Li-Yau and Aronson-Bénilan approach for the Keller-Segel system with critical exponent
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
The Li-Yau and Aronson-Bénilan estimates are fundamental differential inequalities for heat and porous-medium equations, yielding differential Harnack inequalities and sharp smoothing and decay rates. We develop analogues for the critical parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel system on $\mathbb{R}^d$, where diffusion and aggregation act at the same scale. Our main tool is the effective pressure $v=p-u$, with $p=\logρ$ in $d=2$ and $p=\frac{m}{m-1}ρ^{m-1}$ for $d>2$, $m=2-\frac{2}{d}$. We prove quantitative lower bounds on $Δv$, showing that classical pressure estimates subsist in a suitable form despite the nonlocal interaction.
  These estimates unify previous results and yield new regularity. For nonnegative finite-measure initial data of sufficiently small mass, assuming only a logarithmic moment in $d=2$, we construct global solutions smooth for positive times and satisfying $\|ρ_t\|_{L^\infty}\le C/t$. For finite-free-energy data, we obtain global $L^\infty$ bounds of order $1+t^{-1}$ in the subcritical and critical mass regimes.
  We also introduce a new characterization of the critical mass as the minimal mass $M_c^{\mathrm{sub}}(d)$ of subsolutions of the elliptic Lane-Emden equation (Liouville in $d=2$). We prove that it equals $8π$ in dimension $2$ and, for $d\ge3$, coincides with the Keller-Segel critical mass given by the HLS inequality, by reducing the problem to a one-dimensional optimal-control problem.
  Along the way we prove tools of independent interest: $L^\infty$ estimates from lower bounds on $Δv$, critical log-HLS/HLS estimates away from Dirac masses, Hessian bounds for Newtonian potentials, and Lipschitz and Hessian estimates for bounded porous-medium solutions with drifts on the whole space.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Hardy inequalities on the positive integer lattice: a dimensional transition
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We determine exactly in which dimensions the sharp Hardy coefficient on the positive integer lattice agrees with that on the positive Euclidean cone, with Dirichlet conditions on every coordinate face. Equality holds in dimensions one and two, whereas the discrete coefficient is strictly smaller in every dimension at least three. An exact transformation identifies the lattice problem with a weighted Dirichlet problem on a cube. A tangential integration identity evaluates the defect of an explicit critical profile and proves the dimensional transition. The continuous coefficient remains the lower edge of the essential spectrum of the transformed operator; below that edge, the sharp discrete coefficient is a simple eigenvalue with a positive eigenfunction. In dimension three, an explicit supersolution places the coefficient strictly between twelve and forty-nine quarters. A representation on a product of three-dimensional spheres relates the spectral threshold to the local geometry of the transformed problem.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Self-similar solutions for the gSQG patch equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The inviscid generalized surface quasi-geostrophic (gSQG) equations are a family of active scalar equations parametrized by a scalar $α$ that includes the two-dimensional Euler equations ($α= 0)$ and the SQG equation $(α= 1)$. We prove that, for every $α\in (\frac{7}{4}, 2)$ and every $T > 0$, there exists a self-similar patch solution whose boundary is a smooth, unbounded graph for $0 \leq t < T$ and develops a corner singularity at time $T$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Two-Dimensional Narrow Escape Problem with Deterministic Initial Condition: Mean Escape Time and Escape location probabilities
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper presents a rigorous asymptotic analysis of the two-dimensional narrow escape problem for a Brownian particle initiated at a deterministic position x. While we address the mean escape time, the main novelty lies in our derivation of the asymptotic escape distribution. We derive explicit asymptotic formulas that characterize the dependence of the escape behavior on the relative configuration of the starting point and the window centers. These results remain valid as the starting position approaches the boundary windows and include refined error estimates. The formulas are obtained with two independent methods, each of them having their own interest. A central feature of this work is the rigorous treatment of the underlying mixed boundary value problems in the absence of a contact angle at the escape window boundaries. By leveraging recent results on the maximal regularity of the gradient of the solutions of such mixed boundary value problems, we ensure the analytical validity of our approach despite the inherent loss of regularity of these solutions at the escape window boundaries. Finally, we apply these general results to provide a full sharp asymptotic equivalents for regimes where window sizes scale at specific relative rates.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Homogenization of the Stokes equations in a domain perforated by a thin truss
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the homogenization problem of the stationary Stokes equations in a periodically perforated domain whose solid structure consists of a thin truss. That is, the width $a_ε$ of the truss tends to zero faster than the period size $ε$. We identify the different scaling regimes and derive the corresponding effective equations. In the critical regime, we obtain the Brinkman equations, while in the subcritical regime, we recover the unchanged Stokes equations. In a subrange of the supercritical regime, we derive Darcy's law as the effective equation. Furthermore, we explicitly compute the effective coefficients in the Darcy and Brinkman limits. Moreover, as a tool in the analysis, we establish the analogous homogenization result for a periodic forest of cylinders. Finally, we also consider the homogenization result for a fence of cylinders.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 66 pages, 12 figures, Keywords: Homogenization, connected structures, Stokes-Brinkman-Darcy limits

Analysis of PDEs.title: Homogenization of the Stokes equations with slender bodies
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper we study the convergence of solutions of the Stokes equations in a domain perforated by slender bodies placed on a fixed periodic grid of size $2ε$ as the size of the bodies goes to zero and the number of bodies goes to infinity. We assume that the width $b_ε$ of the bodies vanishes faster than the length $a_ε$ of the particles. We identify the critical scaling regimes for $a_ε$ and $b_ε$ and prove that in this case the system is effectively described by the Brinkman equations.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Corner Regularity and Asymptotics for the Two-Dimensional Radiation Transport Equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The regularity of solutions to the two-dimensional radiation transport equation plays a central role in understanding the behavior of scalar flux near geometric corners. In a previous study of Kaper's corner singularity problem, the physical transport kernel was decomposed into its principal inverse-distance singularity and a lower-order remainder, reducing the corner asymptotic analysis to the question of whether the scalar flux possesses sufficient continuity to justify differentiation of the associated singular potential. The required regularity, however, remained unresolved. In this paper, we establish a sharp modulus-of-continuity estimate for the scalar flux generated by the physical transport kernel and prove the estimate $ω_φ(h)=O\!\left(h\log(D/h)\right)$, which implies Dini continuity. This estimate yields absolute convergence of the fluctuation term arising in the differentiated principal potential and permits a rigorous differentiation formula for transport solutions. Using this regularity framework, we derive the fixed-angle asymptotic behavior of the scalar flux and its first derivatives near a rectangular corner. For every fixed interior ray, the gradient exhibits logarithmic growth, while the scalar flux admits an $r\log(1/r)$ correction with an explicitly identified coefficient determined by the corner values of the flux and source. The analysis shows that a rectangular corner does not generate a singularity stronger than the logarithmic first-derivative singularity already present in smooth-boundary transport theory. Numerical calculations on benchmark problems are consistent with the theoretical predictions. These results provide a rigorous resolution of the regularity issue underlying Kaper's corner singularity problem and establish a mathematical framework for corner asymptotics in two-dimensional radiation transport.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Finitely many solutions for the prescribed scalar curvature problem at the critical flatness order
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study the following prescribed scalar curvature problem $$
  -Δu=K(y)u^{2^*-1},\ \ u>0
  \,\ \ \text{in}\ \ \mathbb{R}^N, \tag*{$(*)$} $$ where $2^*=\frac{2N}{N-2}$. For $N\geq4$, we construct a positive $K(y)$ with maximum set $\{|y|=1\}$ and critical order of flatness $m=N-2$ at $|y|=1$, such that problem $(*)$ admits only finitely many positive solutions in $D^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^N)$. To this end, we prove compactness of the solution set of $(*)$ by blow-up analysis and then apply Sard's theorem to choose $K$ for which each solution is nondegenerate and hence isolated, so that the solution set of $(*)$ is finite. Our results give a negative answer to Wei--Yan's conjecture in [J. Wei and S. Yan, JFA, 2010].

Analysis of PDEs.title: Chemotaxis models with signal-dependent sensitivity and a logistic-type source, III: Bifurcation and spike-like solutions
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
This third paper in a series on a parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis model studies bifurcation of positive constant equilibria in one space dimension. We consider $$ \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} u_t=Δu-χ_0\nabla\cdot\left(\frac{u^m}{(1+v)^β}\nabla v\right)+au-bu^{1+α}, & x\inΩ,\\ 0=Δv-μv+νu^γ, & x\inΩ,\\ \frac{\partial u}{\partial n}=\frac{\partial v}{\partial n}=0, & x\in\partialΩ, \end{array} \right. $$ where $Ω$ is a bounded interval, $α,γ,m,μ,ν>0$, $χ_0\in\mathbb R$, and $a,b,β\ge0$. Building on earlier results on global existence, boundedness, persistence, and stabilization, we take $χ_0$ as the bifurcation parameter and examine the effects of $β$ and the domain size on the bifurcation.
  Center manifold reduction yields a coefficient $β_{n_0}$ at a simple bifurcation mode $n_0$ of a positive constant equilibrium. The pitchfork bifurcation is supercritical if $β_{n_0}>0$ and subcritical if $β_{n_0}<0$. Stronger desensitization raises the sensitivity required for loss of linear stability. Bifurcation may be supercritical for small $β$ but is always subcritical for sufficiently large $β$. Thus, desensitization makes patterns harder to trigger and favors abrupt rather than continuous emergence. The bifurcation mode increases with domain size, allowing more complex spatial patterns.
  Under suitable conditions, we prove unbounded continuation of local bifurcation branches. We also show that large-sensitivity stationary sequences satisfying a peak-gap hypothesis develop spike-like profiles. Numerical continuation and time-evolution experiments illustrate the bifurcating branches and spike-like solutions and suggest unbounded continuation and increasingly sharp stationary profiles.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharpness transitions for weighted Triebel--Lizorkin Hardy inequalities with p < q
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For fractional difference energies with two power weights and distinct inner and outer exponents, we determine regimes in which the constant generated by the homogeneous power is optimal and regimes in which it loses optimality. In the range $1<p<q$, we prove sharp Hardy inequalities on nontrivial weight intervals for every sign of $D=d+2β-sp$, including a two-sided interval in the balanced case $D=0$. For $q\ge2$, these intervals extend strictly beyond an elementary pointwise scalar criterion. For $1<p<q<2$, we determine the optimal power exponent in the scalar supporting-line inequality and obtain a larger explicit sharpness interval. The proof pairs opposite logarithmic displacements and controls the nonlinear deficit by a quadratic reference energy of the transformed function. Its translation estimate allows a positive contribution at bounded scales to absorb negative contributions at remote scales. Concentrating tests prove strict loss of homogeneous sharpness near both finite-energy endpoints, and angular variations give concrete bounds for the first sharpness threshold. We extend the method to flat singular sets and regional half-space energies, retaining the distinction between ambient finite-energy conditions and finiteness of the homogeneous candidate. We also treat the complementary order $p>q$, including flat-subspace inequalities and a complete alternative proof for point singularities. All sharpness sequences belong to the specified smooth test classes, and every positive optimal constant extends to their completion in the difference norm.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Symmetry Breaking and Moduli for Ancient Yamabe Flows on the Sphere
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For every $n\ge3$, we construct compact Type II ancient Yamabe flows in the round conformal class of the unit $n$-sphere $\Ss^n$. After stereographic projection and rescaling of time and conformal factor, the solutions are asymptotic backward in time to finite superpositions of Aubin--Talenti bubbles with mutually comparable scales. For integers $h\ge1$ and $k\ge2$, the limiting centers form $h$ coaxial regular $k$-gons; when $h\ge2$, their distinct layer heights may be prescribed arbitrarily in the interval $(-1,1)$. If $hk\ge3$, the resulting flows are not geometrically equivalent to any rotationally symmetric ancient flow. For each flow, there is a fixed point of $\Ss^n$ at which the Ricci tensor has both positive and negative eigenvalues on every time slice. The corresponding volume-normalized Yamabe flows are also ancient. After rescaling each time slice to a fixed volume, the metrics converge to a wedge of $hk$ isometric round $n$-spheres in the Gromov--Hausdorff topology, as time tends to $-\infty$. For fixed $h,k\ge2$, the concentration configurations admit an explicit $(h-1)$-parameter description up to Möbius transformations. Consequently, the construction yields geometrically inequivalent flows indexed by a nonempty open subset of $\R^{h-1}$, all with the same fixed-volume backward Gromov--Hausdorff limit. The proof uses inner--outer gluing for the quasilinear parabolic equation in $n$-dimensional space that exhibits Kelvin symmetry. Weighted Euclidean and spherical Hölder estimates control the nonlinear terms and, together with parabolic regularity, yield smooth extension of the conformal metrics across the north pole of $\Ss^n$.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: v2: Title and exposition revised; proofs clarified, with a more detailed treatment of the backward geometric limits and the classification of concentration configurations up to Möbius transformations

Analysis of PDEs.title: Nonexistence results for the semilinear wave equation on graphs
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate the semilinear wave equation with potential on weighted graphs. We establish sufficient conditions for the nonexistence of global-in-time solutions. Both nonnegative and sign-changing solutions are considered. In particular, the proof for sign-changing solutions relies on a novel technique for this type of result.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Inverse problems and continuity of heat content coefficients
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the small-time asymptotic expansions for the Dirichlet and Open heat contents of convex planar domains. We prove that the small-time asymptotic expansion for the Open heat content can determine a triangle among triangles, a parallelogram among parallelograms, and an acute trapezium among acute trapezia of the same height. In addition, for a sequence of convex polygons converging to a convex set with smooth boundary in the sense of Hausdorff, we show that the coefficients of order $t$ in the small-time asymptotic expansions of the Dirichlet and the Open heat contents converge to those of the limiting set. While, for a sequence of convex sets with smooth boundary converging to a convex polygon in the sense of Hausdorff, we show that the coefficients of order $t$ do not converge to that of the limiting polygon.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The effect of the permeability in interface problems: impermeable barriers and free diffusion
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Focusing on reaction-diffusion models with an interface region dividing the domain, we study the stability of systems as the permeability parameter approaches zero or infinity under Kedem-Katchalsky boundary conditions imposed on the membrane or interface region. These boundary conditions establish that the flux across the interface manifold is proportional to the density jump across that region, with the constant of proportionality defined as the permeability parameter. We analyze both limiting behaviors: when permeability vanishes and when infinite flux is permitted. This analysis is carried out for both the well-known symmetric case, where permeability is identical in both directions across the membrane, and the asymmetric case, where it depends on the direction of the flux. For the asymmetric case, we obtain novel and surprising results that reveal a richer variety of behaviors in this class of interface problems and that differ from the scalar models.

Analysis of PDEs.title: From kinetic activation dynamics to Holling type reaction-diffusion predator-prey systems
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider a kinetic model of predator-prey dynamics in which predation is characterized by a sequence of behavioral transitions. Prey and predators are described by distribution functions in phase space, with the predator population further structured into internal states corresponding to inactive, active, and saturated individuals. We show that different macroscopic functional responses emerge from distinct mechanisms governing predator activation. More precisely, activation driven uniquely by pairwise encounters leads to a saturating Holling type II response, whereas activation additionally modulated by local prey density produces a generalized sigmoidal Holling type III response. This is achieved by means of a diffusive scaling and a formal hydrodynamic limit, from which we derive a closed reaction-diffusion system of Rosenzweig-MacArthur type for the prey and total predator spatial densities.

Analysis of PDEs.title: New time-periodic solutions to the cubic conformal wave equation on $\mathbb{S}^{3}$: I Spherical symmetry
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We present a rigorous construction of novel time-periodic solutions to the radially symmetric cubic conformal wave equation on the Einstein cylinder $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{S}^{3}$. Their existence, hinted by the earlier numerical studies (arXiv:2504.10513), complements prior results on Cantor sets of infinitesimally small solutions. Our proof, based on the contraction principle, requires extensive computations that are performed on a computer by the means of rational arithmetic. We are able to significantly reduce their amount by a thorough analysis of the inverse of the associated linear operator, leading to sharper analytical bounds, as well as introduction of simplified versions of certain relevant operators. We provide examples of three solutions with specific frequency; however, our techniques and tools can be directly adapted to prove the existence of other solutions conjectured in (arXiv:2504.10513).
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 23 pages, 2 figures; supplementary material (Mathematica code and data files) is available at https://github.com/mmal/conformal-wave-cap

Analysis of PDEs.title: Shape optimisation of the maximum of the gradient of the torsion function on convex sets
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We analyse the boundary behaviour of the gradient of the torsion function $w_\Om$ in convex domains $\Om\subset\mathbb{R}^d$. We prove that its $L^\infty$-norm is attained at a boundary point and establish the stability of this norm under general (convex) perturbations. For problems of the form $$\sup\{\|\nabla w_{\Om}\|_\infty: \Om \subset \R^d,\textup{open, bounded and convex}, G(\Om)=m\},$$ where $G$ is either volume or perimeter, we show the existence of maximisers which are $C^1$-smooth, rotationally symmetric about an axis and contain a $(d-1)$- dimensional ball (of estimated size) in their boundary. Other constraints, whether geometric (such as diameter or circumradius) or variational (such as torsion or first Dirichlet eigenvalue), are also briefly discussed, and some of their characteristic behaviours are highlighted.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the Allen--Cahn equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Using the framework developed by OpenAI, we prove that finite Morse index implies $O(R^{n-1})$ energy growth for bounded entire solutions of the quartic Allen--Cahn equation in dimensions $4\leq n\leq9$, uniformly in the center of the ball. Combined with the cited finite-index classification results, this gives planar rigidity for $4\leq n\leq7$ and, for nonconstant solutions, multiplicity-one stable minimal cone blowdowns through dimension nine. Within the framework, we derive an additive adjacent-layer interaction estimate, a weighted curvature and defect estimate with exponent $p=9/4$, and the localization needed for exterior stability. The limiting interaction coefficient $48$ is sharp in the unrestricted low-defect class with sufficiently large logarithmic selection depth.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 89 pages, Revised version. Corrected several arguments, clarified the attribution of the main framework, and updated the AI-use statement. Main conclusions unchanged

Analysis of PDEs.title: Riesz Transform Bounds Imply Parabolic Uniform Rectifiability of Graphs
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that if a $(k+2)$-Ahlfors--David regular measure $μ$ in parabolic space $\mathbb P^n$ has support equal to a parabolic Lipschitz graph with sufficiently small Lipschitz constant, and the parabolic Riesz transform is bounded on $L^2(μ)$, then $μ$ is parabolic uniformly rectifiable and the graph is regular parabolic Lipschitz. The result holds for every integer $0\leq k\leq n-1$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Hörmander spectral multiplier theorem for fractional Hardy operators
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the fractional Laplacian with added critical or subcritical Hardy potential, called Hardy operator. We prove a Hörmander spectral multiplier theorem, i.e., the boundedness of sufficiently smooth multipliers of these Hardy operators on Lebesgue spaces. The range of admissible Lebesgue exponents is optimal, but the smoothness assumption is probably not. The proof combines the Helffer--Sjöstrand formula with a quantitative Jaffard lemma for operator-valued matrices.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Boundary regularity of harmonic functions in $C^1$ slit domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We establish precise upper and lower estimates for harmonic functions vanishing on the slit of a $C^1$ slit domain, with no assumption that the slit lies in a hyperplane. The classical $\sqrt{d}$ growth near the edge, $d$ being the distance to the slit, persists in this generality, up to an explicit factor \[\exp\Big( \pm C \int_ρ^r ω(s)\, \frac{ds}{s} \Big)\] determined by the $C^1$-modulus of continuity $ω$ of the slit, where $ρ< r$ are the two scales being compared. The upper estimates allow a right-hand side and non-zero boundary data. The correction factors remain bounded above and below by positive constants as $ρ\to0$ precisely when $ω$ satisfies the Dini condition. Moduli of continuity beyond the Dini regime, as is the case for the logarithmic moduli arising at singular sets in relevant free boundary problems, were not covered by the previous $C^{1,α}$ theory.
  Previously, the $\sqrt{d}$ growth was known for slits contained in a hyperplane, which additionally have a $C^{1,α}$ edge (De Silva, Savin). For Lipschitz slits, there are boundary Harnack principles, but no growth rate is identified precisely.
  The main technical ingredient is a change of coordinates flattening a Lipschitz slit domain onto the model half-hyperplane slit, with quantitative estimates up to second order. The construction is geometric and does not use the equation, so we expect it to be useful for other boundary regularity problems.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 45 pages, 4 figures. Changes in v2: we added the proof of Corollary 1.7 (previously named Corollary 1.8 in v1) and sharpened the assumptions on the data $f$ in Theorem 1.6

Analysis of PDEs.title: $Φ^4_3$ measures on compact Riemannian $3$-manifolds
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct the $Φ^4_3$ measure on an arbitrary 3-dimensional compact Riemannian manifold without boundary as an invariant probability measure of a singular stochastic partial differential equation. Proving the nontriviality and the covariance under Riemannian isometries of that measure gives a non-perturbative, non-topological interacting Euclidean quantum field measure on curved spaces in dimension 3. To control analytically several Feynman diagrams appearing in the construction of a number of random fields, we introduce a novel approach of renormalisation using microlocal and harmonic analysis. This allows to obtain a renormalized equation which involves some universal constants independent of the manifold. In a companion paper \cite{BDFTCompanion}, we develop all the tools from paradifferential and microlocal analysis that we use to build in our manifold setting a number of analytic and probabilistic objects.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Characterization of intrinsic parabolic Harnack inequalities for doubly nonlinear equations of slow diffusion type
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We characterize metric measure spaces that satisfy intrinsic parabolic Harnack inequalities for doubly nonlinear equations of slow diffusion type. The considered parabolic Harnack inequalities are intrinsic in the sense that the waiting time depends on the solution. Our main results shows that in a metric measure space with a doubling measure, such an intrinsic parabolic Harnack inequality holds if and only if a Poincaré inequality holds. We thus show that estimates in scale and function dependent intrinsic geometries can characterize scale and location invariant functional inequalities.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global solutions to the compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations in the half-space
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the initial boundary value problem for the compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson equations without damping in the three-dimensional half-space and in smooth exterior domains. The velocity satisfies the no-slip boundary condition, and the electric potential satisfies the homogeneous Neumann boundary condition. For small perturbations of a constant state in $H^3$, with a small initial electric field in $L^2$, we establish global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions. The uniform estimates combine density dissipation, tangential and normal derivative estimates, and a modified energy expressed through the Helmholtz projection. In exterior domains, boundary normal coordinates and localized elliptic estimates control the geometric terms. We also obtain algebraic decay in the full energy norm. In the half-space, finite tangential negative Sobolev norms of order $-s$, with $\frac12\leq s<1$, yield the rate $(1+t)^{-s/2}$. In exterior domains, integrable initial density and velocity perturbations yield the same form of estimate for $0<s<\frac14$. The exterior decay proof uses whole-space negative-order estimates for localized variables and the time integrability of the dissipation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniform Regularity for the Compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson System under Navier-Slip Boundary Conditions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we establish the existence of a local-in-time strong solution to the compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson system in a three-dimensional bounded smooth domain, subject to the general Navier--slip boundary condition. The solution is shown to be uniformly bounded in conormal Sobolev spaces, with uniform regularity estimates that are independent of the viscosity coefficients. As a consequence, we obtain the inviscid limit to the corresponding compressible Euler--Poisson system via a strong compactness argument.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Energies with values in networks and geometric quasiconvexity
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study the asymptotic behaviour, as $\varepsilon	o 0^+$, of the $p$-Dirichlet energy of maps $u\colonΩ\subset\mathbb{R}^2 	o \mathbb{R}^2$ constrained to take values in the rescaled periodic network $\varepsilon\mathcal Z$, where $\mathcal Z$ is a standard square network in $\mathbb{R}^2$. The oscillations are carried by the constraint in the target, not by the energy density, and their effect depends on $p$. For $1<p<2$ the constraint disappears in the limit: the $Γ$-limit is an integral functional on the whole of $m{W}^{1,p}(Ω, \mathbb{R}^2 )$, whose density is given by an asymptotic cell formula on tilted cells. This density is equal to $(|a_1|+|a_2|)^p$ on rank-one matrices $a\otimesν$, $|ν|=1$, and exceeds its convex envelope by a quantity comparable to $|\det A|\,|A|^{p-2}$, with constants of order $(2-p)^{-1}$. Consequently, although the original energy density is convex, the limit density is quasiconvex but neither convex nor polyconvex: quasiconvexity is generated by the geometry of the constraint. For $p\ge2$ the constraint survives in the limit as $\det
abla u=0$, and the $Γ$-limit is the degenerate energy $\int_Ω(|
abla u_1|+|
abla u_2|)^p\, m{d} x$, that is, the $p$-energy of $u$ considered as a map into the normed plane $(\mathbb{R}^2,|\cdot|_1)$, the metric limit of the networks.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Bilinear Strichartz estimates on the hyperbolic space and the cubic NLS
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove bilinear Strichartz estimates for the Schrödinger equation on the hyperbolic space. These bilinear estimates are then applied, as part of an I-method argument, to establish global well-posedness for the cubic defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the hyperbolic plane for regularities above 4/7. The I-method is implemented in physical space using a heat-based modified energy.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Application of Onsager's Variational Principle to the Navier-Stokes Equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this note we propose a basic $L^2$-based approach for studying the global and local energy equalities of the incompressible 3D Navier-Stokes equations in the standard energy class on $\mathbb{T}^3 \times (0,T]$. Motivated by L. Onsager's principle of least dissipation of energy (1931), we give a new sufficient condition for the energy equalities in terms of the limit of a sequence of minimizers. In particular, we show that the equalities are attained if this limit is non-vanishing. We observe that the indeterminacy in the vanishing case is reminiscent of turbulence-driven energy transfer dominating other transport processes.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 16 pages. Overall presentation improved; especially in Sections 1 and 4. Accepted for publication in Journal of Mathematical Fluid Mechanics

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniqueness for tv-regularized inverse problems with source in divergence form
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Inverse source problems in divergence form consist in finding a vector field with prescribed support S, whose divergence is the Laplacian of some observed potential. In this paper, we assume the unknown vector field is a vector-valued measure, and we study the corresponding least square inversion problems, regularized by penalizing the total variation, without discretizing the criterion nor the unknown. We prove that this problem has a unique minimizer in the case where S is a slender set; i.e., it has zero Lebesgue measure and each connected component of its complement has infinite Lebesgue measure. The proof relies on a refinement of Smirnov's decomposition of divergence-free measures [62] which is of independent interest.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The elastic figure-eight knot is not planar
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that every elastic knot in any non-torus twist knot class is not planar. In particular, this disproves a numerically motivated planarity conjecture for elastic figure-eight knots.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Peaking self-similar solutions and continuation after blow-up for a quasilinear Hardy-Hénon equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the quasilinear Hardy-Hénon equation $$ u_t=Δu^m+|x|^σu^p, \quad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^N\times(0,T), $$ in the range of exponents and dimension $$ N\geq3, \quad σ\in(-2,\infty), \quad m>1, \quad p>p_S(σ)=\frac{m(N+2σ+2)}{N-2}. $$ We establish sharp ranges of exponents $(m,p,σ)$ guaranteeing existence of \emph{peaking solutions} in backward self-similar form $$ u(x,t)=(T-t)^{-α}f(|x|(T-t)^{-β}). $$ By peaking solutions we understand solutions blowing up at a finite time $T\in(0,\infty)$ but allowing for a continuation after the blow-up time. As a remarkable outcome, a number of ranges of exponents $σ$ and $m$ for which peaking solutions exist for any $p>p_S(σ)$ are deduced, contrasting to the previously considered exponent $σ=0$, where a Lepin-type critical exponent $p_L$ provides an upper bound for $p$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Optimal time decay of the Boltzmann equation with cutoff soft potentials in the whole space
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Since Strain's work \cite{Strain-2012-KRM} on almost optimal time decay rates for the microscopic part of perturbative classical solutions to the Boltzmann system with soft potentials via the time-velocity splitting method, how to obtain the optimal decay of the microscopic part has remained unsolved. In this paper, we resolve this problem by developing a nonlinear energy estimate method different from the time-velocity splitting approach. The proof relies on a combination of a hierarchy of time-weighted energy estimates, the damping factor \(e^{-ν(v)(t-τ)}\), and a dyadic decomposition of velocity space.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Geometry property of stochastic parabolic equations and Prékopa-Leindler inequality on bounded domains
