Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the preservation of spatial concavity and log-concavity for stochastic parabolic equations posed on bounded convex domains. For the linear noise, by using Minkowski convolutions, we establish the convexity preservation of solution almost surely. For the nonlinear noise, by using Itô formula, the impact of noise is given. Moreover, we establish the relationship between the weighted (stochastic) Prékopa-Leindler inequality and properties of (stochastic) parabolic equation on bounded domain, which is new even for deterministic case.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Semilinear Schrödinger equation with harmonic potential and combined power-type nonlinearities
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the Cauchy problem for the semilinear Schrödinger equation with a harmonic potential and combined power-type nonlinearities. The goal is to classify initial data that lead to either global existence or blowup solutions by using an enhanced cross-constrained variational theory. First, we review and analyze this variational approach, pinpointing the main issue for our specific problem. We then introduce new variational structures by carefully selecting terms in the energy functional and adjusting their weights, enabling us to create eight cross-constrained variational combinations and related manifolds to distinguish initial data that result in global solutions or finite-time blowup. Using these structures, we examine three initial energy levels: negative, non-negative low, and high energy. Notably, we prove that for any initial data with negative energy, solutions blow up in finite time regardless of their size. Throughout the study, we utilize these new variational frameworks and functionals to systematically classify initial data for global existence or finite-time blowup. We highlight the comprehensiveness of our approach as we analyze numerous combinations of the energy and mass terms, despite the complexity involved. Interestingly, we find that when initial energy is minimized, classifications based on different functionals coincide. For high initial energy, an unresolved issue even for the standard Schrödinger equation, we develop a strategy controlling bounds of energy to classify the solution dynamics, including global existence or blowup, for our model. We also provide a complete proof for the standard case addressing this open problem.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Long Time Behavior and Stabilization for Displacement Monotone Mean Field Games
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper is devoted to the study of the long time behavior of Nash equilibria in Mean Field Games within the framework of displacement monotonicity. We first show that any two equilibria defined on the time horizon $[0,T]$ must be close as $T \to \infty$, in a suitable sense, independently of initial/terminal conditions. The way this stability property is made quantitative involves the $L^2$ distance between solutions of the associated Pontryagin system of FBSDEs that characterizes the equilibria. Therefore, this implies in particular the stability in the 2-Wasserstein distance for the two flows of probability measures describing the agent population density and the $L^2$ distance between the co-states of agents, that are related to the optimal feedback controls. We then prove that the value function of a typical agent converges as $T \to \infty$, and we describe this limit via an infinite horizon MFG system, involving an ergodic constant. All of our convergence results hold true in a unified way for deterministic and idiosyncratic noise driven Mean Field Games, in the case of strongly displacement monotone non-separable Hamiltonians. All these are quantitative at exponential rates.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Correctness of Biot's model of in situ leaching for incompressible liquid and compressible solid components
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study a mathematical model of in situ leaching of rare metals, in which the joint filtration of two liquids is governed by the microscopic model $\mathbb{A}^{\varepsilon}$. A key difficulty is the unknown (free) boundary $Γ(r)$ between solid and liquid components, determined by an additional condition on $Γ(r)$; no standard methods exist for this nonlinear problem. To resolve it, we apply the fixed point theorem. For a given function $r(\boldsymbol{x},t)$ from a set $\mathfrak{M}_{(0,T)}$ of sufficiently smooth functions describing the skeleton structure, we consider the auxiliary problem $\mathbb{B}^{\varepsilon}(r)$: an elliptic system for displacements of the liquid and solid components coupled with parabolic equations for the acid concentration. Selecting the weak solution of minimal smoothness, we apply the homogenization method to pass from the microscopic to the macroscopic description. The resulting macroscopic model $\mathbb{H}(r)$ contains a homogenized boundary condition that expresses the normal boundary velocity $V_{N}=\partial r/\partial t$ as a linear function of the acid concentration $c$. Since $c$ depends on $r$ via an operator $\mathbb{F}\colon\mathfrak{M}_{(0,T)}\to\mathfrak{M}_{(0,T)}$, we prove that $\mathbb{F}$ is Lipschitz continuous and, by Banach's theorem, possesses a unique fixed point $r^{*}$, which yields the unique solution $\mathbb{H}=\mathbb{H}(r^{*})$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Self-similar finite-time blowups with singular profiles of the generalized Constantin-Lax-Majda model: theoretical and numerical investigations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For the generalized Constantin-Lax-Majda model with a parameter $a$, we investigate novel scenarios of self-similar finite-time blowups that arise from a new setting where the smooth initial data satisfy a certain derivative degeneracy condition. In this setting, our numerical study reveals distinct self-similar blowup behaviors depending on the sign of $a$. For $a>0$, we observe one-scale self-similar blowups with regular profiles that have not been found in previous studies. In contrast, for $a\le 0$, we discover a novel two-scale self-similar blowup scenario where the outer profile converges to a singular function at the blowup time while the inner profile remains regular on a much smaller scale. Correspondingly, an $a$-parameterized family of singular self-similar profiles with explicit expressions are constructed for $a<0$ and shown to match nicely with the limiting profiles obtained in numerical simulation. In particular, for the specific case of $a=0$, we rigorously prove the convergence of the outer profile to an explicit singular function in self-similar coordinates. Furthermore, we demonstrate the two-scale nature of the blowup in this scenario by showing that the local inner profile behavior around the singularity point of the outer profile is governed by a traveling wave on a smaller scale. To support this observation, we rigorously establish the existence of such traveling wave solutions via a fixed-point method.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 59 pages, 20 figures; (1) Made Theorem 2.7 more complete and elaborate with more detailed properties of the traveling wave profiles; (2) Added a formal proof of Theorem 2.7 at the end of Section 7; (3) Improved writing and presentation throughout Section 7; (4) Corrected a non-essential typo in Lemma 7.5; (5) Added a figure of multiple numerically computed traveling wave profiles in Appendix C

Analysis of PDEs.title: Well-posedness for the Cubic Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation With Nonlinearity Supported on a Hypersurface
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that the 2-d cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation with nonlinearity supported on a line or a sphere is globally well-posed in \(H^1(\mathbb{R}^2)\). For higher dimensions, we prove that the equation with hyperplane-supported nonlinearity is locally well-posed in suitable anisotropic Sobolev spaces. We also prove that the equation with sphere-supported nonlinearity is globally well-posed in \(H^1(\mathbb{R}^n)\) for radial data.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Gagliardo--Nirenberg extremals on manifolds with small holes
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the sharp homogeneous Dirichlet Gagliardo--Nirenberg quotient on a closed Riemannian manifold with holes of small capacity and connected complements. For each fixed exponent $2<q<2^*$, the nonnegative $L^2$-normalized extremal exists and is unique when the first Dirichlet eigenvalue $λ_D$ is sufficiently small. If the ambient volume is $V$ and $β=n(q-2)/2$, the sharp constant satisfies $C_D=V^{1-q/2}λ_D^{-β/2}(1+O(λ_D))$. For the normalized first eigenfunction $\varphi_D$, we obtain $\|u_D-\varphi_D\|_{H^1}=O(λ_D^{3/2})$ and $C_D/W_{M_D}(\varphi_D)=1+O(λ_D^2)$, together with a quantitative stability estimate in terms of the relative deficit. The constants depend only on the ambient manifold and the exponent. On general compact manifolds with Dirichlet boundary conditions, we prove compactness above the Euclidean sharp constant and describe concentration at equality. Positive scalar curvature at one interior point implies attainment. For the $L^2$-critical nonlinear Schrödinger energy, the mass threshold for negative energy tends to zero as the capacity of the holes tends to zero, whereas the threshold for unboundedness below is unchanged.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 17 pages, split off from arXiv:2601.22665v1. Comments highly appreciated!

Analysis of PDEs.title: Coupling perturbations of the conformal Einstein-Dirac system on round spheres
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the conformal Einstein-Dirac system on the round sphere $S^m$, $m\geq3$, with coupling coefficient $1+\eps k$, where $k\in C^2(S^m,\R)$ and $\eps$ is small. Morse and degree conditions yield solutions with positive scalar component, and a generic nondegeneracy condition gives multiplicity modulo spinorial symmetries. For a suitable fixed coefficient, we obtain a noncompact solution sequence with infinitely many distinct energy values. A Kazdan-Warner identity gives nonexistence for a smooth Morse potential and its small $C^2$-perturbations, even with positive coupling. The existence proofs use a local reduction in the interior of the positive cone, accommodating the negative powers occurring when $m\geq5$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Homogenization of a thin linear elastic plate reinforced with a periodic mosaic of small rigid plates
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In the framework of linearized elasticity, we study thin elastic composite plates with thickness $δ$. The plates contain small, rigid rectangular plates distributed periodically along $\varepsilon$. Between two neighboring rigid plates is an elastic beam with thickness $δ< \varepsilon/3 < 1$. Through a simultaneous process of homogenization and dimension reduction, we obtain the limit model. Our analysis yields Korn-type inequalities adapted to the rigid-elastic geometry of the structure and provides a precise characterization of the limit deformation and displacement fields. In the $2$D limit problem, the bending is the sum of two functions, each depending on only one variable. This is due to the fact that the mixed derivatives of the outer-plane displacement vanish. Finally, the limiting 2D problem is two decoupled plates or strips, each one with just three degrees of freedom: shear along the strip axis, the cross-contraction (-extension), and the cross-bending. The corresponding correctors are defined in the same way in the periodicity cell. In the linearized setting, all the correctors are decomposed.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 39 pages, 4 figures. To appear in Asymptotic Analysis

Analysis of PDEs.title: Linear Stability and a Turning Point Principle for Barotropic Liquid Stars with a Free Boundary in General Relativity
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the linear stability of spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat steady states of the Einstein-Euler system describing a liquid star surrounded by vacuum. The equation of state has positive surface density, positive causal sound speed, and an asymptotically linear high-density limit. We construct the equilibrium family and derive the linearized equation with a Robin boundary condition. The linearized operator has discrete real spectrum, and its negative Morse index equals the number of growing modes. We prove that the linearized operator around steady states with large central redshift admits a growing mode, while such growing modes do not exist for steady states with small central redshift. A parameter derivative of the equilibrium family provides a regular interior zero solution of the linearized equation, whose boundary defect is a nonzero multiple of the parameter derivative of the total mass. This gives a turning point principle: the kernel is one-dimensional precisely at mass critical points, and the sign of the crossing eigenvalue is determined by the bending of the mass-radius curve.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Bounds of singular sets for elliptic equations in $C^{1, Dini}$ domains with singular potentials
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the quantitative codimension-two estimate for the singular set in the boundary neighborhoods of the solutions of \begin{equation*} Δu+V(x)u=0\qquad\text{in }Ω, \qquad u=0\qquad\text{on }\partialΩ, \end{equation*} where $Ω\subset\mathbb R^n$ is a bounded $C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}$ domain and $V\in L^p(Ω)$ for some $p>n$. We first prove the explicit upper bound for the doubling index is given by $C(n,p,Ω)(1+\|V\|_{L^p(Ω)}^{\frac{2p}{3p-2n}})$.The analytic input is an interior volume estimate for solutions of second order elliptic equations with uniformly elliptic Dini leading coefficients and $V\in L^p$. Using the quantitative doubling index bound, boundary flattening, we show an explicit upper bound for singular sets in the neighborhood of the boundary of the $C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}$ domain.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Well-posedness for $p(x)$-Laplacian parabolic equations under a multiple-regime setting on an annulus
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper proposes an energy-variational framework for the well-posedness of the initial boundary value problem of the parabolic equation with variable exponents on an annulus, under the multiple-regime setting consisting of the subcritical, critical and supercritical regimes of the variable exponents. The multiple-regime setting leads to the appearance of the critical and supercritical regions of positive measure, which cause the failure of the classical Sobolev embedding and the lack of compactness. To address the challenges posed by multiple regimes to well-posedness within the energy framework, we recover the compact Sobolev embedding for a class of radially symmetric functions by the Strauss inequality and obtain the local existence of the solution via the combination of the subdifferential technique and the Principle of Symmetric Criticality for any given radially symmetric initial data. Additionally, the uniqueness result is also given with the recovered Sobolev embedding. Moreover, examining the impact on well-posedness of solutions caused by the variable exponents crossing three sensitive regions, we establish a variational structure of the potential well theory for the evolution equation under the multiple-regime setting on the annulus. For subcritical and critical initial energy levels, we consider the non-positive and positive initial energy cases separately. We obtain the finite-time blow-up of the solution with non-positive initial energy and the threshold condition for global existence and finite-time blow-up of the solution with positive initial energy. For supercritical initial energy level, several sufficient criteria for the global existence and finite-time blow-up of the solution are given. Finally, the above results, including global existence and finite-time blow-up, are generalized to a more general locally symmetric domain containing an annulus.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Hyperbolic Monge-Ampère Equation on a Cylinder: Well-Posedness and Stability
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper develops a rigorous analytic framework for the hyperbolic Monge-Ampère equation on strip-like domains, which model wrinkled patterns in thin elastic sheets. Our work addresses the rigid side of the classical rigidity-flexibility dichotomy by defining this regime not by high smoothness, but by the more fundamental property of partial convexity. The hodograph transformation is the natural tool for this setting, as its validity is predicated on partial convexity. It converts the nonlinear Monge-Ampère equation into a linear damped wave equation, allowing us to formulate a well-posed Cauchy-Goursat problem. A key challenge is the corner singularity that arises where characteristic and non-characteristic boundary data meet. To resolve this, we develop a parametrix-corrector decomposition that captures the solution's inherent singular behavior. This method recasts the problem as a singular Volterra integral equation, for which we prove the existence and uniqueness of a new class of hodograph weak solutions. Finally, we derive energy estimates to establish the quantitative stability of these rigid solutions under perturbations of the underlying curvature function.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Weighted and nonlocal Poisson equations on domains with capacity density conditions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for global Hölder solvability of weighted Poisson equations and related fractional problems. On domains satisfying a capacity density condition, a nonnegative measure with bounded support depth admits a bounded globally Hölder continuous zero-boundary solution if and only if it satisfies an interior Morrey-type growth condition. Conversely, uniform boundary decay estimates for solutions with localized nonnegative sources characterize the capacity density condition. Analogous characterizations are established for the restricted and spectral fractional Laplacians. Our approach is based on weighted strong barriers and also yields two-weight Hardy inequalities, compact trace embeddings, and global Hölder solvability for nonlinear Dirichlet-to-Neumann operators.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global recovery of a scalar diffusivity from a single final state
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove global uniqueness and Lipschitz stability for a scalar diffusivity in the heat equation from a single final state at any prescribed positive time. On each prescribed uniformly elliptic $C^{1,α}$-bounded class with known coefficient boundary values, we choose a constant initial datum and a spatially constant exponential boundary input that work for the entire class. The result holds on smooth bounded connected domains in every dimension $n\ge2$ and gives an affirmative answer to \cite[Problem~8.2]{Alessandrini} within these classes. The stability estimate controls the $L^2$ diffusivity difference by the $H^2$ final-state difference, and this data norm is optimal within the Sobolev scale for the chosen experiment.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global regularity for 3D large spherically symmetric degenerate compressible Navier-Stokes equations with superlinear BD viscosity and far-field vacuum
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Superlinear density-dependent viscosity presents a fundamental obstacle of global regularity to the compressible Navier-Stokes equations in the presence of far-field vacuum: the viscous diffusion vanishes at infinity, so excluding vacuum on bounded sets does not suffice to control the flow globally. For $α\in (1,11.7)$ and $γ\in [2α-1,3α-1)$ , we establish global regularity for arbitrarily large, strong, finite-mass initial data with positive density at every finite point and vacuum at infinity. First, we introduce new rescalsed variables regarding the velocity, effective velocity and mass, then we exploit several novel quantities near the center and employ a refined maximum principle to establish the Lipschitz continuity of the velocity at the center-thereby resolving the singularity of the velocity gradient. Another key mechanism is a quantitative control of material volume distortion that remains effective in the vacuum tail. Conservative estimates for the physical and effective velocity gradients yield uniformly vanishing exterior variation tails. These estimates identify a material trajectory with small cumulative Jacobian variation and lead to two-sided bounds for the exterior volume Jacobian, making the evolving density comparable to its initial value along particle paths. On spatial scales determined by the initial density, the resulting degenerate equations admit uniform parabolic estimates that recover control of the physical deformation without a global density lower bound. Combined with compact positivity estimates and a one-sided Glaeser inequality, this closes a homogeneous continuation argument without imposing $L^2$-integrability on the density powers themselves. The solutions conserve mass, preserve far-field vacuum, and remain smooth and strictly positive on every compact spacetime cylinder.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Dynamic Inventory Rationing Model for Last-Mile Delivery of Medication in Liberia's Community Health Program
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the dynamic allocation of scarce medications in Liberia's community health program. A central warehouse supplies a health facility and the Community Health Assistants (CHAs) it supervises. When a CHA runs out of medication, patients are referred to the facility, incurring travel costs if they complete the referral and remain untreated otherwise. Allocating inventory to CHAs allows more patients to receive treatment without traveling, while retaining inventory centrally preserves flexibility to respond to uncertain demand. The allocation problem must balance these considerations while accounting for fairness across locations. We formulate this problem as a finite-horizon stochastic control problem whose objective combines the costs of referrals and untreated patients with a demand-weighted fairness utility. Because standard dynamic programming methods are computationally intractable in this setting, we develop a continuous-time approximation that involves controlling the drift rate of a reflected Brownian motion. We then adapt the deep splitting method, using deep neural networks to approximate the value function and its gradient and compute a dynamic allocation policy. We calibrate the model using data on malaria cases among children in the Fangonda region of Lofa County, Liberia, and evaluate the proposed policy in the original discrete-time model. In the baseline setting, our policy reduces operating costs by about 6% relative to the strongest benchmark, the fairness-only policy, while retaining approximately 98% of its fairness utility. Additional experiments show that higher referral costs shift inventory toward CHAs and reduce local unmet demand, while greater demand variability increases our policy's performance over the fairness-only benchmark. Our model and computational approach provide a framework for studying similar last-mile allocation problems.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Wave breaking for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we investigate wave breaking for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations. We establish more general wave breaking criteria that strictly extend earlier wave breaking criteria for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations. The approach relies on analyzing the monotonicity and continuity properties of a linear combination comprising the supremum and infimum of the solution's slope. Further generalizations are demonstrated via applications to the Camassa-Holm equation, the $μ$-Camassa-Holm equation and the hyperelastic rod equation. Our refined approach yields more precise wave breaking criteria, thereby extending the theoretical understanding of singularity formation in dispersive waves.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Asymptotic behavior of the one-dimensional Vlasov--Poisson system with a repulsive harmonic potential
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the one-dimensional Vlasov--Poisson system with a repulsive harmonic potential. For repulsive self-interactions, we prove modified scattering for initial data of arbitrary size, assuming only velocity weights and one derivative; no smallness, symmetry, compact support, or spatial moments are required. In the lens variables of \cite{HK26}, the self-consistent force carries a nonintegrable time weight. We remove it by a momentum correction that solves a forced Burgers equation; the repulsive sign makes this correction monotone, which gives bounds for large data. We also construct modified wave operators for both signs of the interaction. Together with \cite{VR24,BVR25,HK26}, this gives a scattering theory in every dimension.

Functional Analysis.title: Variational principles and aplications to symmetric PDEs
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we explore various equivalences of Ekeland's variational principle within the framework of group-invariant mappings. We introduce and analyze several key theorems, including the Drop theorem, the Petal theorem, Caristi-Kirk fxed-point theorem, and Takahashi's theorem, all of them within this context. Moreover, we extend the classical Drop theorem and Petal theorem to a more generalized setting. We also demonstrate the practical signifcance of these findings through numerous applications to diverse areas of mathematics. In particular, in the context of partial differential equations, we explore their implications on the solution of the Plateau problem, and in control theory. We also extend the classical Pontyargin maximum principle.

Functional Analysis.title: Characterization of the boundedness of the segment multiplier on rearrangement-invariant spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: Given rearrangement-invariant (r.i.) spaces $X$ and $Y$, we show that the segment multiplier, the truncated Hilbert transform, and the discrete Hilbert transform (on the associated discretized space) are bounded from $X$ to $Y$ simultaneously. Moreover, when $X = Y$ this boundedness is characterized by a condition on a pair of Boyd-type indices. We also exhibit an r.i. space on which the segment multiplier is bounded while the (non-truncated) Hilbert transform fails to be bounded.

Functional Analysis.title: Sobolev inequalities for sections and projections of log-concave functions
Functional Analysis.summary: Higher order sharp Sobolev and local Sobolev type inequalities for log-concave functions are established. The new inequalities directly imply the isoperimetric inequalities by Bollobás and Thomason in 1995, by Liakopoulos in 2019, and the recently discovered local isoperimetric inequalities from [1]. In order to do so, we make use of three ingredients. First, sets of functional inequalities proven by Alonso-Gutiérrez, Bernués, Brazitikos and Carbery in 2021. Second, a multidimensional polynomial optimization result that originated in [1] and was initiated by Bollobás and Thomason. Third, a new integral formula for the projection of a log-concave function that links the geometric part with the more functional versions via some dependence on the Hessian matrix restricted to subspaces.

Functional Analysis.title: Hardy inequalities on the positive integer lattice: a dimensional transition
Functional Analysis.summary: We determine exactly in which dimensions the sharp Hardy coefficient on the positive integer lattice agrees with that on the positive Euclidean cone, with Dirichlet conditions on every coordinate face. Equality holds in dimensions one and two, whereas the discrete coefficient is strictly smaller in every dimension at least three. An exact transformation identifies the lattice problem with a weighted Dirichlet problem on a cube. A tangential integration identity evaluates the defect of an explicit critical profile and proves the dimensional transition. The continuous coefficient remains the lower edge of the essential spectrum of the transformed operator; below that edge, the sharp discrete coefficient is a simple eigenvalue with a positive eigenfunction. In dimension three, an explicit supersolution places the coefficient strictly between twelve and forty-nine quarters. A representation on a product of three-dimensional spheres relates the spectral threshold to the local geometry of the transformed problem.

Functional Analysis.title: The $L^2$-Cartesian Numerical Radii of Hilbert Space Operators
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a complex Hilbert space, and let $T=H+iK\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ be the Cartesian decomposition of $T$, where $H=H^{*}$ and $K=K^{*}$. We introduce the $L^2$-Cartesian numerical radius and study its basic properties. We compare it with the classical numerical radius $ω(T)$. In particular, we establish the sharp estimate $ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}ω(T)\le \wcart{2}(T)\le ω(T), $ and establish lower and upper bounds in terms of the Cartesian parts $H,K$. We also give an equality characterization and explicit sharpness examples. As a consequence, we obtain $\frac{1}{4}\left\|T^{*}T+TT^{*}\right\|\le \wcart{2}(T)^2\le ω(T)^2. $ More generally, we study the $L^p$-Cartesian numerical radius and prove the sharp comparison $ c_p\,ω(T)\le \wcart{p}(T)\le ω(T),\qquad 1\le p<\infty. $ Finally, we present a block-operator analogue of the classical refinement of the triangle inequality.

Functional Analysis.title: Recent perspectives on the Invariant Subspace Problem
Functional Analysis.summary: We review recent work connected with the invariant subspace problem for operators, in particular new developments in the last 15 years. In particular, we include discussions of almost-invariant subspaces, universal operators, specific classes of operators and new results in the framework of Banach spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: Expansivity of algebraic semigroup actions
Functional Analysis.summary: For a semigroup $S$ and a right $\mathbb{Z}[S]$-submodule $J\leq \mathbb{Z}[S]^n$, we study expansivity of the algebraic action of $S$ induced on the Pontryagin dual of $\mathbb{Z}[S]^n/J$. We completely determine the class of semigroups for which expansivity of this action is characterized by the triviality of $J^\perp$, in terms of the existence of a finite subset $K\subseteq S$ such that $S=KS$. This condition is satisfied in particular by every monoid, and more generally by every semigroup with a left unital convolution Banach algebra, in which case we are able to extend the characterization of expansivity in terms of an invertibility condition when $J$ is finitely generated. We also exhibit examples of non-unital semigroups satisfying the hypotheses of our results.
Functional Analysis.comment: Added Corollary C, which applies to semigroups with a stably finite Banach algebra, and subsection 4.2 showing that inverse semigroups with finitely many idempotents satisfy this condition

Functional Analysis.title: Restricted isometries in finite-dimensional $\ell^p$-spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: For $d,n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq1}$ and $p\in[1,\infty)\setminus\{2\}$, we characterize all linear maps $s\colon\ell_d^p\to\ell_n^p$ for which there is $E\subseteq X_d$ such that $\|s(ξ)\|_p=\|ξ|_E\|_p$ for every $ξ\in\ell_d^p$. We call these maps \emph{restricted isometries}. Our Lamperti-type theorem gives a unique description of each such operator using a set transformation, a positive amplitude function, and a unimodular phase function. In particular, it includes noninjective and nonsurjective operators, even when the dimensions differ. We further characterize restricted isometries between finite $\ell^p$-spaces with arbitrary positive atomic weights. Applications include formulas counting set transformations and uniform restricted isometries, as well as a geometric description of all restricted isometries with fixed column supports.

Functional Analysis.title: Commutative exact superalgebras and super-modular tensor categories
Functional Analysis.summary:
We extend the theory of commutative exact algebras in braided finite tensor categories (Shimizu-Yadav) to superalgebras, motivated by extensions of vertex operator (super)algebras.
  For a braided category $\C$ let $\B=\C^{\gr}$ be the category of $\mathbb Z/2$-graded objects with the Koszul-signed braiding. It is the underlying category of the supercategory of Creutzig-Kanade-McRae. A supercommutative superalgebra $A=A_0\oplus A_1$ in $\C$ is the same
  as a commutative algebra $\bA$ in $\B$, and super-local modules are the local $\bA$-modules.
  Hence rigidity, pivotality and ribbon statements are instances of the ordinary theorems, with the ribbon condition $θ_{A_0}=\id$, $θ_{A_1}=\varepsilon\,\id$, where $\varepsilon=\pm1$ is fixed by the statistics of the odd part. For $\C$ non-degenerate and $\bA$ haploid and exact we prove
  that the category of super-local modules is a braided finite tensor category whose Müger center is $\mathsf{sVect}$. It is the centralizer of a fermion in a non-degenerate category obtained by condensing in $\C\boxtimes(\text{toric code})$. If $\C$ is ribbon and $\bA$ is symmetric Frobenius it is ribbon. We construct examples from graded simple currents, treat the free fermion and the symplectic fermion,
  and compare with Creutzig-Kanade-McRae and Creutzig-McRae-Shimizu-Yadav.

Functional Analysis.title: Azumaya descent and étale-local cyclotomic comparison: a noncommutative filtration
Functional Analysis.summary:
Bhatt-Morrow-Scholze motivic filtration on topological Hochschild homology ($THH$) is extended to Azumaya algebras over quasisyntomic rings. We prove the Azumaya descent theorem:
  $THH$ of such an algebra is equivalent, as an underlying spectrum, to $THH$ of its center,
  normalized on $π_0$ by the reduced trace instead of the unit map. This comparison $Φ_A$ is not shown to be étale-locally cyclotomic.
  But what is cyclotomic étale-locally is a separate Morita trace, agreeing with $Φ_A$ only on $π_0$. The resulting transported filtration is exactly the center BMS filtration, well defined up to the automorphism ambiguity of $Φ_A$. It is insensitive to the Brauer class, reflected instead by $K$-theoretic and module-categorical pairings $THH$ does not see. We establish the analogous statement for derived Azumaya algebras over connective $\mathbb{E}_\infty$-rings, under a connectivity hypothesis.

Functional Analysis.title: Joint q-Numerical Ranges of Continuous Operator-Valued Functions
Functional Analysis.summary: This paper develops a unified theory of joint $q$-numerical ranges $\Fq(F)$ for continuous functions $F:\Om \to \B(\cH)$, where $\Om$ is a compact Hausdorff space and $\B(\cH)$ denotes the $C^*$-algebra of bounded linear operators on a complex Hilbert space $\cH$. We prove that $\Fq(F)$ is totally bounded in $\cC(\Om)$, the space of continuous complex-valued functions on $\Om$, and establish the upper semicontinuity of the set-valued map $F\mapsto \Fq(F)$, and show that $\Fq(F)$ is compact when $\cH$ is finite-dimensional. The main result of the paper is a realization theorem. We prove that, for every totally bounded subset $K$ of $\cC(\Om)$ and every $q\in \C$ with $|q|=1$, there exist a Hilbert space $\cH$ and a continuous function $F:\Om\to\B(\cH)$ such that $qK\subset \Fq(F)\subset q\cok$. Consequently, if $K$ is closed and convex, then $\Fq(F)=qK$. As applications, we derive analogous realization results for bounded subsets in $\C^n$ and for totally bounded subsets in arbitrary Banach spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: $L$-tauberian operators and subspaces with equi-integrable unit ball
Functional Analysis.summary: We introduce the class $LW_+$ of $L$-tauberian operators and its dual counterpart, the class $MW_-$ of $M$-cotauberian operators. We obtain sequential, perturbative, and algebraic characterizations of these classes. As a consequence, every $T\in LW_+(E,Y)$ is disjointly non-singular, and the converse implication holds if and only if every dispersed subspace of $E$ has equi-integrable unit ball. For $E=L_p$, the latter property depends on $p$. For $1\leq p<2$, equi-integrability of the unit ball is equivalent to dispersedness, and $L$-tauberian operators coincide with disjointly non-singular operators, while for $p\geq 2$ these equivalences fail. Moreover, $LW_+(L_p)$ is neither open nor stable under composition. Applying a result of Haydon, Odell, and Schlumprecht, we show that for $2<p<\infty$ every infinite dimensional dispersed subspace of $L_p$ contains an infinite dimensional subspace with equi-integrable unit ball. However, we give an example showing that this is not true for $p=2$.

Functional Analysis.title: A solution to a conjecture on the norm of the Copson operator minus the Identity for monotone sequences
Functional Analysis.summary: We investigate the operator distance between the Identity and the Copson operator on the cone of nonnegative, nonincreasing sequences within the Lebesgue sequence spaces $\ell^p(\mathbb{N})$. By proving the exact value of this distance, we confirm a conjecture originally formulated by A. Ben Said, S. Boza, and J. Soria in ``The norm of Hardy-type oscillation operators in the discrete and continuous settings'' (\emph{Analysis and Applications}, 2025).

Functional Analysis.title: Nadler Theorem on Generalized Metric Spaces with Weighted Graphs
Functional Analysis.summary: We introduce a generalized metric space endowed with a weighted graph and establish sufficient conditions for the existence of fixed points for set-valued mappings that satisfy a contractive condition only along the links of the graph. To demonstrate the applicability and significance of our results, several illustrative examples are presented. As an application, we establish the solvability of a class of integral problems involving set-valued data.

Functional Analysis.title: Weak-$L^\infty$ and BMO with Hausdorff Content
Functional Analysis.summary:
The space of weak-$L^{\infty}$ on measure space was introduced by Bennett et al. (Ann. of Math., 113(1981), 601-611) and proved to contain the space of $L^\infty$ and possess the appropriate interpolation property. In this paper, we are aimed to continue this line of research on the Euclidean space $\mathbb R^n$ endowed with Hausdorff content, which is a low-dimensional outer measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$, and fails to be additive or absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measures. But low-dimensional subsets, such as fractals, of $\mathbb{R}^n$ are Hausdorff capacitable. Precisely, in the setting of Hausdorff content, an analogue of weak-$L^\infty$ is defined and proved to possess an improved Marcinkiewicz interpolation theorem. Moreover, we show that the space of functions with bounded mean oscillation associated to the Hausdorff content is embedded into this new weak-$L^\infty$ space by establishing a key estimate for the distribution via a packing condition.
  As a by-product,
  the boundedness of the Hardy-Littlewood operator on the space of weak-$L^{\infty}$ is established.

Functional Analysis.title: Block Toeplitz Operators, Matrix Valued Truncated Toeplitz operators, and Conjugations
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we characterize the complex symmetry of block Toeplitz operators on the Hardy-Hilbert space H2(E) with conjugation C_{u,λ}, where E is a finite dimensional Hilbert space. We also extend the application of this conjugation to matrix valued truncated Toeplitz operators.

Functional Analysis.title: On the Propeller Conjecture
Functional Analysis.summary: We simplify and improve OpenAI's proof of the propeller conjecture of Khot and Naor from 2008: the sum of the squared lengths of the Gaussian moments of any partition of Euclidean space is at most $9/(8π)$. We show equality only occurs for three 120 degree sectors in the plane (up to symmetries, measure zero changes, and taking orthogonal cross products with Euclidean space). We also remove computer assistance from the three-dimensional case of the conjecture, which previously used an epsilon net traversal.

Functional Analysis.title: Displacement structure and eigenvalue bounds for multiband prolate matrices
Functional Analysis.summary:
We obtain explicit non-asymptotic bounds for the eigenvalue transition of multiband prolate matrices. Let $S\subset[-1/2,1/2]$ be a finite union of pairwise disjoint intervals, and let $λ_0\ge\cdots\geλ_{N-1}$ be the eigenvalues of $B_{N,S}$. If $ν$ is the number of boundary points of $S$ on the frequency torus, then, for every $0<\eps<1/2$, \[ \#\{k:\eps<λ_k<1-\eps\} \le ν\ceil{\frac{\log(4N)}{π^2} \log\!\left(\frac{4}{\eps(1-\eps)}\right)}. \] Compared with the multiband estimate of Zhu and Wakin~\cite{wakin2017approximating}, this improves the dependence on $\eps$ from order $1/[\eps(1-\eps)]$ to logarithmic dependence. We also prove a second bound in which the main logarithmic term depends on the time--bandwidth product $N|S|$ rather than only on $N$.
  We also compare $S$ with frequency sets having fewer boundary points. Using a classical large-sieve estimate, we take into account not only the total size of the change in the frequency set, but also how that change is distributed. For sets with many small gaps, this can give a bound growing like $\log N$ for fixed $\eps$, even when the bounds based only on the total size of the gaps grow at least linearly in $N$. We also obtain exponential bounds for individual eigenvalues and use them to estimate the error in approximating sampled multiband signals by leading eigenvectors. A discretization argument gives corresponding results for the continuous problem. Numerical examples compare the bounds and examine how the locations of the frequency intervals affect the eigenvalues.

Functional Analysis.title: Weighted and nonlocal Poisson equations on domains with capacity density conditions
Functional Analysis.summary: We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for global Hölder solvability of weighted Poisson equations and related fractional problems. On domains satisfying a capacity density condition, a nonnegative measure with bounded support depth admits a bounded globally Hölder continuous zero-boundary solution if and only if it satisfies an interior Morrey-type growth condition. Conversely, uniform boundary decay estimates for solutions with localized nonnegative sources characterize the capacity density condition. Analogous characterizations are established for the restricted and spectral fractional Laplacians. Our approach is based on weighted strong barriers and also yields two-weight Hardy inequalities, compact trace embeddings, and global Hölder solvability for nonlinear Dirichlet-to-Neumann operators.

Functional Analysis.title: Optimal Non-Homogeneous Improvements of the Anisotropic Hardy Inequality
Functional Analysis.summary: We consider the Hardy inequality associated with a strongly convex Finsler norm $F$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and we study its optimal non-homogeneous improvements in the whole range $1<p<\infty$. We show that the anisotropic Hardy difference controls a weighted critical Sobolev norm when $1<p<n$, a weighted exponential integrability of Trudinger type when $p=n$, where the Hardy term is replaced by its Leray logarithmic correction, and a weighted Hölder seminorm when $p>n$, proving in each regime that the logarithmic weights appear with the optimal exponents. In the borderline case $p=n$ this extends to general functions the optimal exponent previously known only for anisotropically radial functions. The proofs rely on a common ground-state reduction, combined with a splitting into an $F_o$-radial and a mean-free part for $1<p\le n$, and with an anisotropic Morrey representation formula for $p>n$.

Functional Analysis.title: On the transformation of unbounded convergent sequences by linear operators on Banach lattices
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we introduce a weak variant of the concept of unbounded Dunford-Pettis linear operators, which we call unbounded weak Dunford-Pettis operators. We investigate the properties of this new class, establish inclusion and coincidence results involving unbounded Dunford-Pettis operators, and examine its relationship with the class of unbounded absolutely weakly continuous operators.

Functional Analysis.title: Weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for noncommutative maximal truncated rough singular integrals
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove a weak type $(1,1)$ estimate for maximal truncations of noncommutative rough singular integrals whose angular kernels satisfy the classical $L\log L$ integrability and cancellation conditions. The main ingredient of the proof is a new linearization method for handling the maximal truncations acting on the bad functions arising from the noncommutative Calderón--Zygmund decomposition.

Functional Analysis.title: Dunford-Pettis Multilinear Operators and Their Weak Variant on Banach Spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we address broader concepts of Dunford-Pettis operators, presenting new classes and results that relate this class to others already well studied in the literature, as well as an approach outside the origin. We also investigate inclusion results and conditions for the coincidence of this class with previously studied classes and with new classes that arise throughout this work.

Functional Analysis.title: Topological cones and positively polarizable hyperbolic norms
Functional Analysis.summary: In the first part of this article, we study linear cones over totally ordered fields. We show that for each such cone there uniquely exists a universal vector space (called its spanned vector space) into which it embeds as a generating convex cone. Moreover, we investigate topologies on cones for which the natural cone operations are continuous, and study how these topologies carry over to the spanned vector space. In the second part, we deal with hyperbolic norms which satisfy a polarization identity and are defined on cones over the real numbers. We show that, under reasonable assumptions, such hyperbolic norms induce a Lorentzian inner product on the spanned vector space. Finally, we establish a link between completeness under the Wick rotation of a Lorentzian inner product and order-theoretic completeness.
Functional Analysis.comment: 25 pages, to appear in Monatshefte Math

Functional Analysis.title: Variational relaxation and gradient flows for degenerate elliptic conductivity problems
Functional Analysis.summary: We develop a convex-analytic $L^2$-framework for gradient flows of pumping-energy functionals coupled with elliptic state equations and an evolving nonnegative conductivity $a\geq 0$. The main difficulty is that the conductivity may be merely square-integrable, or degenerate, and formal differentiation need not produce an $L^2$-subgradient. After imposing the strictly positive lower cutoff $r+a\geq r>0$, we define the pumping-energy functional by a variational formula, prove convexity and lower semicontinuity, and show that its $L^2$-subdifferential is nonempty if and only if the pressure gradient belongs to $L^4$. We also obtain a unique maximal-monotone $L^2$-gradient flow satisfying an energy identity. Moreover, we prove Mosco convergence of the pumping-energy functionals as the cutoff vanishes. An inverse-moment conductivity constraint provides a weak alternative to a uniform positive lower bound. For nonlinear laws $a=μ(b)$, primal and flux representations distinguish two complementary regimes. If $μ$ is concave, the pumping-energy functional remains convex, and we characterize its $L^2$-subdifferential and the induced gradient flow. If $1/μ$ is concave, the pumping-energy functional is concave, and therefore its negative is convex. We construct its pointwise gradient flow on a uniformly elliptic box. Admissible stationary points for power laws yield $p$-Laplacian equations with $p>2$ and $1 < p < 2$, respectively.

Functional Analysis.title: Geometric Properties of Variable Mixed Lebesgue-Sequence Spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We investigate the geometric properties of the variable mixed Lebesgue sequence space \(\ell^{q(\cdot)}(L^{p(\cdot)})\). Assuming that \(q_->1\), \(p_+<\infty\), and \(q(\cdot)\le p(\cdot)\) almost everywhere, we prove that both \(\ell^{q(\cdot)}(L^{p(\cdot)})\) and its dual space are strictly convex and smooth. Moreover, we establish that \(\ell^{q(\cdot)}(L^{p(\cdot)})\) is uniformly convex under these assumptions. We further show that the condition \(q_->1\) is sharp: when \(q_-=1\), the space fails to be uniformly convex, and its modular is not uniformly convex either. Finally, we apply these geometric results to the renormability of the associated variable-exponent Besov space \(B_{p(\cdot),q(\cdot)}^{α(\cdot)}\).
Functional Analysis.comment: Revised version. The abstract and introduction have been revised, and the presentation of the main results has been improved

Analysis of PDEs.title: Optimal tradeoffs between variance and sensitivity, via Hellinger-Kantorovich geometry
Analysis of PDEs.summary: While the goal of classical statistical theory is to minimize the variance of unbiased estimators, an additional goal of some recent research is to minimize or constrain other notions of the instability of estimators. In particular, a subset of the authors recently introduced a notion of instability termed "sensitivity", which represents the expected amount that an estimator would change if its inputs were infinitesimally perturbed. In this work, we study the multiobjective problem of minimizing both the variance and sensitivity over unbiased estimators in a given statistical model, and we aim to determine Pareto optimal tradeoffs between these two objectives. Our main results show that the Pareto front for these tradeoffs is precisely determined by endowing the statistical model with the Hellinger-Kantorovich geometry, which interpolates between the Hellinger and Wasserstein geometries that are known to be associated, respectively, with the separate minimization of variance and sensitivity. We also develop a $Z$-estimation technique which constructs estimators that asymptotically achieve Pareto optimal pairs of variance and sensitivity. While computing the Pareto front and constructing the resulting estimators in practice requires solving a continuum of partial differential equations, we fully execute this program in some parametric examples of interest where the analysis is already non-trivial. Our results also shed light on some classical statistical problems, for example by showing that the maximum likelihood estimator achieves the smallest asymptotic sensitivity among all estimators achieving the optimal asymptotic variance.

Analysis of PDEs.title: $C^{1,α}$ and $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ regularity for the $2$-Hessian equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, for every $\varepsilon>0$, we establish interior and global a priori $C^{1,α}$ estimates for some $α\in(0,1)$ from $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ bounds for bounded smooth $2$-admissible solutions of the $2$-Hessian equation, with the interior estimate requiring only an upper bound on the density. Under positive upper and lower density bounds, we prove global $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ estimates for some $\varepsilon>0$ on bounded strictly mean convex $C^{2,β}$ domains with $C^{2,β}$ boundary values. For densities bounded above and below by positive constants, the interior $C^{1,α}$ estimate follows by combining the first result with an interior $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ estimate obtained by a slight modification of an existing argument. Combining the first result with the global $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ estimate yields the global $C^{1,α}$ estimate. Known examples show that the $C^{2,β}$ regularity assumptions on the boundary and boundary values are optimal in the Hölder scale for both the global $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ estimate and the global $C^{1,α}$ estimate.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Nonabelian Higgs fields from minimal submanifolds
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Yang-Mills-Higgs fields on a broad class of noncompact Riemannian manifolds, concentrating in the large-mass limit along prescribed nondegenerate minimal submanifolds of codimension three. The solutions have uniformly bounded rescaled energy. On closed manifolds with $b_1(M)=0$, adding a suitably scaled Higgs potential gives an analogous concentration result. Our construction completes one direction of the correspondence proposed by Parise, Pigati and Stern, realising prescribed minimal submanifolds of codimension three as concentration sets of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Yang--Mills--Higgs fields.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Characteristic gluing to extremal Kerr horizons and the third law of black hole thermodynamics in vacuum
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We prove a non-perturbative, non-axisymmetric characteristic gluing theorem for the Einstein vacuum equations: every Boyer-Lindquist sphere in the domain of outer communication of a Kerr black hole, in particular every symmetry sphere of a Schwarzschild exterior, can be glued along a single outgoing null hypersurface to a horizon sphere of an extremal Kerr black hole of sufficiently large mass. The gluing is exact at both ends and matches the full sphere data, including the transversal curvature. This proves a conjecture of Kehle and Unger in the extremal case. We first raise the angular momentum to the extremal value by rotating shear pulses of non-axisymmetric gravitational radiation, and then damp the incoming data exponentially along a long non-expanding neck. At the degenerate target horizon we invert the linearised problem at all angular frequencies, using a factorisation of a fourth-order angular operator into an angular Teukolsky-Starobinsky product.
  As an application, we construct one-ended asymptotically flat vacuum initial data whose maximal development contains an exactly Schwarzschild apparent horizon and, at a later advanced time, an exactly extremal Kerr event horizon. This is the first rigorous counterexample to the third law of black hole thermodynamics in vacuum, and proves a second conjecture of Kehle and Unger.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Morse index characterization of the Veronese projective plane
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Following Simons' seminal work in 1968, every closed, connected, embedded minimal surface in the four-sphere that is not totally geodesic has Morse index at least five. In this paper, we prove that equality holds if and only if the surface is congruent to the Veronese projective plane. Relying on recent advances by Bernstein and Ketover, this characterization settles Kusner's 1996 conjecture on the minimizers of the Willmore functional in dimension four for surfaces whose normal bundle has nonzero Euler number. This is always the case, in particular, for embeddings of nonorientable surfaces whose orientation double cover has even genus.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Parabolic Rectifiable Reifenberg for Measures
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We announce a structure theory for measures on $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ equipped with the parabolic distance. Our results include a parabolic rectifiable Reifenberg theorem for arbitrary Radon measures, qualitative and quantitative characterizations of regular parabolic rectifiability by Jones square functions, and sharp results for $L^p$ beta numbers. The results hold in every parabolic dimension and extend the theories of Edelen--Naber--Valtorta, Azzam--Tolsa and David--Semmes to space-time. The stated theorems and corollaries, together with their proofs, are formalized in Lean~4 with Mathlib.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Comments are welcome. 15 pages, 7 figures, link to a github repository for formalization

Analysis of PDEs.title: Continuous Data Assimilation for Memristive FitzHugh--Nagumo Neural Networks
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this study, we investigate continuous data assimilation for a class of partly diffusive FitzHugh--Nagumo neural networks with memristive feedback and linear synaptic coupling. The nudging algorithm implemented here only adds a feedback term to the membrane-potential equations, while the recovery and memductance variables remain unobserved. We obtain weighted energy estimates that give sufficient conditions for exponential convergence of the data-assimilated solution to the reference solution under full or coarse membrane potential observations. Moreover, we prove energy-class uniqueness in dimensions one and two. In dimension three, the uniqueness criterion is an \(L^4\) membrane-potential initial data. We also establish an observational-noise estimate for locally square-integrable forcing, yielding an asymptotic error bound when the noise energy is eventually bounded.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The generic structure of the singular set in the Stefan problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We show that, in every space dimension $n\ge2$, the singular set $Σ$ of a generic (in the Baire-category sense) solution of the Stefan problem is countably parabolically $(n-2)$-rectifiable. In particular, $\dim_{\mathrm{par}}(Σ)\le n-2$. This is achieved by proving the following sharp result: in every space dimension, points of the maximal stratum of a generic solution are discrete in space-time.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the Nash equilibrium for a model of traffic flow
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
The paper consider a conservation law model of traffic flow on a highway, where each driver chooses an optimal departure time $τ^d$, based on a departure cost $\varphi(τ^d)$ and an arrival cost $ψ(τ^a)$. Nash equilibria are studied, where no driver can reduce his own cost by changing his departure time.
  The first results provide continuity estimates on the arrival time, depending on the distribution of departures. In terms of the ${\bf L}^1$ distance, we show that the corresponding map is Hölder continuous with exponent $1/2$ in Lagrangian variables (labelling individual drivers), and Lipschitz continuous in Eulerian space variables.
  Concerning the regularity of the a Nash equilibrium, our results show that, when the total number of drivers is sufficiently large, a queue alway forms at the entrance of the highway and the corresponding traffic density contains a shock. Moreover, for any number of drivers (possibly small), we prove that for generic $\mathcal C^2$ cost functions $\varphi, ψ$ the Nash equilibrium solution still contains a shock.
  In the last section of the paper, assuming that the initial departure rate is not a Nash equilibrium, we consider an evolution equation for the departure rate, where each driver keeps changing his daily departure time in order to reduce his own cost. It is proved that this nonlocal integro-differential evolution equation admits a unique solution, globally in time. This provides some theoretical support to earlier numerical simulations, which indicated the dynamic instability of the Nash equilibrium and the possible existence of a chaotic attractor.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Keywords: Conservation laws, shocks, Nash equilibrium, integro-differential evolution equation

Analysis of PDEs.title: Traveling Waves for Mixed Nonlocal-Local Systems of Conservation Laws on $\mathbb{S}^1$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Non trivial traveling waves in genuinely nonlinear conservation laws hardly appear and, in some cases, scalar nonlocal conservation laws inherit this feature. Here, we show that mixed nonlocal-local systems of conservation laws display a far richer scenario. A variety of traveling waves may exist, different components may travel with different speeds and traveling waves can appear as time-asymptotic limits. Technically, these results need a significant extension of Dafermos' "trend to steady state" theory, exploiting properties of Hamiltonian systems solved by generalized characteristics.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The estimates for Boolean surface area of polynomial threshold functions
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
Polynomial threshold functions (PTFs) are an important low-complexity class of Boolean functions, with strong connections to learning theory and approximation theory. Recent work on learning and testing PTFs has exploited structural and isoperimetric properties of the class, especially bounds on average sensitivity, one of the central themes in the study of PTFs since the Gotsman--Linial conjecture recently solved by OpenAI, \cite{GLsol}.
  In this work we study PTFs through the lens of the Boolean surface area (or Talagrand boundary) \[ \mathbf{BSA}[f]=\mathbb{E}|\nabla f|=\mathbb{E}\sqrt{s_{f}(x)}, \] a natural measure of vertex-boundary complexity on the discrete cube. Our main result is that every degree-$d$ PTF has polylogarithmic Boolean surface area: \[ \mathbf{BSA}[f]\le C_d(\log(en))^{C_d}. \] The proof is based on the PTF Restriction Lemma of Kabanets, Kane, and Lu \cite{KKL2017} and proceeds through a tail bound for the pointwise sensitivity. In particular, it controls all subcritical fractional moments of the sensitivity. We also record a random block partition principle for Boolean surface area and an alternative recursive argument following Kane's work \cite{DK} on average sensitivity, which independently yields the second bound \[ \mathbf{BSA}[f]\le \exp(C(d)\sqrt{\log n}). \] This bound was obtained in \cite{FSVZ} without clarifying the magnitude of $C(d)$, which we do below. For lower moments $\bE |\nabla f|^η \le C(d, η)$ there is no dependence on $n$ for $0<η<1$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Existence and uniqueness of solutions for a random PDE-ODE model describing glioma invasion and radiotherapy
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study a stochastic model for the growth and invasion of glioma cells in the anisotropic brain tissue, also incorporating effects of radiotherapeutic interventions and associated uncertainties. The PDE-ODE model couples glioma and healthy tissue dynamics in a nonlinear manner and explicitly includes treatment-related stochasticity through random depletion terms. The macroscopic system has been obtained by an upscaling procedure from a microscopic description in [1]. We prove the existence and uniqueness of local strong solutions to the corresponding stochastic system. The analysis addresses challenges arising from the nonlinear coupling, anisotropic diffusion, taxis mechanisms, and stochastic treatment effects, providing a first rigorous step toward the mathematical understanding of stochastic continuum models for glioma invasion and therapy response.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A heterogeneous nonlocal advection--diffusion system
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We present a self-contained investigation of the local and global well-posedness of a system of nonlocal advection--diffusion equations for a heterogeneous population over $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d \in \mathbb{N}$. Each convolution kernel $K_{ij}$, which describes the nonlocal advection of species $i$ according to the distribution of species $j$, is assumed to have its own regularity $\nabla K_{ij} \in L^{q_{ij}}(\mathbb{R}^d)$, $1 < q_{ij} < \infty$. Local well-posedness of the mild solution and its regularity is obtained using semigroup theory and contraction mapping arguments. For kernels that satisfy a given interaction cycle condition, global existence is established using a Nash-type inequality to show an \textit{a priori} energy bound. For a class of kernels that need not satisfy the interaction cycle condition, a dynamical property satisfied by a normalised \(L^p\) norm of each species is used to obtain a uniform-in-time bound under a smallness condition on the initial data. An example family of kernels with varying regularities, supplemented by numerical simulations, is then considered to illustrate the theory developed in this work and how it may be generalised.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Invariant measures for the one-dimensional stochastic Navier-Stokes-Korteweg equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate the long-time behaviour of a one-dimensional compressible viscous fluid with general capillarity and density dependent viscosity, driven by a stochastic force. In particular, we prove the existence of invariant measures by applying the Krylov-Bogoliubov method in a setting where the dynamics is supported on a non-complete phase space. This analysis is further enhanced by the derivation of a refined stability result determining the continuous dependence with respect to the initial data. The present paper exhibits some properties and results for Korteweg fluids which are not known in absence of the capillarity tensor. In particular, we prove that the Markov semigroup associated with strong solutions is Feller and we can consider ranges of the adiabatic and viscosity exponents $γ$ and $α$ larger than those available in the current ergodic literature for compressible fluids. Also the interplay between the choice of the physical domain and the use of a damping term is discussed.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Unconditional scattering below the ground state for the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical generalized Hartree equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Unconditional global existence and scattering are established for the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical generalized Hartree equation with $0<α<3$, below the ground-state energy and kinetic thresholds. The initial data lie in $\dot H^1$, with no radial symmetry, finite-mass, or finite-variance assumption. Annular frequency estimates and Gaussian interaction estimates rule out a compact critical trajectory by first controlling its nonlinear forcing and then recovering its conserved mass.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp volume tests and entropy thresholds for quasilinear elliptic inequalities with gradient reactions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate positive weak solutions of $-Δ_m u\ge u^p|\nabla u|^q$ on complete noncompact Riemannian manifolds without curvature, volume doubling, or Poincaré assumptions. For the superhomogeneous mixed reaction we derive a curvature-free integral volume test by combining two first-order estimates with a recurrence for the mass of a \emph{fixed} density. The same approach organizes the pure-gradient and capacity criteria and yields sharp finite hierarchies of iterated-logarithmic growth bounds, with counterexamples on smooth model manifolds. In the subhomogeneous region, vanishing lower growth of $\log V(R)/R^{m-q}$ forces the Liouville property. On the homogeneous line $p+q=m-1$, we obtain the optimal strict lower-volume-entropy threshold $(p+1)((m-1)/p)^{p/(p+1)}$ for $p>0$ (and $1$ for $p=0$), together with examples at equality. The existing six-region classification is not claimed as new; the advances concern refined volume hypotheses and their model sharpness. The tests remain valid for smooth weighted measures and for locally bounded positive Sobolev solutions. Sharpness is understood within the stated model families; no characterization from volume alone on an individual manifold is asserted.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Abstract second-order boundary control systems
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Many physical systems, such as vibrating elastic bodies, acoustic media and electromagnetic fields, are governed by second-order evolution equations $\ddot x+D\dot x+Sx=0$ and interact with their environment through their boundary. The classical analysis via the operator matrix $\mathcal{A}=\left[\begin{smallmatrix}0&I\\-S&-D\end{smallmatrix}\right]$ requires $S$ to be self-adjoint, which typically fixes a boundary condition a priori and thus excludes boundary control. We therefore use $S$ only to define the energy space and govern the dynamics by a maximal operator $S_{\max}\supset S$ whose domain carries no boundary condition. Based on a factorization $S=A^*A$, we construct a boundary triplet for the associated operator matrix and define boundary inputs and outputs of Robin type, parametrized by an operator $P$ on the boundary space. We show that the resulting system is impedance passive and internally well-posed if $P$ is a contraction, and that for $D=0$ this covers all boundary conditions under which the free dynamics generate a contraction semigroup. Moreover, we show that the position-momentum formulation (e.g., $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}0&I\\Δ&0\end{smallmatrix}\right]$ for the wave equation) and the strain-momentum formulation (e.g., $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}0&\nabla\\\operatorname{div}&0\end{smallmatrix}\right]$) describe the same open system, including its boundary inputs and outputs. We illustrate our results by an $n$-dimensional wave equation and Maxwell's equations.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Index and nullity of critical spherical catenoids in hyperbolic three-space
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that every critical spherical catenoid in a geodesic ball of hyperbolic three-space has Morse index four and nullity two. This resolves Medvedev's index conjecture throughout the parameter range of the catenoid family. The kernel consists precisely of the normal components of rotations that preserve the center of the ball and tilt the axis of the catenoid. As a consequence, the radius of the supporting ball increases strictly along the family. The proof combines a global boundary inequality obtained from a Wronskian, a positive Dirichlet eigenfunction supplied by the time component of the unit normal, and a Riccati comparison for the angular mode $k=2$. A ground-state identity then yields positivity of every angular mode $k\ge2$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Asymptotic observable symmetry for spacetime observability of waves II: Smooth bounded domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Continuing \cite{NWX} and Part I \cite{AOSI}, we further investigate symmetry for spacetime observability of wave equations. Building on asymptotic observable symmetry (AOS) introduced in \cite{AOSI}, we study symmetry under glancing propagation and caustics. We prove that, on every smooth bounded domain in $\R^2$ and for every positive observation time, there is a fixed measurable set satisfying the essential spacetime measurable geometric control condition. However, the observability inequality fails on this set.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Boundedness and continuity of phase-corrected gradients on Sobolev spaces
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
For a function $ψ: \mathbb{R}^d ightarrow \mathbb{C}$, we define the phase-corrected gradient $
abla_{\!\circ} ψ= |ψ|^{-1} \overlineψ\,
ablaψ$ and study the regularity of the map $ψ\mapsto 
abla_{\!\circ} ψ$ on Sobolev spaces. Since $\mathrm{Re}[
abla_{\!\circ} ψ] = 
abla |ψ|$, the phase-corrected gradient fits naturally into the framework of nonlinear composition operators. Its imaginary part $Λ= \mathrm{Im}[
abla_{\!\circ} ψ]$, on the other hand, plays a key role in quantum hydrodynamic models. We prove that $ψ\mapsto 
abla_{\!\circ} ψ$ is bounded and continuous from $W^{s,2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to $W^{s-1,2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for $1 \leq s <  rac32$, and we show that the threshold $s =  rac32$ is sharp. In particular, this answers an open question concerning the continuity of the map $ψ\mapsto |ψ|$ on Sobolev spaces. We also show that our results remain valid for functions that do not necessarily decay at infinity, a relevant setting in the context of Ginzburg--Landau theory. Finally, we extend our analysis to more general phase-corrected gradients of the form $f(|ψ|^{-1} ψ) 
abla ψ$, where $f: \mathbb{S}^1 ightarrow \mathbb{C}$ is Lipschitz, and discuss implications for certain parabolic PDEs.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Gradient estimates and Liouville theorems for exponentially harmonic functions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study exponentially harmonic functions on complete Riemannian manifolds. Under a lower Ricci curvature bound \(\Ric_g\geq-Kg\), we first establish a local gradient estimate in terms of the oscillation. We then prove a pointwise gradient estimate for solutions bounded from one side. As an application, when \(\Ric_g\geq0\), we obtain a Liouville theorem under a one-sided sublinear growth condition. In particular, every exponentially harmonic function bounded above or below is constant.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Liouville Theorem for the Real k-Hessian Equation with a One-Sided Growth Condition
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We establish a scale-invariant interior $C^2$ estimate for smooth solutions of the real $k$-Hessian equation. As an application, we prove that every smooth entire solution of $σ_k(D^2u)=1$ satisfying $u(x)\ge b|x|^2-B$ for some constants $b,B$ with $b>0$ is a quadratic polynomial. For smooth solutions, admissibility is forced by the growth condition.
  The results also hold for viscosity solutions and for weak solutions in Trudinger's sense. Admissibility is required in the latter case.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Local Algebraic Stability of Wasserstein Gradient Descent-Ascent and Mean Field Langevin Dynamics without Spectral Gap
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the local stability of Wasserstein gradient descent-ascent (GDA) for entropy regularized two-player zero-sum games on noncompact domains. When one or both equilibrium measures fail to satisfy a Poincaré inequality, the spectral gap arguments underlying local exponential convergence are unavailable. we show that Wasserstein GDA converges algebraically to the mixed Nash equilibrium in chi-squared divergence, provided the initial relative density is a small perturbation in $L^2$ with bounded algebraic moments. The proof has two main ingredients: a cancellation in a negative Sobolev energy estimate, and a bootstrap argument that keeps the moments bounded uniformly in time. For polynomial-tailed equilibria, we construct perturbations supported far out in the tails that survive over diffusive time scales, which gives algebraic lower bounds on the worst-case relaxation rate. We also establish analogous local algebraic stability and lower bound results for mean-field Langevin dynamics, when the equilibrium fails to satisfy a spectral gap.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Variational properties of Perron's extremal solutions in the Bernoulli one-phase problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the Perron extremal solutions of the stationary one-phase Bernoulli problem. These solutions are important in several applications, but not much is known about the regularity of their free boundaries due to their non-variational construction. We show that, in fact, Perron extremal solutions retain some variational features; specifically, they are solutions in the sense of inner variations. We establish this property by showing that extremal solutions arise as infinite-time limits of monotone solutions of the parabolic Bernoulli problem. As a consequence, we are able to describe the structure of singularities for Perron extremal solutions in two dimensions: largest subsolutions have smooth free boundaries, while smallest supersolutions have free boundary points that are either smooth, or whose blow-up limits are two-plane wedges with equal slope.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Thermosolutal Marangoni instabilities in a weakly viscoelastic falling film with soluble surfactant
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We examine the linear stability and nonlinear evolution of a heated falling film containing a soluble surfactant and a weakly viscoelastic liquid. The stress response is described by the short-memory Walters model, while surface tension depends on temperature and surface concentration. An Orr--Sommerfeld analysis and its long-wave limit determine how elastic memory and the two Marangoni stresses enter the instability threshold. A five-field weighted-residual model is then derived to describe finite-amplitude disturbances. The bulk and surface transport equations are written with compatible fluxes, which conserve their combined projected surfactant inventory in a periodic domain. The numerical examples show that solutal Marangoni stress suppresses disturbance growth and reduces the amplitude of the nonlinear waves. Thermal Marangoni stress increases the maximum growth rate, although its effect on the width of the unstable wavenumber band is different. Elastic memory changes both the onset and the finite-wavelength response. The nonlinear profiles develop a main hump and capillary ripples, accompanied by variations in bulk concentration, surface concentration, and interfacial temperature. These results describe the competition between thermocapillary forcing, surfactant redistribution and elastic stress within the retained long-wave model. The larger elastic parameters are interpreted as formal predictions of the truncated constitutive equations, rather than as a controlled extension to strongly elastic flow.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Differentiability and Convexity of the Solution Maps for Fully Non-linear Parabolic HJB Equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the dependence on the terminal condition of solutions to a fully nonlinear parabolic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) equation, when the terminal condition varies along a finite-dimensional family. This problem is motivated by a dual formulation of semimartingale optimal transport. The equation is posed as a terminal-value Cauchy problem on an unbounded spatial domain. Under structural ellipticity and regularity assumptions on the nonlinear operator, we recall local parabolic Hölder estimates and stability results for bounded uniformly continuous terminal data. We then establish continuous directional differentiability of the solution map with respect to the finite-dimensional parameter, and identify its derivative through the corresponding linearized Cauchy problem. Under an additional convexity assumption on the Hamiltonian and a non-degeneracy condition on the terminal data, we prove local strong convexity of the point-evaluated solution map. The analysis relies on Evans--Krylov theory for fully nonlinear parabolic equations and combines PDE arguments with probabilistic representations. Finally, we extend the differentiability and convexity results to cascades of Cauchy problems in which successive equations are coupled through terminal conditions at several prescribed times. This structure is motivated, for instance, by optimal transport problems with marginal constraints imposed at several maturities.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Extremal Trudinger-Moser inequality associated with many point vortices with multi-intensities
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the boundedness of extremal 2D Trudinger-Moser inequality associated with many point vortices with multi-intensities. Sufficient conditions for continuously-distributed measures are given in one-sided and two-sided cases.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The divergence of continuously differentiable vector fields
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For $m\geq 2$, we give a complete characterisation of the continuous functions on $\mathbb{R}^m$ that are divergences of continuously differentiable vector fields. The characterisation is formulated in terms of distributions and, equivalently, in terms of the continuous dual of a suitably topologised subspace of the Arens--Eells space. The two implications yield contrasting applications. First, there exists a compactly supported continuous function which is the divergence of a bounded Lipschitz vector field but not of any continuously differentiable vector field. Second, every continuous function whose distributional partial derivatives are locally $m$-integrable (the critical exponent for Sobolev embedding) is the divergence of a continuously differentiable vector field.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Numerical study of the 2D Kaup-Broer-Kuperschmidt Boussinesq system
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this work we consider the well posed version of the Kaup-Broer-Kuperschmidt system in two dimensions. We numerically construct soliton type solutions and show that they are unstable both against dispersion and singularity formation.
