Further, we study line solitons and their stability, as well as generally localised initial data. In either case we fail to find stable structures.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Boundary Layer Criterion for the Low Mach Number and Inviscid Limits in Compressible Fluid-Rigid Body Interaction
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate the simultaneous low Mach number and vanishing viscosity limit for a three-dimensional compressible viscous fluid interacting with a freely moving rigid body. The fluid satisfies the compressible Navier-Stokes equations and the no-slip condition on the body surface, while the body evolves according to Newton's laws driven by the fluid stresses. We establish convergence of finite-energy weak solutions to a strong solution of the corresponding incompressible Euler-rigid body system on its interval of existence. Assuming that the initial relative energy tends to zero, convergence holds under a Kato-type condition in a boundary layer whose thickness is proportional to the viscosity. This condition combines vanishing viscous dissipation with a weighted estimate on the fluid momentum relative to the rigid body motion. The proof uses the relative entropy method and a boundary layer corrector adapted to the fluid-rigid body coupling, providing a sufficient condition for convergence in relative energy as the Mach number and viscosity tend to zero simultaneously.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The role of density in phase transitions and new perspectives on theta functions
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
Let $z\in \mathbb{H}:=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:\Im(z)>0\}$ and $Λ:=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\Im(z)}}\big({\mathbb Z}\oplus z{\mathbb Z}\big)$, and set $
θ(α;z):=θ(α;Λ)=\sum_{(m,n)\in\mathbb{Z}^2}e^{-πα\frac{|m+nz|^2}{\Im(z)}}. $
We study the minimization of the functional $θ(α;z)-bθ(2α;z)$ and establish a complete phase diagram for all $α>0$ and $b\in(0,\sqrt{2})$. For $0<b<\sqrt{2}$, an explicit threshold $b_1=0.0767767081\cdots\in(0,1/10)$ separates two distinct types of phase transitions.
  Type I: $0<b<b_1$: it admits a type of ``hexagonal--rhombic--square--rectangular'' phase transition.
  Type II: $b_1\le b<\sqrt{2}$: it admits a type of ``hexagonal--square--rectangular'' phase transition, without passing through the rhombic lattices.
  These phase transitions contrast with Montgomery's theorem \cite{Mon1988}, where the hexagonal lattice minimizes the single theta function at all scales, and the recent Bétermin-Faulhuber-Steinerberger theorem \cite{BFS2026} for translated Gaussian lattice sums, where the hexagonal lattice prevails in a min-max structure. In our setting, the density parameter $α$ governs the sequence of optimal lattice shapes, while the competition parameter $b$ controls the emergence of the rhombic phase, which exists for $b<b_1$ and vanishes for $b\ge b_1$.
  As an application, we resolve Bétermin's conjecture \cite{Betermin2021AHP}. Bétermin predicted a Type I phase transition for the functional $θ(α;z)-(1/10)θ(2α;z)$ with $b=1/10$. We instead rigorously establish that no rhombic lattice is a global minimizer at any density and prove that the system undergoes a Type II phase transition, thereby settling the conjecture in corrected form.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Log-Concavity and Fundamental Gaps on Complex Projective Domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove quantitative log-concavity and fundamental-gap estimates for Dirichlet Schrödinger operators on complex projective domains. With holomorphic sectional curvature four, the boundary condition $\mathrm{II}\ge\sqrt{44/5}\,g$ suffices in every complex dimension under $\operatorname{Hess} V\ge2|\nabla V|g$ and $\operatorname{osc}V\le4n$. It yields $\operatorname{Hess}(-\logφ_1)>g$ and $λ_2-λ_1>\max\{n+2+\sqrt{n^2+5n+11},\,2n+14/3\}$. The main difficulty is to control the distinguished Hopf direction together with a transverse Hessian block whose dimension grows with $n$. We extend modified-Hessian first-contact arguments by retaining the Hopf term and using longitudinal and transverse rotational tests. A trace minimization reduces all gradient orientations to three extreme directions. A dimension-scaled logarithmic barrier then compares their contact costs with a single limiting profile. A radial spectral estimate supplies the required quadratic-in-dimension spectral threshold from a dimension-independent boundary curvature bound. For $n\ge3$ these are, to our knowledge, the first log-concavity estimates for domains in $\mathbb{CP}^n$ without symmetry assumptions. We also prove a sharp diameter bound and Hessian levels linear in $n$ under larger dimension-free curvature bounds.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Gevrey Regularity for a Sum of Two Squares in Two Variables
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the Gevrey hypoellipticity of a sum of two squares in two variables, satisfying the Hörmander hypothesis, assuming that the function, $ q $, describing (the space projection of) its characteristic variety vanishes only at a single point, which can be assumed to be the origin. A hypoellipticity result is given in a Gevrey class, depending on $ q $. In some examples the found regularity is known to be optimal.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Quantitative approximation theorem of neural operators for the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study neural operators for the Dirichet-to-Neumann map (DN map), which is encountered in the famous Calderón's problem. In many numerical methods used for reconstructing the unknown conductivity from the knowledge of the DN map need to evaluate the corresponding DN map at a given conductivity function, which involves solving the boundary value problem for the conductivity equation and taking the Neumann data. Such procedure is time consuming and not effective. Hence, it is a favorable strategy to construct a surrogate to replace the forward map mapping conductivity functions to corresponding DN maps. The main theme of this paper is to derive quantitative bounds on the parametric complexity of these neural operators. In particular, under suitable assumptions, their depth grows at most logarithmically with $\varepsilon^{-1}$, while the relevant spectral and projection ranks grow algebraically. It should be noted that general neural operators suffer from "the curse of parametric dimensionality". This work demonstrates the construction of neural operators for the DN map that does not suffer from such curse.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Periodic dynamics of transonic shocks in Euler-Poisson flows
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper studies the existence and dynamical stability of time-periodic transonic shock solutions to the one-dimensional Euler--Poisson equations under periodic boundary perturbations. The analysis relies on two key mechanisms: the structural dissipation induced by the transonic shock and the stabilization effect of the positive electric field on the shock position. Using a reformulation of the Rankine-Hugoniot conditions and uniform estimates on the flow and shock perturbations, we establish the existence of a time-periodic transonic shock solution. We further prove its dynamical stability under small perturbations of the initial data.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Improved well-posedness for the limit flow of differentiation of roots of polynomials
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study the partial differential equation on the circle that was heuristically obtained by Steinerberger \cite{steinerberger2019nonlocal} on the real line and which represents the evolution of the density of the roots of polynomials under differentiation. After integrating the partial differential equation in question, we observe that it can be treated with the theory of viscosity solutions. This equation at hand is a non linear parabolic integro-differential equation which involves the elliptic operator called the half-Laplacian. Due to the singularity of the equation, we first restrict our study to strictly positive initial condition. We obtain a comparison principle for solutions of the primitive equation which yields uniqueness, existence, continuity with respect to initial condition. We then extend these results to general initial data. We finally prove that the system of particles on the circle introduced by Steinerberger indeed approximates the solution of the equation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The quermassintegral inequalities for k-convex spiral-star-shaped domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We extend the quermassintegral inequalities of our earlier work \cite{GuanLi2009} from star-shaped domains to a substantially broader class of domains in Euclidean space, which we call spiral-star-shaped. A smooth domain is spiral-star-shaped if its boundary satisfies \[
  \langle X+A X,ν\rangle>0 \] for some fixed skew-symmetric linear map $ A$, where $X$ is the position vector and $ν$ is the outward unit normal. The vector field $X+A X$ is conformal Killing, with dilation component $X$ and rotational component $A X$; its trajectories combine expansion and rotation, giving rise to the spiral terminology. When $A=0$, it reduces to ordinary star-shapedness, while nonzero $A$ allows domains that are not star-shaped in the usual radial sense.
  For smooth $k$-convex spiral-star-shaped domains, we prove long-time existence and exponential convergence to a round sphere for a locally constrained inverse curvature flow. The positive spiral support function provides the geometric control needed to treat initial hypersurfaces that need not be star-shaped in the usual sense. Monotonicity of the quermassintegrals along the flow yields sharp quermassintegral inequalities in this enlarged class, with equality if and only if the domain is a ball.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The metastability phenomen for a radiative gas model
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the time-asymptotic behaviour of solutions to a singular perturbation of the inviscid Burgers problem describing sound propagation in a radiating gas. This radiating gas model exhibits the interesting phenomenon known as metastability that has been first identified for the viscous Burgers equation. Precisely, on an initial time span, that scales linearly in the inverse of the perturbation parameter, we can quantify the L1-distance of the solution to the so-called sharp N-wave solution of the inviscid Burgers problem and to a diffusive N-wave. On a second long-time stage that scales exponentially in the inverse of the perturbation parameter, the solutions still remain close to a diffusive N-wave before finally collapsing into diffusion waves. Besides our analysis of the radiating gas model, we also provide an alternative description of metastability in the viscous Burgers model which, unlike other studies, relies on L1-estimates and does not require the passage to similarity variables.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Determinants of Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on Constant Curvature Surfaces with Geodesic Polygonal Boundary
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We express the zeta regularized determinants of the Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on compact Riemann surfaces with constant curvature metrics and geodesic polygonal boundary in terms of the Laplacian determinant on their closed conical doubles. The formulae apply without restrictions on the genus or number of boundary components. They involve explicit corner angle factors and a quotient of the Reidemeister and $L^2$ norms on the determinant line of cohomology. The proof combines a relative BFK gluing formula with the comparison theorem for analytic and combinatorial torsion on manifolds with boundary, due to Lück and Vishik. As an application, we give a rigorous proof of the Aurell-Salomonson formula for Euclidean polygons. We also obtain explicit determinants for spherical and hyperbolic triangles and certain other geodesic polygons from known formulae for their doubles.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Ground states for Brezis-Nirenberg-type fractional elliptic systems with sublinear absorption and subcritical perturbation
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
This paper addresses the non-local fractional counterpart of the Laplace equation involving critical nonlinearities, a famous problem originally investigated by Brezis and Nirenberg in [Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 36(4) (1983), pp. 437--477]. We study a class of fractional elliptic systems and equations with critical exponents, sublinear absorption, subcritical perturbation, and general noncoercive frequency parameters. The work is carried out both within a general framework involving non-local integrodifferential operators and in specific concrete models.
  Our results extend and complement the existing literature on critical fractional elliptic problems in several directions: (1) we include sublinear absorption together with a subcritical perturbation, so that the overall nonlinearity is not superlinear at zero; (2) we provide two types of concrete verification of the energy threshold condition in the presence of the critical term, the sublinear absorption, and the subcritical perturbation, whereas the existing verifications are restricted to the pure critical case; (3) we obtain ground state solutions for coupled systems, not merely nontrivial solutions for scalar equations; (4) we allow a general noncoercive range of frequency parameters, including negative values.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Two improved Liouville-type theorems for the 3D stationary tropical climate model without temperature assumptions
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
In this paper, we establish two improved Liouville-type theorems for the three-dimensional stationary tropical climate model without imposing any temperature assumptions. Compared with previous results, we achieve significant improvements on the growth assumptions imposed on $u$, $v$ and $
abla v$. Owing to the special structure inherent to the equations, we fully exploit the $L^2$-estimate for the oscillation of the temperature, refined interpolation techniques and an iteration argument to establish a Liouville-type theorem under flexible and relaxed power-law growth conditions. As an interesting consequence, we obtain the triviality of solutions under the integrability conditions imposed only on $(u,
abla v)$ or $(
abla u,
abla v)$. Furthermore, by developing a systematic framework to handle the energy function associated with the non-trivial solutions and with the aid of delicate ODE analysis and a contradiction argument, we refine our Liouville-type theorem by introducing logarithmic corrections to the growth rates.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniform Exponential Stability for Finite Energy Weak Solutions to the Barotropic Compressible Navier--Stokes Equations with Large Potential External Forces
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the large-time behavior of Lions--Feireisl finite energy weak solutions to the barotropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations in three-dimensional bounded domains with Dirichlet boundary conditions and large potential external forces. For $γ>3/2$, we prove that these weak solutions converge exponentially to the steady state as time tends to infinity, provided that the steady density is bounded away from zero. The main novelty of our analysis is a compactness argument based on Young measures. Furthermore, we prove that the Young measures generated by the density are Dirac measures. Together with the extra integrability of the density, this yields strong convergence to the nonconstant steady density and uniform smallness of the energy $w$ for sufficiently large time. We use Taylor expansion and the Bogovskii operator to construct a Lyapunov functional, and use this smallness of $w$ to obtain exponential decay with a time $T_0$, which is independent of the particular weak solution, thereby answering the question raised by Kang, Peng and Xiong in \cite[Remark~1.1]{KPX}. Corresponding decay estimates for the density, momentum, kinetic energy and the viscous dissipation integrated from large times to infinity also hold, allowing vacuum.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Quantitative Analysis of Second-Harmonic Generation in Plasmonic Nanowires: Symmetry Breaking and a Topological Defect
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper develops a quantitative theory of second-harmonic generation (SHG) in hollow plasmonic nanowires, distinguishing geometric symmetry breaking from cavity effects. We consider a centrosymmetric material with a concentric circular cavity and a slightly perturbed outer boundary. Relative to the solid nanowire in~\cite{liu2026quantitative}, the cavity introduces a topological defect by changing the cross-section from a disk to a doubly connected domain, whereas the outer-boundary perturbation breaks geometric symmetry. Local inversion-symmetry breaking at the interfaces induces nonlinear surface polarization. Using layer potentials and boundary-perturbation asymptotics, we derive explicit leading- and first-order formulas for the fundamental and second-harmonic fields. For a circular outer boundary, the leading-order second-harmonic field is purely quadrupolar; its amplitude differs from the solid-wire case by $O(γ^2)$ as $γ=r_i/r_e\to0$ and decays as $O(r_e-r_i)$ in the nonresonant thin-shell limit. For perturbations proportional to $\cos(nθ)$, $n\ge3$, the first-order second-harmonic correction contains only modes $n-2$, $n$, and $n+2$, yielding dipolar, quadrupolar, or higher-order radiation for $n=3$, $n=4$, or $n\ge5$, respectively, provided the lowest-order modal coefficient is nonzero. We derive plasmonic resonance conditions at both frequencies and estimate the singular orders of single and simultaneous resonances, including possible higher-order singularities from coincident resonance factors. Thus geometric symmetry determines the multipolar modes, whereas the cavity radius controls their amplitudes and resonant enhancement.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A theoretically exact filtered back-propagationformula for single-time wave inversion
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider single-time wave inversion, that is, recovering the initial pressure $f$ from the wave field $\mathcal{W}_T f = u(\cdot,T)$ at a single time $T$, where $u$ solves the wave equation with sound speed $c$ and initial data $(f,0)$. In two dimensions this is the main reconstruction step of full-field photoacoustic projection imaging, where each camera image is a two-dimensional wave field at a single time instant. An efficient direct method is back-propagation by the Fourier multiplier $2\cos(cT|ξ|)$. It yields exact inversion in odd dimensions but not in two. We give its error in closed form, with bounds, and derive an exact explicit filtered back-propagation $f = 2\mathcal{W}_T \mathcal{M}_K \mathcal{W}_T f$ in analogy to filtered backprojection for the Radon transform.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Numerical Method for the Fractional Semilinear Calderón Problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We present a finite element method for reconstructing a coefficient in a fractional semilinear equation from a single exterior measurement.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Regularization and Full Support for the CBO Equation with Measure Initial Data
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove global well-posedness and regularization for the isotropic consensus-based optimization equation with initial probability measures of finite fourth moment. Under suitable weight decay assumptions, after any nonconstant consensus motion, both the density and the consensus trajectory become smooth, and all spatial Sobolev norms are locally bounded in time. The proof uses a Fourier commutator estimate, localization and iteration, followed by a nonlinear time bootstrap. Counterexamples show that smoothing can fail at a stationary consensus point. For non-Dirac initial data, we also prove positivity away from the consensus point and full support at every positive time in all dimensions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Liouville Theorems for the Stationary Fractional Hall-Magnetohydrodynamic Equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper we prove Liouville-type theorems for the stationary fractional Hall-magnetohydrodynamic equations in $\mathbb R^3$. Smooth solutions vanishing at infinity, with $u\in\dot H^{α/2}$ and $b\in\dot H^{β/2}$, are trivial for $1\leα\le\frac53$, $1\leβ<2$ and $α+2β\le5$, with no additional integrability assumption. The key step is to estimate the Hall boundary term through the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension of $b$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Bach-flat metrics and global regularity of conformal structures
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study global regularity properties of conformal structures on compact manifolds with applications to conformally invariant variational problems. We find sharp conditions ensuring that a manifold equipped with a Riemannian metric of Sobolev class is conformally diffeomorphic to a smooth one. In particular, we prove that $W^{2,q}$ Bach-flat four-manifolds with $q > 2$ are smooth up to conformal diffeomorphisms. We also solve the Yamabe problem for $W^{2,q}$ metrics with $q > 2$ on three-manifolds under a mild conformal condition.

Analysis of PDEs.title: At last, an explicit singular value decomposition for electrical impedance tomography
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We derive a diagonalization of the normal operator of the linearized electrical impedance tomography (EIT) problem on the disk in the case of a radially symmetric Schrödinger potential with Dirichlet-to-Neumann data. The diagonalization is achieved by transforming the normal operator to the adjacent interval finite Hilbert transform which has a known spectral theory including a commuting differential operator. The normal operator in this case is not compact and the spectrum continuous.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the symmetric Morrey problem in three dimensions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the relations between seven generalized notions of convexity for continuous integrands in the space of symmetric $3\times 3$ matrices. Here, symmetric quasiconvexity is defined through symmetrized gradients, and symmetric rank-one convexity through symmetrized rank-one lines. We construct a symmetric quasiconvex integrand that is not polyconvex at symmetric matrices, and an integrand that is both symmetric rank-one convex and Hessian quasiconvex but not symmetric quasiconvex. We also establish a transfer principle that converts smooth rank-one convex functions that lack Hessian quasiconvexity into symmetric rank-one convex integrands while preserving this lack of of Hessian quasiconvexity. Applying this scheme to already existing counterexamples yields the existence of symmetric rank-one convex integrands that are not Hessian quasiconvex. Together with known examples, these results determine all pairwise implications among the seven notions considered here.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Instability of exact finite-amplitude acoustic-gravity waves
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Godin (\textit{J. Fluid Mech.}, vol. 767, 2015, pp. 52--64) showed that compressible fluids in a uniform gravity field support finite-amplitude incompressible wave motions, in which every parcel conserves pressure and density, and constructed exact Gerstner-type surface and edge waves, possibly carried by currents. Using the short-wavelength instability method for compressible flows, we show that these waves are linearly unstable above a critical steepness. The stability of each fluid level reduces to a Floquet problem depending on two parameters: the steepness $\mathfrak{e}=e^{ka_2}$ and $ν^2=(1-\mathfrak{e}^2)ν_0^2$, where $ν_0^2=\cos^2α\,N_0^2/Ω^2$, $N_0$ is the buoyancy frequency of the hydrostatic reference state, $α$ the inclination of the plane of motion and $Ω=(gk\cosα)^{1/2}$ the intrinsic orbital frequency. In an isentropic fluid, a level is unstable if $\mathfrak{e}>1/3$, recovering Leblanc's threshold for Gerstner waves (\textit{J. Fluid Mech.}, vol. 506, 2004, pp. 245--254) and extending it to compressible surface and edge waves; weak stable stratification lowers the threshold to $\frac13-\frac{32}{81}ν_0^2+O(ν_0^4)$. In an isothermal atmosphere, $ν_0^2=κ\cosα/(kH)$, where $H$ is the pressure scale height. For horizontal wavelengths near $5.5\,H/\cosα$, principal subharmonic resonance makes the critical steepness vanish. For the fast airglow wave observed by Hecht et al. (\textit{J. Geophys. Res.}, vol. 107, 2002, D20, 4444), which Godin interpreted with his solution, the lidar temperature places the layer in which this interpretation is consistent on this resonance, where the critical steepness is typically 0.1 instead of $1/3$. Instability is confined to a layer beneath the free surface of surface waves and to a wedge at the shoreline of edge waves.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A PDE-Based Model of Runner Flow in Mass Participation Events
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper presents a macroscopic approach for modeling pedestrian movement. A convection-diffusion partial differential equation (PDE) is described and used to model the flow of runners along a marathon course. A marathon is a good modeling case study for human movement because the location of runners is only known in sparse locations, so an accurate model is needed to know where people are at all times. As well, marathons offer many safety and logistical problems that can be solved by modeling human movement. Data is obtained from the 2023 Columbus Marathon, and model improvements are made to include a temporally varying convection term. Results show an increase in model accuracy which can allow for better resource allocation and safety measures.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 6 pages, 8 figures, 2 tables. Accepted to the 2026 Modeling, Estimation and Control Conference (MECC)

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniqueness and attractiveness of stationary solutions in a harvesting mean field game
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Sustainable harvesting of natural resources is a central challenge both in ecology and economics. This paper explores a MFG model for harvesting in an aquatic ecosystem. Such systems have recently attracted attention from the applied mathematics community, and, due to the interplay between the competition of agents and the internal dynamics of the fish population, the analytical properties of the resulting system are very delicate to study. In the present work, we focus on stationary solutions, with a strong emphasis on their uniqueness and dynamical stability.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global regularity for a class of degenerate/singular Monge-Ampere equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the global regularity of solutions to the homogeneous Dirichlet problem for a class of Monge-Ampere equations, which become degenerate or singular on the boundary due to the zero boundary value and the distance function. The degeneracy and singularity are described by the index - the sum of the powers of the distance function and the solution. We give a complete classification of the index, and prove that the solution is globally Holder continuous, log-Lipschitz continuous, $C^{1,eta}$, $C^{2,alpha}$ and $W^{2,p}$ respectively, depending on the size of the index. We also obtain estimates related to the five regularity results. All these results are optimal.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 32 pages, no figures. Submitted for publication

Analysis of PDEs.title: Survey on periodic vortex patches
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This survey revisits classical results on the existence of periodic solutions in incompressible fluid dynamics. Owing to the breadth of the subject, we restrict our attention to the simplest and most illustrative framework: the two-dimensional Euler equations and vortex patch solutions. The aim is not to present new results, but rather to provide a unified and streamlined exposition of several classical constructions by combining ideas from the original works with more recent developments.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Non-local Interfacial Energies in Grain Boundaries via Dirichlet-to-Neumann Map and Energetic scaling
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper deals with the variational analysis of edge dislocations arising in small-angle grain boundaries (Read--Shockley) and semi-coherent interfaces (van der Merwe). Using the Nabarro--Peierls approach to model edge dislocations, we reduce the two-dimensional isotropic Navier--Lamé system governing the linearized elastic energy to a one-dimensional non-local energy on the slip interface through a Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. We prove that the resulting boundary energy coincides, up to a multiplicative constant, with the fractional \(H^{\frac12}\)-Gagliardo seminorm of the displacement jump along the interface. Within this framework, we establish the existence of a unique global minimizer by combining our dimensional-reduction result with the characterization of De Luca, Goldman, and Ponsiglione. Indeed, we show that the optimal defect configuration is uniquely attained, up to translations, by an equispaced periodic array. Finally, we provide a physical rescaling that recovers the classical logarithmic energy regimes of both the Read--Shockley and van der Merwe models.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Smooth stationary water waves with multiple vortex spikes
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For any prescribed positive integer $n$, we establish the existence of a family of stationary solutions to the two dimensional capillary-gravity water wave equations in finite depth, whose stream functions exhibit $n$ well-separated vertically aligned vortex spikes with alternating signs. The construction is based on a nonlinear gluing scheme for a singularly perturbed semilinear elliptic equation coupled to the Bernoulli equation on the free surface. Our results extend the single-spike construction to arbitrary finite multi-spike configurations and reveal a mechanism through which exponentially localized vortex spikes can coexist with an almost flat free surface.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A point-free theory of quantitative homogenization
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We introduce a purely operator-theoretic framework for quantitative
  homogenization that bypasses the traditional reliance on large-scale
  spatial regularity and probabilistic assumptions. Inspired by
  Tartar's vision of a point-free theory, we derive explicit norm
  resolvent estimates using only the algebraic structure of multiscale
  operators and the abstract geometry of Hilbert spaces. In this
  framework, the effective macroscopic dynamics and the abstract
  corrector emerge naturally from an orthogonal decomposition of the
  state space, governed algebraically by a Schur complement. To
  quantify the convergence rate, we introduce a frequency-splitting
  technique and a flux corrector obtained by inverting the microscopic
  derivative on the residual field; this controls the error for
  regular macroscopic data in terms of explicit,
  $\varepsilon$-independent operator norms.
  This abstract perspective places on one footing stationary,
  non-stationary, periodic, quasi-periodic, and stochastic
  homogenization. We demonstrate that the physical distinctions
  between these media---and their respective convergence rates---are
  captured by the behavior of the spectral measure of the microscopic
  derivative operator, evaluated on the residual field, near zero
  frequency; in the periodic case the rate $O(\varepsilon)$ is proved,
  while in the stochastic case the rates are conditional on a
  density-of-states hypothesis. Furthermore, our results apply for
  multiscale systems that do not uphold subadditivity of energy
  quantities or do not have a well-defined Brillouin zone.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 62 pages. New results and details are added. Several errors are addressed

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the Dirichlet boundary value problem on Cartan-Hadamard manifolds
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study bounded solutions of Dirichlet boundary value problems for semilinear elliptic equations on Cartan-Hadamard manifolds with pinched negative curvature. We prove nonexistence when the asymptotic boundary has zero Hausdorff measure at an exponent determined by the upper curvature bound and the spectral parameter. The result holds for continuous viscosity solutions under a one-sided bound on the nonlinearity, including the Allen-Cahn equation. The proof combines convex barriers at infinity, distance comparison for $C^{1,1}$ hypersurfaces and a spectral maximum principle. For surfaces, no lower curvature bound is needed.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 31 pages, 8 figures. v2: revised version with stronger results

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Bennati-Dragulescu-Yakovenko model in the continuous setting: PDE derivation and long-time behavior
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this manuscript, we develop and analyze a continuous version of the well-known Bennati-Dragulescu-Yakovenko (BDY) dollar-exchange discrete model. Starting from the conservative BDY exchange mechanism, we rely on kinetic theory for multi-agent systems in order to propose an analogous Boltzmann-type continuous dynamics, which does not belong to the class of other popular kinetic models for wealth exchange. We employ the quasi-invariant limit procedure to rigorously derive a nonlinear PDE on the half-line, which is a Fokker-Planck equation featuring the boundary value in the drift term. The PDE is supplemented with a nonlinear Robin-type boundary condition encoding conservation of total agents and wealth. We prove relative entropy decay to the unique stationary state that is the Boltzmann-Gibbs (exponential) distribution with a $\mathrm{e}^{-c\sqrt{t}}$ convergence rate. We determine a new entropy production term which is a Fisher information minus a competing term which measures the temporal distance of the boundary term from its equilibrium value. Thanks to an inequality relating the Fisher information relative to the Boltzmann-Gibbs equilibrium to the $L^1$-norm, we prove $L^1$-convergence toward equilibrium and convergence of the boundary term (up to a subsequence), as well as convergence in both the Hellinger and Fourier distances. This represents an advancement in classical arguments of entropy decay for Fokker-Planck equations in a kinetic framework.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On Gill's problem with anomalous diffusion
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The classical formulation of Gill's theorem establishing the linear stability of the buoyant flow in a vertical porous channel subject to transverse diffusion and bounded by impermeable walls is here reconsidered from the perspective of anomalous mass diffusion. Anomalous diffusion is a physical effect implying a more general formulation of the governing equations of mass transfer either in a fluid or in a fluid-saturated porous medium. Anomalous diffusion is mathematically modelled via a diffusion equation with a time-dependent mass diffusivity. In this study, the stationary and parallel buoyant flow in a vertical porous layer saturated by a fluid is investigated. The implications of the anomalous diffusion model for the proof that such a flow is always linearly stable are analysed.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Type-II Singularities of Immersed Locally Convex Curves Evolving under Generalized Anisotropic Gage Area-Preserving Flows with Slow Curvature Speeds
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study the singularity behavior of immersed locally convex closed plane curves evolving under generalized anisotropic Gage area-preserving flows with slow curvature speeds of the form $κ_σ^α$, where $0<α\le 1$. Here $κ_σ$ denotes the anisotropic curvature associated with a prescribed anisotropy function $σ$. We prove that every finite-time blow-up is of Type-II provided that the Euclidean length of the evolving curve remains uniformly bounded away from zero. This result holds without any symmetry assumptions on either the initial curve or the anisotropy. When the initial signed area is nonzero, this length lower bound is automatically satisfied, and thus any finite-time singularity is necessarily of Type-II. By means of Hamilton's rescaling method combined with a differential Harnack estimate, we show that along a suitable blow-up subsequence, the rescaled curves at the selected times converge locally to the profile of a translating solution of the corresponding anisotropic curvature flow $V=κ_σ^α$. We also establish sufficient conditions for finite-time singularity formation in terms of the initial signed area and anisotropic length. Moreover, we construct locally convex initial curves arbitrarily close to the Wulff curve for which a finite-time Type-II singularity occurs.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Supercritical Geometric Optics for multidimensional scalar conservation laws
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This article studies the propagation, near a smooth non-constant ground state, of monophase oscillatory wave trains with small amplitude and very high frequency for multidimensional nonlinear scalar conservation laws. These oscillations lie beyond the classical regime of uniformly bounded variation. Two scenarios may occur. Under suitable compatibility conditions, the oscillations propagate. Otherwise, they are damped through shock formation. In the baseline supercritical regime, we give an explicit criterion distinguishing these two behaviors and justify the corresponding asymptotic descriptions. At higher frequencies, the propagation mechanism becomes more restrictive and is governed by compatibility conditions involving a Lie algebra. Under a natural local constant-rank assumption, we obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of complete WKB expansions. We also prove cancellation under first-order incompatibility. Perturbing a non-constant background state limits the propagation of small scales compared with the constant-background case. Our constructions contribute to the understanding of the fractional smoothing effect conjectured by Lions, Perthame and Tadmor.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Inverse heat source problem from terminal data on a set of low Hausdorff dimension
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the recovery of a spatial source in the heat equation from terminal observations on a compact interior set $E$ with positive $β$ dimensional Hausdorff content for some $β>d-1$. The prescribed temporal forcing vanishes on a nontrivial interval immediately preceding the observation time. Under a spectral Sobolev prior and a quantitative noncancellation condition on the terminal spectral multipliers, we establish conditional logarithmic stability. For scattered observations on such sets, we derive a sampling inequality under a quasi uniformity assumption. Under explicit sampling and independent noise assumptions, we prove a logarithmic convergence rate in probability for the corresponding Tikhonov reconstructions with a data driven parameter choice. Two numerical experiments using a finite candidate approximation of a fixed Hausdorff set assess discrete spectral sampling stability and illustrate the effects of the waiting interval and measurement noise on reconstruction.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Structural stability of cylindrical transonic shocks to the three-dimensional Zeldovich-von Neumann-Döring combustion equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We address the structural stability of transonic shock solutions to the Zeldovich-von Neumann-Döring (ZND) combustion equations in a cylindrical domain under three-dimensional perturbations of the incoming supersonic flow and exit pressure. The perturbed transonic shock is completely free and its strength and position are uniquely determined by the incoming flow and the exit pressure. The solution shares the same regularity for the velocity, the pressure, the entropy and the fraction of unburned gas. The main difficulties are that the shock front is a free boundary to be determined simultaneously with the subsonic flow and the equations for all states are coupled with each other due to the combustion process. One of the key ingredients of the analysis is to reformulate the three-dimensional ZND combustion equations into a deformation-curl system and four transport equations in terms of the deformation tensor and vorticity. Another one is an elaborate decomposition of the Rankine-Hugoniot conditions so that the shock front is uniquely determined by an algebraic equation and an unusual second order differential boundary condition is obtained on the shock front for the first order nonlocal deformation-curl system, from which an oblique boundary condition can be derived after homogenizing the curl system and introducing the potential function.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Genus Increase in Closed Mean Curvature Flows
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct counterexamples to Ilmanen's genus-reduction conjecture for closed mean curvature flows. We prove that a compact hypersurface with a single isolated conical singularity and a power rate of convergence to its cone admits a mean curvature flow whose forward rescaled limit is a prescribed expander smoothly asymptotic to that cone. Combining this theorem with closed mean curvature flows with prescribed tangent flows (arXiv:2405.15577, arXiv:2607.23879) and the noncompact counterexample (arXiv:2605.09657) gives the desired examples.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Singular set estimates in quasilinear Alt-Caffarelli problems
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For a nonnegative, uniformly convex function $Φ$, we study nonnegative minimizers of the quasilinear Alt-Caffarelli energy $\int_ΩΦ(\nabla u)+χ_{\{u>0\}}$. Under mild regularity assumptions on $Φ$, we show that the codimension of the singular set of the free boundary is at least $2+η$ for a positive $η$. With a singular minimizer in three dimensions in a forthcoming work, this result is sharp as long as integer dimensions are considered. Our proof method is flexible, and we use it to also prove a similar result for minimizers of the $p$-Laplacian counterpart of the Alt-Caffarelli energy.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Normalised Hamiltonian Elliptic Systems: a Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality for bilinear mass
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study Hamiltonian elliptic systems with prescribed bilinear mass $\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}uv=a>0$. We establish a Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality in the crossed gradient pairing and bilinear mass, on scaling-invariant component-bounded classes. It identifies the critical curve $1/p+1/q=N/(N+2)$ and the restricted energy trichotomy. For power nonlinearities, we establish uniqueness up to common translations and nondegeneracy of positive profiles throughout the Sobolev-subcritical hyperbola. Exact scaling then classifies positive normalised solutions and identifies the unique critical mass. In dimension two, we develop a bilinear exponential Gagliardo--Nirenberg estimate with a sharp gradient threshold and a truncated scalar refinement with the optimal quartic leading coefficient. Adapting variational ideas from [Cassani-Tarsi, Calc.Var.PDE (2015)] we combine a mass-normalising quotient, reduction over the full negative fibres and compactness below the concentration threshold to obtain least-energy positive radial solutions for pure exponential nonlinearities at every prescribed mass below the cubic limiting mass. Local perturbative branches and a small-frequency exponential branch yield explicit mass-response formulas.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On Brezis' open problem 2.4
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We show the existence of a ``nonradial" smooth entire solution of the Ginzburg--Landau equation with degree $q\in\{8,9\}$ and modulus tending to one at infinity. This answers Brezis' Open Problem 2.4 negatively. To construct the counterexample, we vary a cone parameter $q \in [8, 9]$ and keeping the degree on the cone equal to one. Several key ingredients are needed. First, we need to compute the Morse index of radial vortex solutions at $q\in \{8, 9\}$. Second, we need to show compactness. Finally, Leray-Schauder degree theory and a homotopy argument yield the desired existence result.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Development of singular surfaces and formation of generic singularities in 3D pressureless flows
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, the Cauchy problem for the equations of pressureless flows in three space dimensions is considered. It is well known that for smooth initial data, the density and velocity gradient often become unbounded at a finite time $t_0$. This type of singularity is associated with sticky-particle dynamics. For an open dense set of smooth initial data, the formation and structure of singularities are investigated using the transversality theorem, with the aid of constructive methods for initial velocity fields. In contrast to the two-dimensional case studied by Bressan, Chen and Huang (arXiv:2408.06877), for $t>t_0$ a singular hypersurface will be formed, whose governing system of equations is not hyperbolic. By assuming the initial data are analytic, we are able to precisely analyze the singular behavior of velocity and density. Based on this, the system of equations for singular hypersurfaces can be recast into a first-order system of Briot-Bouquet type, and the local analytic solution can be constructed using a version of the Cauchy-Kovalevskaya theorem.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Sharp Constant in the Second-Order Hydrogen Uncertainty Principle: Spectral Characterization and Quantitative Approximation
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
In this work, we study the sharp constant \(\mathcal H_d\) in the second-order Hydrogen Uncertainty Principle in every dimension \(d\ge2\). Using a spectral basis built from generalized Laguerre polynomials, together with a linearization procedure and spherical harmonic decomposition, we establish a spectral characterization of \(\mathcal H_d\). More precisely, we show that \[ \mathcal H_d =
\frac12\min\{d+1,c_d^*\}, \] where \(c_d^*\in(0,d+3)\) is the unique parameter such that \[ \|S_{c_d^*}^{(d)}\|_{\ell^2\to\ell^2}=1. \] Here, for \(0<c<d+3\), \(S_c^{(d)}\) is an explicit positive Hilbert--Schmidt operator on \(\ell^2(\mathbb N_0)\). This characterization reveals a competition between the radial sector, which yields the value \(d+1\), and the first non-radial sector, encoded by the spectral parameter \(c_d^*\). For \(d\ge4\), we recover the known identity \[ \mathcal H_d=\frac{d+1}{2} \] through a spectral argument, giving an alternative proof of the results of Cazacu, Flynn and Lam \cite{CazacuFlynnLam} for \(d\ge5\) and Huang and Ye \cite{HuangYe} for \(d=4\). For \(d\in\{2,3\}\), this characterization yields \[ \mathcal H_d=\frac{c_d^*}{2}. \] We then exploit this spectral formulation to derive an explicit finite recursive scheme yielding effective two-sided bounds for \(\mathcal H_2\) and \(\mathcal H_3\), substantially improving the estimates of Huang and Ye \cite{HuangYe}.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Effective Hamiltonians in Perforated Domains: Inf-Max formula and Stability
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the dependence of the effective Hamiltonian $\overline H_Ω(p)$ on the geometry of periodic perforated domains for convex Hamilton--Jacobi equations with state-constraint boundary conditions. We establish an inf--max representation over smooth test functions for domains with $C^1$ boundary. Using this representation, we derive a quantitative stability estimate in terms of the Hausdorff distance between domains and the reach of one boundary. This estimate yields convergence for non-nested domain approximations whose Hausdorff error is negligible relative to their boundary reach. Examples demonstrate the sharpness of the continuity modulus and show that Hausdorff convergence alone can fail to preserve the effective Hamiltonian, even for smooth domains and the quadratic Hamiltonian.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Linear Stability, Inviscid Damping, and Scattering for Monotone Shear Flows in 2D Ideal MHD
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the linearized 2D ideal incompressible magnetohydrodynamic equations around a monotone shear flow $(U(y),0)$ with a constant horizontal magnetic field $(β,0)$ on $\mathbb{T} \times \mathbb{R}$. For each fixed $β\neq 0$, we assume that the shear rate $U'$ is bounded above and below by positive constants and varies sufficiently slowly, although it need not be close to any constant. For every nontrivial perturbation with zero horizontal average, we establish sharp $L^2$ time rates in the corresponding paired norms: the horizontal velocity and magnetic components remain of order one, the vertical components decay at rate $\langle t \rangle^{-1}$, and the vorticity--current pair grows at rate $\langle t \rangle$. We prove strong $L^2$ scattering to two Alfvén profiles, identify the leading asymptotic behavior of the physical variables, and establish asymptotic completeness in the natural energy space.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniform Large Deviations, Barrier Identity and the Néel--Arrhenius Law for the One-Dimensional Stochastic Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert Equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study the one-dimensional stochastic Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation with a regularised, multiplicative, degenerate trace-class noise of strength sqrt(eps), the regularisation being Q_delta^{1/2} = (I + delta A^{beta/2})^{-1}, A = -d^2/dx^2, beta > 3/2, and determine the exponential rate of thermally induced magnetisation reversal.
  (i) Uniform large deviations at fixed delta: for every delta > 0 the solution satisfies a large deviation principle on C([0,T];H), with a good rate function, uniformly in the initial datum over a V-bounded set with compact H-closure; no non-degeneracy of the noise is assumed.
  (ii) Removal of the regularisation: as delta tends to 0 the noise tends to space-time white noise. With U_delta the state-space quasi-potential and U_0 that of the limiting control problem (Q_0^{1/2} = I), U_delta converges to U_0 in the Gamma-sense, and the barrier is delta-independent: the infimum of U_delta over the boundary of D equals that of U_0 and equals c_* times the infimum of the micromagnetic energy E over that boundary, c_* = 2 lambda_2/(lambda_1^2 + lambda_2^2), under two structural assumptions only and with no geometric or transversality input. Pointwise convergence fails, so the Gamma-limit is the sharp form of the statement.
  (iii) Neel-Arrhenius law: combining (i) and (ii) with the classical exit-time theorem, the escape time tau from D = {E < r} satisfies both levels of the law - for every fixed delta > 0, eps log E[tau] converges, uniformly on compact subsets of the initial set, to the barrier, and lim_{delta->0} lim_{eps->0} eps log E[tau] = c_* times the infimum of E over the boundary of D. The Arrhenius exponent is therefore stable under the regularisation of the noise and is determined by the micromagnetic energy alone.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Failure of the local decay formula for Arnold multiplicities under twisted Kähler--Ricci flow
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Di Nezza--Guedj--Lu asked whether local Arnold multiplicities under maximal weak twisted Kähler--Ricci flow with fixed cohomology class satisfy $λ(\varphi_t,x)=\max\{λ(\varphi_0,x)-t,0\}$. We construct counterexamples with analytic initial singularities in every dimension $n\ge2$. On the Hirzebruch surface $\mathbb F_e$, $e\ge2$, the initial current $[S]+(e+1)[F]$ yields $λ(\varphi_t,x)=1/2-t/e$ for $x\in S\setminus F$ and $0<t<e/2$, where $S$ is the negative section and $F$ a fibre. Products with smooth stationary factors give higher-dimensional examples. The Zariski negative part of $\{S\}+\{F\}$, the reduced support class, forces extra divisor mass. For pure divisorial data with simple normal crossings support, a smooth semipositive representative of the reduced support class's positive part gives exact short-time formulas. On one surface we construct flows with identical initial current germs, background data and global initial Arnold multiplicity, but different local rates.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Morse theory methods for a class of quasi-linear elliptic systems of higher order
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We develop the local Morse theory for a class of non-twice continuously differentiable functionals on Hilbert spaces, including a new generalization of the Gromoll-Meyer's splitting theorem and a weaker Marino-Prodi perturbation type result. They are applicable to a wide range of multiple integrals with quasi-linear elliptic Euler equations and systems of higher order.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Differences between this version and the published version [Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations 58 (2019), no. 4, Paper No. 134] are as follows: in addition to the passage from inequalities (2.7)-(2.8) through the end of the proof of Lemma 2.10, several typographical errors in other parts of the paper have also been corrected

Analysis of PDEs.title: Endpoint well-posedness for the Boussinesq equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove small-data global well-posedness for the quadratic good Boussinesq equation on the real line and the circle at the endpoint $H^{-1/2}\times H^{-3/2}$. On each domain, a small invariant spectral set supports a continuous global group, with uniqueness in a fixed local integral class. In the periodic case, both components have zero mean and the flow is Lipschitz on bounded time intervals. The a priori bounds follow from a balanced perturbation determinant for the third-order Lax operator. Averaging two real spectral branches yields coercivity and frequency-tail control. On the line, we construct the endpoint flow by commuting Hamiltonians and Green-field estimates. On the circle, discrete spectral bounds and Kishimoto's endpoint local theory give global well-posedness.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Designed short-time observations for rotational damping recovery in Timoshenko beams
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the recovery of spatial rotational damping in a clamped Timoshenko beam. The coefficient belongs to a prescribed bounded finite-dimensional family. One fixed spatial average of rotation is recorded in separately labelled experiments with known initial rotational velocities. We construct these velocities so that the leading coefficient-to-data map is an invertible Gram matrix. Testing the equations against the smooth observation kernel gives a uniform parameter-Lipschitz remainder without differentiating the damping coefficient. A weighted temporal moment then yields global injectivity, Lipschitz stability and a globally convergent projected fixed-point reconstruction for sufficiently short observation times. Upper and deterministic two-point lower bounds give the same noise-amplification order $T^{-5/2}$ for $L^2$ time-history errors. A second sensitivity estimate supplies a separate sufficient condition for strong convexity and global projected-gradient convergence. We derive continuous and exact discrete adjoints, prove finite-time convergence of a conforming finite-element midpoint scheme, and propagate forward error into coefficient error. Reproducible synthetic experiments examine symmetry, gradient accuracy, noise and discretization bias.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Liouville theorems for the stationary Navier-Stokes equations under partial component conditions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove Liouville theorems for smooth stationary incompressible Navier-Stokes flows in $R^3$ with finite Dirichlet integral and velocity vanishing uniformly at infinity. If the partial components of velocity $(u_1,u_2)$ belong to $L^{4,\infty}$, then we show that $u$ must vanish. The second result only requires that one component $u_1$ belongs to $L^{3/2,\infty}$. The proofs are based on the head-pressure sign and a localized energy identity, combined with different pressure estimates for the two cases.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Higher-Order Paracontrolled Calculus for Geometric Rough Paths
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study the rough differential equation
  $$
  \frac{du_t}{dt}= F(u_t) ζ_t, \ \ u(0) = u_0 \in \mathbb{R}^d,
  $$
  where $F : \mathbb{R}^d \to L(\mathbb{R}^d, \mathbb{R}^d)$ is a sufficiently regular vector field, and the noise $ζ$ is a distribution in $\mathscr{C}^{α-1}(\mathbb{R})$ for $α\in (\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{3})$. We construct solutions to this equation at lower regularity than previous work of Gubinelli-Imkeller-Perkowski and Prömel-Trabs using ideas from the high-order paracontrolled viewpoint of Bailleul-Bernicot. The key tool in our work is the development of a harmonic-analytic framework for proving a set of iterated commutator estimates which are necessary for the solution theory. We also show the procedure of enhancement when the noise $ζ= dZ$, where $Z$ is a realization of fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H \in (\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{3})$.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 50 pages; small typos with scaling fixed in Lemma 3.3f. Comments welcome!

Analysis of PDEs.title: Propagation dynamics of a parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis model in a time-periodic shifting environment
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The current paper is devoted to the study of the propagation dynamics of a parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis model in a shifting environment. We investigate the scenario in which the favorable and unfavorable habitats are spatially separated, with the favorable habitat shifting at a time-periodic speed. We first establish the vanishing, persistence, and spreading properties of solutions with compactly supported and front-like initial data. In particular, we show that if the self-limitation rate of the species is large relative to the chemotactic sensitivity and the species is initially confined to a bounded region, then the species eventually becomes extinct when the habitat shifts rightward with a large average speed. In contrast, when the average shifting speed of the habitat is moderate, the species can persist and spread along the shifting habitat into an increasingly large spatial region. Finally, we establish the existence and nonexistence of time-periodic forced wave solutions whose wave speed coincides with the average shifting speed of the habitat.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Unconditional uniqueness for the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation in $H^{1/2}(\Bbb T^3)$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we establish unconditional uniqueness for the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLS) in the scaling-critical class $H^{1/2}(\mathbb{T}^3)$. Unlike approaches based on the GP-hierarchy or normal form reductions, which typically involve higher-order expansions, our proof works directly with the original cubic NLS, where we also make use of several new a priori Euclidean-like Strichartz estimates. More precisely, we show that every distributional solution in $C_tH_x^{1/2}$ belongs a priori to the class $L^2_{t,\mathrm{loc}}L_x^6$. The key ingredients are a suitable high-low modulation decomposition and the compactness of solution trajectories on bounded time intervals. We also exploit the preservation of the canonical symplectic form under the truncated NLS flow, in order to obtain necessary stability estimates in the rough Sobolev space $H^{-1/2}(\mathbb{T}^3)$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Singular analysis of the principal eigenvalue for cooperative elliptic systems with drifts
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We determine the small-diffusion limit of the principal eigenvalue for a one-dimensional cooperative elliptic system with component-dependent drifts and Neumann boundary conditions. For scalar equations, this limit is determined by local data at the drift equilibria and boundary points. We show that such localization fails for systems: switching between components can make some intervals spectrally relevant. We first prove that the logarithmic transforms of all component eigenfunctions converge to the same function, which solves a scalar Hamilton-Jacobi equation. The associated Aubry set determines the asymptotic behavior of the principal eigenvalue. Under nondegeneracy assumptions, this set decomposes into isolated points, regular intervals, and composite intervals containing common drift zeros. We then identify the effective value of each class through local Ornstein-Uhlenbeck spectra and interval transport problems, and establish that the limit of the principal eigenvalue is the minimum of these class values. A unique minimizing class also determines the common logarithmic eigenfunction profile.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Free boundary regularity for the porous medium equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we resolve the local cone conjecture proposed by Kienzler, Koch, and Vázquez concerning the free-boundary regularity of the porous medium equation. We prove that the local cone condition guarantees the smoothness of the free boundary lying outside the initial support. The proof relies on new gradient estimates obtained through maximum principle arguments and comparison principles. As an application, we establish the global-in-time smoothness of the free boundary for solutions with convex initial support under standard assumptions on the initial data.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Asymmetric Periodic Water Waves in Finite Depth
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the full two-dimensional water-wave equations in finite depth, with and without surface tension. Water waves have been studied mathematically for more than two centuries. Reflection symmetry remains a common assumption in constructions of periodic steady waves, although asymmetric profiles have been observed in experiments and numerical computations. We construct families of periodic stationary solutions whose free surfaces have no axis of reflection, in both the pure-gravity and capillary--gravity cases. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first rigorous construction of asymmetric periodic pure-gravity waves for the full two-dimensional water-wave problem in finite depth. The proof combines localized vorticity laws with a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction. In the pure-gravity case, we introduce a small background shear flow to obtain an invertible boundary operator and couple the interior and free-surface approximations at leading order.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Deterministic Game-Theoretic Approach to Convexity-Preserving Property and Finite-Time Extinction of Level Sets for Geometric Equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the convexity-preserving property and finite-time extinction of level sets for quasilinear geometric equations using a game-theoretic approach introduced by Kohn and Serfaty. To construct the game whose value function approximates the viscosity solution, we use the approach introduced by Sato.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The inverse Monge--Ampère flow on klt Fano varieties
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish the long time existence of the inverse Monge--Ampère flow on a klt $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano variety $X$. We further prove that $X$ admits a Kähler--Einstein metric if and only if the flow converges in $L^1$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Almost Periodicity Properties Arising From the Sodin-Yuditskii Theory
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The Kotani-Last problem and the Deift conjecture are two well known statements, which both concern the almost periodicity properties of the functions under consideration, and which have both been disproved in their original formulation, which involves Bohr/Bochner almost periodicity. To contrast these disproofs, and to further elucidate the essence of these two challenging problems, we establish positive results regarding each of them by showing that Weyl almost periodicity can be deduced whenever the Sodin-Yuditskii setup can be implemented. The latter requires that the Schrödinger operator associated with the function in question has purely absolutely continuous spectral measure and a spectrum with finite total gap length and the Parreau-Widom property. We also show that the known examples for which Bohr/Bochner almost periodicity has been shown or suggested to fail in the context of the Deift conjecture are in fact Weyl almost periodic. As a result, an accordingly modified version of the Deift conjecture remains a tantalizing open problem.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Nonrelativistic limit of nonlinear Dirac ground states on noncompact quantum graphs
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the nonrelativistic limit of nonlinear Dirac ground states on finite noncompact metric graphs with Kirchhoff-type conditions. For a nondecreasing nonlinearity of arbitrary finite superquadratic growth, a sufficiently long pendant path guarantees ground states whose nonrelativistic limits are Schrödinger ground states. Every choice of these states is relatively compact in $H^1$ and satisfies a uniform exponential decay estimate. On general graphs, we prove a compactness alternative: loss of compactness requires at least the action of a full-line ground state. Translated line profiles show that the loss constants are sharp. The proof combines an $H^1$ estimate in terms of the action with convergence of Dirac fiber maxima to Schrödinger ray maxima. For power nonlinearities, we give an integral criterion in terms of the dimensionless pendant length and obtain the same conclusions for arbitrary edge lengths on four graph topologies.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: We have revised and rewritten the manuscript based on the reviewers' comments. 35 pages, comments are welcome

Analysis of PDEs.title: Free boundary regularity and well-posedness of physical solutions to the supercooled Stefan problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the regularity and well-posedness of physical solutions to the supercooled Stefan problem. Assuming only that the initial temperature is integrable, we prove that the free boundary, known to have jump discontinuities as a function of the time variable, is $C^1$ as a function of the space variable, and is $C^{\infty}$ outside of a closed, countable set, which we describe explicitly. We also prove that, as conjectured in arXiv:1902.05174, the set of positive times when a jump occurs cannot have accumulation points. In addition, we prove that short-time uniqueness of physical solutions implies global uniqueness, which allows us to obtain uniqueness for very general initial data that fall outside the scope of the current well-posedness regime. In particular, we answer two questions left open in arXiv:1811.12356, arXiv:2302.13097, regarding the global uniqueness of solutions. We proceed by deriving a weighted obstacle problem satisfied by the solutions, which we exploit to establish regularity and non-degeneracy estimates and to classify the free boundary points. We also establish a backward propagation of oscillation property, which allows us to control the occurrence of future jumps in terms of the past oscillation of the solution.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: To appear in Probab. Theory Related Fields. 31 pages, 2 figures. v3: Extended the local finiteness result to all singular times, including non-jump singularities

Analysis of PDEs.title: A fractional modular Poincaré--Wirtinger-type inequality in Sobolev spaces with variable exponents
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain and let $p:Ω\to[1,\infty)$ be a measurable, essentially bounded exponent; no regularity of $p$ -- in particular, no log-Hölder continuity -- is assumed. For a general non-negative measurable kernel $\mathcal{K}(x,y)$ admitting a radial bounding function $κ(x,r)$ in the second variable, we establish the fractional modular Poincaré--Wirtinger-type inequality $$
  \iint_{Ω\timesΩ}\mathcal{K}(x,y)\,|u(x)-u(y)|^{p(x)} d y\, d x
  \leqslant C\int_Ωc(x)\left(\int_Ω
  \frac{|\nabla u(z)|^{p(x)}}{|z-x|^{n-1+θ}}\, d z\right) d x, $$ valid for every $u\in W^{1,1}(Ω)$, in particular every $u\in W^{1,p(\cdot)}(Ω)$, and every $θ\in[0,1)$. Here $$ c(x)=\int_0^{D}r^{n+p(x)-2+θ}κ(x,r)\,d r, $$ $D$ is the diameter of any fixed ball containing $\overlineΩ$, and the constant $C$ depends only on $n,p^+,θ$ and the fixed domain $Ω$. For the fractional kernel $\mathcal{K}(x,y)=|x-y|^{-n-λp(x)}$ we obtain a variable-exponent Gagliardo-modular estimate. The proof replaces the starshaped chain decompositions used there by a combination of a Morrey-type estimate on starshaped domains, a positive-kernel proof of weighted Poincaré inequalities, and one reflection extension for the weights $|z-x|^{-(n-1+θ)}$. The constants are uniform down to exponent $1$, and the inequalities are understood in the extended nonnegative sense when either side is infinite.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Calderón problem for the fractional Schrödinger equation at a single point
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We revisit the Calderón problem for the fractional Schrödinger equation and prove that the potential is determined by Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps at a single exterior point, with exterior inputs varying in a disjoint open set. This holds for continuous potentials for all $0<s<1$ and for bounded potentials when $s\geq 1/4$. For ordered nonnegative bounded potentials, one fixed nonzero nonnegative input and one point measurement suffice for every $0<s<1$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Two-layer conjugate flows in an open channel
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate conjugate flows in a two-layer fluid system with a flat bottom and a free surface. These are up- and downstream states consistent with simultaneous conservation of mass, momentum, and energy; and therefore candidate end-states of one-dimensional dissipationless bores. By choosing variables in a specific way, we are able to explicitly parameterize all physical non-trivial conjugate flows in the system, using only rational functions. This two-parameter family can be categorized according to whether the states are compatible with (1) a rising surface, and falling internal interface; or (2) vice versa. In particular, we rule out the existence of monotone bore solutions, consistent with an earlier result due to Chen, Walsh, and Wheeler. However, here we do so already at the level of conjugate flows. Separating these two distinct categories is a one-parameter family of critical trivial conjugate flows. The complete description obtained in the present paper serves as an important stepping stone towards finding actual realizing heteroclinic orbits connecting such conjugate states.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Keller problem for the lowest positive eigenvalue of Dirac operators with Lorentz scalar potentials
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the Keller problem for the Dirac operator $\mathcal{D}_m - Vβ$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and minimize its lowest positive eigenvalue over all potentials $V$ with prescribed $L^p$ norm. We prove that optimal potentials always exist and that the corresponding eigenspinors solve the nonlinear Soler equation. This provides a variational proof of existence of solitary waves for this equation. We prove that there are no zero modes for such operators in dimensions $1$ and $2$, and conjecture that zero mode may exist in dimension $3$. In dimension $d = 2$, we provide numerical evidence that the optimal potentials concentrate on flower-shape regions, which are not necessarily radial, showing that Faber--Krahn type results may fail for such Dirac operators. In dimension $1$, all quantities are explicit.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Topological Anderson Insulators by homogenization theory
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
A central property of (Chern) topological insulators is the presence of robust asymmetric transport along interfaces separating two-dimensional insulating materials in different topological phases. A Topological Anderson Insulator is an insulator whose topological phase is induced by spatial fluctuations.
  This paper proposes a mathematical model of perturbed Dirac equations and shows that for sufficiently large and highly oscillatory perturbations, the systems is in a different topological phase than the unperturbed model. In particular, a robust asymmetric transport indeed appears at an interface separating perturbed and unperturbed phases.
  The theoretical results are based on careful estimates of resolvent operators in the homogenization theory of Dirac equations and on the characterization of topological phases by the index of an appropriate Fredholm operator.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Corrects the norm-resolvent estimate (Theorem 2.6), index formulas (Sect. 2), and the gap-closing remark from the published version [Comm. Partial Differential Equations 49 (2024), 989-1010], alongside minor misprints. An official corrigendum has been submitted to the publisher

Analysis of PDEs.title: Finite-time blow-up for the real-valued defocusing energy-supercritical NLW
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We construct real-valued solutions of the defocusing energy-supercritical nonlinear wave equation $\partial_t^2u-Δu+u^p=0$ that blow up in finite time from smooth, compactly supported initial data. We consider three cases: for $p=3$ we construct blow-up solutions in all dimensions $d\geq 9$, for $p=5$ we treat all dimensions $d\geq 7$, while for $p=7$ we treat all dimensions $d\geq 6$.
  The solutions we construct here appear to be the first blow-up solutions of defocusing energy-supercritical nonlinear wave equations with smooth real-valued data. The main step is the construction of nonzero \emph{discretely self-similar profiles} that are periodic in self-similar time and real-analytic across the light cone. We find approximate profiles by numerical continuation from rotating self-similar solutions of the complex-valued equation and upgrade them to exact solutions by a computer-assisted Newton--Kantorovich argument in a Banach algebra of Fourier--Chebyshev coefficients. The main analytic ingredients are an exact description of the linear mode operators and uniform bounds for their inverses.
  The codes for the computer-assisted parts of the proofs, together with the approximate solutions, are available on GitHub \cite{code}.

Analysis of PDEs.title: $L^p$ Convergence of AMV Laplacians on completions of Riemannian manifolds
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study conditions for the $L^p$ convergence of the AMV Laplacian $Δ_r$ on completions of Riemannian manifolds $(M,g)$. The condition invloves the Minkowski dimension of the set $\overline{M} \setminus M$ and how much the curvature is blowing up around $S$. We build a concrete family of sets that satisfies these conditions, and provide an example of non convergence when these conditions are not met.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniqueness and large-time continuous dependence in a doubly degenerate nutrient taxis system
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
\[
  u_t = \nabla \cdot (uv\nabla u) - χ\nabla\cdot (u^2 v\nabla v) + \ell uv,
  \qquad \qquad
  v_t = Δv - uv, \] is considered in a smoothly bounded domain $Ω\subset {\mathbb{R}}^n$ and with $χ\ge 0$ and $\ell\ge 0$.
  Within a suitable concept of solvability, a statement on uniqueness of solutions emanating from initial data $(u_0,v_0)$ is derived under the mere assumption that $u_0\in L^\infty(Ω)$ and $v_0\in W^{1,\infty}(Ω)$ are such that $u_0\ge 0$ and $v_0>0$ in $\overlineΩ$; in particular, no condition on continuity of $u_0$ is imposed.
  This result is thereafter used to reveal that in physcally meaningful scenarios, for any initial data which are additionally assumed to be continuous and nontrivial, such solutions can always be found, and that these solutions depend continuously on the initial distributions not only in bounded sets of the form $Ω\times (0,T)$, but actually throughout $Ω\times (0,\infty)$, in a suitable sense.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Quantitative stability and strict inequalities for the Escobar functional
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For Euclidean domains whose boundaries are sufficiently close to a sphere in $C^2$, we bound the deficit of the Escobar constant from below by the squared $H^{3/2}$ norm of the boundary graph, after fixing its constant and first spherical harmonics. This holds in every dimension $n\ge3$ and implies a bound in Fraenkel asymmetry with optimal quadratic power. Under fixed $C^{6,α}$ and size bounds, the asymmetry estimate also holds for star-shaped domains in dimensions $n\ge6$. For compact Riemannian manifolds with minimal boundary and uniform geometric bounds, we prove $S_\ast-C^*_{\text{Esc}}(M,g)\ge ca^4/\log(Λ/a)$ in dimension six and $S_\ast-C^*_{\text{Esc}}(M,g)\ge ca^4$ in higher dimensions, where $a=\|\mathring{\mathrm{II}}\|_{L^\infty}>0$. A family satisfying the same bounds has deficit comparable to $a^{8/3}$, excluding uniform lower bounds with smaller powers. We also compute the cubic coefficient of the standard boundary bubble quotient and give uniform remainder estimates.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 52 pages. Split from arXiv:2601.22665v2 (Part 1/3), with new results on the geometric stability of the Escobar functional. Other parts forthcoming. Comments welcome!

Analysis of PDEs.title: Simultaneous Recovery of Wave Speeds and Initial Sources on Graphs via Redundant Frontier Propagation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the simultaneous recovery of an unknown initial signal and unknown vertex wave speeds for the wave equation on a finite graph from time-dependent measurements on a prescribed set of vertices. With the graph geometry known, we first show that a single experiment determines both quantities under a new two-witness zero forcing condition and generic nondegeneracy assumptions. We then develop a more general frontier-propagation framework in which the redundancy required for simultaneous recovery is distributed across successive graph contours rather than localized at individual forcing vertices. We derive Lipschitz stability estimates for the frontier propagation problem. We also show the recovery and stability results extend to positively weighted graphs.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Generic small-scale creation in the two-dimensional Euler equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The Cauchy problem for the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation is globally well-posed for smooth initial data. We prove that, for all $p>2$ and for a dense $G_δ$ set of initial vorticities in $W^{1,p}$, the solutions lose regularity in infinite time, in the sense that the $L^p$ norm of the gradient of the vorticity is unbounded. This confirms a long-standing conjecture of Yudovich.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: This new version extends the previous result: we now prove the full Yudovich conjecture. It avoids some issues in Sections 8 and 10, simplifies the proof, and significantly shortens the paper

Functional Analysis.title: Complete entropy contraction from conditional hyperboundedness
Functional Analysis.summary:
For finite-dimensional quantum channels compatible with a faithful conditional expectation, we show that conditional hyperboundedness and strict GNS contraction together yield a relative entropy contraction. For KMS-symmetric quantum Markov semigroups, a conditional $2\to q$ hyperboundedness at time $t_0>0$ combined with a GNS gap $λ>0$ implies a modified logarithmic Sobolev constant \[ α=\frac{λ(1-2/q)}
  {12(λt_0+\log M+1-2/q)},\] where $M$ is the hyperboundedness constant. As a consequence, completely bounded hyperboundedness over auxiliary systems gives complete versions of entropy contraction with the same rates.

Functional Analysis.title: The $\varepsilon$-smoothed Entanglement of Formation and its relation to the Moreau-Yosida approximation
Functional Analysis.summary:
We describe a family of convex continuous functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$, on the set of states of a bipartite quantum system (consisting of finite-dimensional or infinite-dimensional subsystems) obtained by applying the Mora-Piani-Briegel construction of $\varepsilon$-measure (proposed in [Phys. Rev. A 109, 052413]) to the Entanglement of Formation (EoF) with the use of the trace norm distance in the role of basic metric. These functions are non-increasing in $\varepsilon$ and converge pointwise to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$.
