We conducted a detailed analysis of properties of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, using (among others) the relationship between the family $\{E_{F,\varepsilon}\}_{\varepsilon\in[0,1]}$ and the family $\{E^λ_F(ρ)\}_{λ>0}$ of Moreau-Yosida approximations of the EoF explored in [arXiv:2609.30246].
  We obtain a variational expression for the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ (which for $\varepsilon=0$ turns into the standard variational expression for the EoF). We also describe the weak subadditivity property of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ and analyse their continuity properties.
  The semicontinuity bounds for the EoF (presented in [Lob.J.Math., 46, 2632-2658],[arXiv:2404.07978]) allow us to obtain easily computable upper bounds on the rate of uniform convergence of the function $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$ on the sets of states with bounded rank/energy of one of the marginal states.
  Applicability of the obtained results to other entanglement measures, in particular, to the relative entropy of entanglement, is discussed.
  As an auxiliary result, it is shown that for any state of an infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum system, there exists a nearest separable state w.r.t. the trace norm distance. The non-uniqueness of such a state is also shown.
Functional Analysis.comment: 36 pages, preliminary version, one comments and references are welcome

Functional Analysis.title: Exponential Growth of Mean Multiplicities in Length Spectra of Semi-Arithmetic Surfaces of Arbitrary Arithmetic Dimension
Functional Analysis.summary: For a semi-arithmetic Fuchsian group $Γ$ of arithmetic dimension $r$ with a generalized modular embedding, EGMM holds for $r\leq2$, and for $r\geq3$ under an explicit \emph{strong contraction condition}, via a multi-dimensional Schwarz-Pick bound and a geometry-of-numbers estimate. A covering construction turns every known example into an infinite explicit family with the same exponent via principal congruence towers. We add new $r\leq2$ examples (genus-$3$/$4$ Prym eigenform loci, a different commensurability class from the known triangle groups and McMullen genus-two family) and attempt a direct flat-geometric bound on the contraction constant $δ$ for the latter via its Lyapunov exponents ($δ=2/3$ on ergodic average, by Bainbridge exact computation), explaining why an average bound does not yet certify the pointwise one \eqref{eqstrong-contraction} needs.

Functional Analysis.title: A solution to Haagerup's problem: Normality of weights is commutatively determined
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove that a weight on a C$^*$-algebra is lower semi-continuous if it is lower semi-continuous on commutative C$^*$-subalgebras. This can be used to prove a von Neumann algebraic counterpart that a weight on a von Neumann algebra is normal if it is normal on commutative von Neumann subalgebras. This provides an affirmative solution to Haagerup's second problem (Problem 1.11) on normal weights posed in 1975.

Functional Analysis.title: Self-intersection local times of Volterra Gaussian bridges with large end-to-end distance
Functional Analysis.summary: Self-intersection local times serve as the Hamiltonian in the Gibbs measure of continuous polymer models, for which the end-to-end distance is a key quantity. We study multiple self-intersection local times of Volterra Gaussian bridges, \emph{i.e.}, Volterra Gaussian processes conditioned on their final location $a$, as $\|a\|\to\infty$. For $d$-dimensional $(2,ζ)$-locally nondeterministic processes with $ζ\in(0,2/d)$, we prove that these local times exist in every $L^p$. Under two further conditions on the kernel, the $p$-th moment of the $m$-multiple self-intersection local time of the bridge is of exact order $\|a\|^{-γ}$ for every integer $p\geqslant1$, with $γ=p(m-1)(2-ζd)/(2-ζ)$. In the plane, for kernels $k(t-s)$ with $k(0)\neq0$ and under strong local nondeterminism, we restrict the double self-intersection local time to $\{t_2-t_1\geqslant\|a\|^{-α}\}$, $α>0$, and establish a phase transition: its expectation decays like $\exp(-c\|a\|^{2-α})$, converges to an explicit positive limit, or grows logarithmically, for $α<2$, $α=2$ and $α>2$ respectively.

Functional Analysis.title: Endpoint gradient bounds for centered convex maximal operators and probability kernels
Functional Analysis.summary: We establish the endpoint gradient estimate for centered homothetic maximal averages in every dimension $d\ge2$ over each fixed convex body with $C^{1,θ}$ boundary, $0<θ\le1$. In particular, the centered ball maximal operator satisfies the $W^{1,1}$ gradient bound in every dimension. Neither strict convexity nor a lower bound on the support gap is required. The geometric argument combines concentration in gradient values with nonhomogeneous calibrated rows and a summable radial correction. It extends the scalar refinement, direction-history construction and global assembly of the planar centered-disk proof of OpenAI. A separate transfer theorem gives sharp singular-derivative identities for bounded compact probability kernels once local BV output is known, and gradient continuity under an additional spatial-tail condition. Quantitative contact and translation estimates yield further profile and kernel examples. The estimates retain the fixed body's regularity data; the endpoint for arbitrary $C^1$ and nonsmooth convex bodies remains open here.

Functional Analysis.title: Entropic hypocoercivity via the Polchinski flow: an application to the lattice sine-Gordon model
Functional Analysis.summary: We develop a multiscale criterion for exponential decay of relative entropy in the canonical stochastic quantization of lattice field theories, the underdamped Langevin dynamics of the field and its momentum. For smooth bounded perturbations of Gaussian fields, the criterion requires the uniform operator-norm bound on the smoothed interaction Hessian along the Polchinski flow of Bauerschmidt and Bodineau to have a small $L^2$ norm in the scale variable. The decay constants depend only on this $L^2$ norm and the friction. The proof measures the transfer of momentum dissipation to position on the same scales that decompose entropy. A phase-space extension of the Polchinski flow gives Gaussian coarse-graining that commutes with free kinetic evolution. Integrating position--momentum cross terms over these scales yields a corrector bounded by entropy. A force defect accounts for changes in the averaged interaction force away from equilibrium; its evolution in scale controls the errors in the kinetic estimate. For the massive two-dimensional lattice sine--Gordon model with $0<β<4π$ and small dimensionless local coupling, the criterion gives entropy decay for all finite-entropy initial laws, uniformly in the lattice spacing and the volume. For friction proportional to the mass $m$, the rate has optimal order $m$.

Functional Analysis.title: Characterizations of the unit vector basis of $c_0$ or $\ell_p$ among minimal systems
Functional Analysis.summary: Given a minimal system E for a Banach space X, Casazza, Dilworth, Kutzarova and Motakis introduced a multiplication $\otimes$ on span(E) and studied the Schauder bases for which $\|x \otimes y\|\approx \|x\|\|y\|$ asking whether every such basis is equivalent to the canonical unit vector basis of $c_0$ or $\ell_p$. We continue this study in the more general setting of minimal systems that are not assumed to be Schauder bases, and we obtain positive answers under hypotheses that are formally weaker than the ones considered so far: partial democracy instead of democracy or bidemocracy, and truncation quasi-greediness instead of quasi-greediness. Along the way we show that the above multiplicative estimate forces invariance under translations, we characterize when such a minimal system is a Schauder basis, and we give examples showing that the one-sided variants of the estimate behave very differently.

Functional Analysis.title: Hyper-dual group inverse: existence, characterizations, and applications
Functional Analysis.summary: Motivated by the recent work of Xiao and Zhong [AIMS Math. 9 (2024), 35125--35150: MR4840882], we propose a generalized inverse for a hyper-dual matrix called hyper-dual group generalized inverse (HDGGI). Firstly, we characterize the existence of the HDGGI of a hyper-dual matrix and we show that it is unique, whenever exists. The HDGGI is then used to solve a linear hyper-dual system. We discuss the minimal $P$-norm least-squares properties of hyper-dual group inverse. We also exploit some sufficient conditions under which the reverse and forward-order laws for a particular form of the HDGGI and hyper-dual Moore-Penrose generalized inverse (HDMPGI) hold. Using the definition of dual matrix of order $n$, we finally establish necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of the group inverse of a dual matrix of order $n$.
Functional Analysis.comment: We propose a generalized inverse for a hyper-dual matrix called hyper-dual group generalized inverse (HDGGI). Under certain necessary and sufficient conditions, we establish the existence of the HDGGI of a hyper-dual matrix. We then show that the HDGGI is unique (whenever exists)

Functional Analysis.title: Critical Schatten exponents for the Berger-Coburn endpoint problem
Functional Analysis.summary: Berger and Coburn showed that boundedness of a Toeplitz operator $T_g$ on the Fock space controls the heat transform $g^{(t)}$ for $1/4<t<1$, and conjectured that $T_g$ is bounded if and only if $g^{(1/4)}$ is bounded. Looi recently disproved the forward implication by constructing a bounded $T_g$ with unbounded $g^{(1/4)}$. We prove that the reverse implication also fails, even for a real-valued admissible symbol $g$ with $g^{(1/4)}\in C_0(\mathbb{C}^n)$, and that the forward implication fails even when $T_g\in S_p$ for every finite $p>1$. Our counterexamples come from Baire category and closed graph arguments, which yield no explicit symbols. Despite this two-sided failure, the forward implication has a sharp Schatten-class form: $\|g^{(1/4)}\|_\infty\le 2^n\|T_g\|_{S_1}$ for every admissible symbol $g$ with $T_g$ trace class. We show that the constant $2^n$ is optimal and that the same estimate holds with $S_p$ in place of $S_1$ for $T_g\in S_p$ when $0<p\le1$. For $p>1$, no corresponding uniform estimate holds, even for smooth compactly supported symbols. We also determine the optimal constants in the Berger--Coburn estimates for $1/4<t\le1$. Finally, for $1\le p<\infty$, we show that the equivalence $T_g\in S_p$ if and only if $g^{(1/4)}\in L^p$ holds exactly when $p=2$, answering a question of Bauer, Coburn, and Isralowitz.

Functional Analysis.title: Boundedness and continuity of phase-corrected gradients on Sobolev spaces
Functional Analysis.summary:
For a function $ψ: \mathbb{R}^d ightarrow \mathbb{C}$, we define the phase-corrected gradient $
abla_{\!\circ} ψ= |ψ|^{-1} \overlineψ\,
ablaψ$ and study the regularity of the map $ψ\mapsto 
abla_{\!\circ} ψ$ on Sobolev spaces. Since $\mathrm{Re}[
abla_{\!\circ} ψ] = 
abla |ψ|$, the phase-corrected gradient fits naturally into the framework of nonlinear composition operators. Its imaginary part $Λ= \mathrm{Im}[
abla_{\!\circ} ψ]$, on the other hand, plays a key role in quantum hydrodynamic models. We prove that $ψ\mapsto 
abla_{\!\circ} ψ$ is bounded and continuous from $W^{s,2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to $W^{s-1,2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for $1 \leq s <  rac32$, and we show that the threshold $s =  rac32$ is sharp. In particular, this answers an open question concerning the continuity of the map $ψ\mapsto |ψ|$ on Sobolev spaces. We also show that our results remain valid for functions that do not necessarily decay at infinity, a relevant setting in the context of Ginzburg--Landau theory. Finally, we extend our analysis to more general phase-corrected gradients of the form $f(|ψ|^{-1} ψ) 
abla ψ$, where $f: \mathbb{S}^1 ightarrow \mathbb{C}$ is Lipschitz, and discuss implications for certain parabolic PDEs.

Functional Analysis.title: Sharp Norm Approximation of Covering Markov Operators
Functional Analysis.summary:
We study the operator-norm approximation of Markov operators associated with finite graph coverings. Let $q:Y\to X$ be a connected covering of degree $d\geq 2$ between finite connected graphs, and let $A_q:C(Y)\to C(X)$ be its fiber-averaging operator. We show that $A_q$ is not a finite convex combination of extreme Markov operators, although such combinations approximate $A_q$ arbitrarily well in operator norm.
  We determine the exact distances from $A_q$ to convex combinations of at most $m$ extreme Markov operators, with arbitrary or equal convex weights. If $m=kd+r$, where $k\geq 0$ and $1\leq r\leq d$, these distances are
  $2(d-r+1)/[d(k(d-r+1)+1)]$
  and
  $2r(d-r+1)/(dm)$,
  respectively. Both distances are attained and depend only on the covering degree $d$ and the number of terms $m$. We also determine when equal weights are optimal and quantify the additional approximation error when they are not. Our proofs use total-variation estimates and continuous rearrangements of labelled weighted atoms. In particular, the unrestricted errors have a common scaled limit, while the equal-weight errors exhibit residue-dependent asymptotic behavior.

Functional Analysis.title: A Complex Geometric Approach to the Discrete Gabor Transform and Localization Operators on the Flat Torus
Functional Analysis.summary: In a recent paper, the discrete Gabor transform was connected to a Gabor transform with a time frequency domain given by the flat torus. We show that the corresponding Bargmann-Fock spaces can be expressed as theta functions (or equivalently line bundles on Abelian varieties). We give applications of this viewpoint to frame results for the discrete Gabor transform. In particular, we get necessary conditions which hold in higher dimensions and can expand the known results in the one dimensional case, the primary tool being the theorem of the square. We also give an application to asymptotics of restriction operators which arises via the asymptotic behavior of Bergman kernels and Toeplitz operators for high tensor powers of line bundles and find that discrete time frequency restriction operators will exhibit "plunge" behaviors similar to those of time frequency restriction operators in other contexts.
Functional Analysis.comment: 24 pages, 3rd version, Theorem B has been changed from the last version

Functional Analysis.title: Comparing positive Toeplitz operators on holomorphic and pluriharmonic Fock spaces
Functional Analysis.summary:
We prove sharp norm comparisons between positive Toeplitz operators associated with the same positive Borel measure, acting respectively on holomorphic functions and on sums of holomorphic and antiholomorphic functions, both equipped with the Gaussian-weighted $L^2$ norm. For every positive Borel measure $μ$ on $\mathbb{C}^n$ and $0<p<\infty$, both operators are compact with summable $p$th powers of their singular values (i.e. Schatten) exactly when $z\mapstoμ(B(z,r))$ belongs to $L^p(\mathbb{C}^n)$ for some fixed radius $r>0$.
  For other weights, this agreement can fail dramatically. We construct a weight $e^{-2φ}$ and a finite positive measure $μ$ on $\mathbb{C}$ for which the operator on holomorphic functions has the same singular values as with the Gaussian weight and the same measure $μ$. These values have summable $p$th powers for every $p>0$, yet the quadratic form on sums of holomorphic and antiholomorphic functions is unbounded in weighted $L^2$. The example still satisfies $Δφ=2$, as for the Gaussian choice $φ(z)=|z|^2/2$.
Functional Analysis.comment: 25 pages. v3: Streamlined exposition, with greater emphasis on the example where the holomorphic operator belongs to every Schatten class while the pluriharmonic Toeplitz form is unbounded

Functional Analysis.title: On shallow feedforward neural networks with inputs from a topological space
Functional Analysis.summary: We study feedforward neural networks with inputs from a topological space (TFNNs). We prove a universal approximation theorem for shallow TFNNs, which demonstrates their capacity to approximate any continuous function defined on this topological space. As an application, we obtain an approximative version of Kolmogorov's superposition theorem for compact metric spaces.
Functional Analysis.comment: Published version with two minor corrections. Namely, in Theorem 2.1, C(K) was replaced with C(X), and in the proof of Proposition 2.1, the formula for τ(t) was corrected. The results remain unchanged

Functional Analysis.title: The divergence of continuously differentiable vector fields
Functional Analysis.summary: For $m\geq 2$, we give a complete characterisation of the continuous functions on $\mathbb{R}^m$ that are divergences of continuously differentiable vector fields. The characterisation is formulated in terms of distributions and, equivalently, in terms of the continuous dual of a suitably topologised subspace of the Arens--Eells space. The two implications yield contrasting applications. First, there exists a compactly supported continuous function which is the divergence of a bounded Lipschitz vector field but not of any continuously differentiable vector field. Second, every continuous function whose distributional partial derivatives are locally $m$-integrable (the critical exponent for Sobolev embedding) is the divergence of a continuously differentiable vector field.

Functional Analysis.title: Compact linear combination of composition operators on weighted Bergman-Orlicz spaces induced by doubling weights
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $A^Ψ_ω(\mathbb{D})$ be the weighted Bergman-Orlicz spaces induced by doubling weights $ω$ on the unit disk $\mathbb D$. Suppose Orlicz function $Ψ$ satisfies the $Δ_{2}$-condition. In this paper, the compactness of finite linear combination of composition operators on $A^Ψ_ω(\mathbb{D})$ are completely characterized in terms of Julia-Carathéodory type conditions and vanishing Carleson measure, respectively.

Functional Analysis.title: Converse symplectic interlacing via low-rank singular value perturbations
Functional Analysis.summary: The symplectic interlacing theorem states that the symplectic spectrum of a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix satisfies a $2k$-step interlacing relation with the symplectic spectrum of every $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix. We prove the converse in this paper. More precisely, given a positive global symplectic spectrum of size $n$ and a positive local symplectic spectrum of size $n-k$ satisfying the $2k$-step interlacing inequalities, we construct a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix having the prescribed global symplectic spectrum and a $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix of it having the prescribed local symplectic spectrum. Our main tool is a reduction of $s$-principal compression to a rank-$k$ singular value perturbation. In the context of the Gaussian quantum marginal problem, our result implies that the symplectic interlacing inequalities are not merely necessary conditions on Gaussian marginals, but are also the complete spectral compatibility conditions for the global-versus-local-mode marginal problem.

Functional Analysis.title: Unique direct-sum decompositions of infinite-dimensional unitary representations of the infinite dihedral group via real CMV matrices
Functional Analysis.summary:
Unitary representations of the infinite dihedral group arise naturally and play an important role in a wide range of areas including mathematics, physics, and engineering. CMV matrices, introduced by Cantero, Moral, and Velázquez, are five-diagonal unitary matrices that are standard tools in the theory of orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle. It is known that every unitary representation of the infinite dihedral group on a separable Hilbert space admits a discrete direct-sum decomposition into representations arising from the natural factorizations of real CMV matrices and copies of two exceptional one-dimensional irreducible representations.
  We prove that such a decomposition is unique up to unitary equivalence when the summands arising from real CMV matrices are grouped according to their multiplicities and the spectral measures of the corresponding matrices are mutually singular across distinct multiplicities. Furthermore, we show that the representation associated with each such real CMV matrix $C$ admits a direct integral decomposition into irreducible unitary representations with respect to the push-forward of the restriction of the spectral measure of $C$ to the closed upper half circle.
  These results make it possible to study the structure of unitary representations of the infinite dihedral group using CMV matrices and the theory of orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle.

Functional Analysis.title: Ubiquity in the setting of forward-reverse Brascamp-Lieb inequalities
Functional Analysis.summary: The ubiquity of geometric Brascamp-Lieb data, which refers to a certain density property of geometric data within the set of all feasible Brascamp-Lieb data, has recently been studied. Motivated in part by a question of Bennett-Tao concerning a possible connection or analogue of the adjoint Brascamp-Lieb inequality to the forward-reverse Brascamp-Lieb inequality, we establish ubiquity in the forward-reverse setting. Our proof takes an analytic approach and, to overcome the difficulties arising in extending ubiquity to the forward-reverse setting, makes use of tools from the calculus of variations such as Danskin's theorem and Ekeland's variational principle.
Functional Analysis.comment: 12 pages. The main result has been extended to the setting of the forward-reverse Brascamp-Lieb inequality

Functional Analysis.title: Multilinear extrapolation on Banach function spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We solve an open problem on the multilinear Rubio de Francia extrapolation on Banach function spaces. The first result states that, under the assumption of boundedness of the multisublinear Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator, the multivariable boundedness on Banach function spaces can be extrapolated from some weighted Lebesgue space, including the cases where some exponents may be infinite. Under the same assumption, the second result asserts that if a multilinear operator is bounded on some weighted Lebesgue space, then its compactness can be extrapolated from some unweighted Lebesgue space to Banach function spaces. Our results do not require any convexity or concavity conditions on Banach function spaces. The main ingredients in the proof are a multilinear version of the Rubio de Francia algorithm, a stopping-time argument, convex analysis, and a compactness criterion on Banach function spaces. As applications of extrapolation theorems, we obtain multilinear extrapolation for the boundedness and compactness of commutators on Banach function spaces. These results can be further applied to specific operators, which cover both the full range case including multilinear Calderón-Zygmund operators, multilinear pseudo-differential operators, and bilinear paraproducts, and the limited range case including the bilinear Hilbert transform, multilinear rough singular integrals, and bilinear oscillatory Fourier multipliers.

Functional Analysis.title: From one particle to N particles: uniform transport-information and log-Sobolev inequalities for Coulomb gases on the torus
Functional Analysis.summary: We study how a functional inequality satisfied by the one-particle conditional distributions of a Gibbs measure, with a constant independent of the positions of the other particles, can be propagated to the whole N -particle system, with a constant independent of N , when the interaction is singular. Our model is the Coulomb gas on the torus T 3 in the mean-field regime. We distinguish two mechanisms. The first one is a dependent tensorization, governed by Dobrushin-Wu interdependence coefficients. It yields uniform Poincar{é} and transport-information W 2 I inequalities with fully explicit constants. We explain why this mechanism does not extend to the log-Sobolev inequality: the Zegarlinski-type coefficients, which require pointwise bounds on the interaction, are infinite. The second mechanism is a tensorization with a defect. Using a uniform bound on the partition function due to Duerinckx and Jabin, it yields a uniform log-Sobolev inequality for the Coulomb gas on T 3 at small charge. We identify the assumptions on the interaction under which each mechanism applies. All the results are then extended to the two-dimensional Coulomb gas and to periodic Riesz gases 1/|x|^s , 0 < s $\le$ 1. The extension to d $\ge$ 4 is also discussed.

Functional Analysis.title: Revisiting the Schwarz Lemma for the Pentablock: Counterexamples and Sharp Interpolation Criteria
Functional Analysis.summary: Alshehri and Lykova (\emph{J. Geom. Anal.} \textbf{33} (2023)) formulated a Schwarz lemma for the pentablock $P$, giving a criterion for the existence of an analytic map from the unit disc $\mathbb D$ into the closed pentablock $\overline P$ that sends the origin to the origin and a prescribed point $λ_0\in\mathbb D$ to a given point $x_0\in\overline P$. We show that the sufficiency direction of their criterion is false. We identify the underlying error as the extension to the open unit disc of a Fejér--Riesz identity that is valid only on the unit circle. We establish a corrected necessary and sufficient interpolation criterion when the last two components are prescribed by a fixed rational $Γ$-inner function and resolve the special case $s_0=0$. Using the Poisson integral representation of the associated outer spectral factor, we obtain a sharp comparison between the corrected bound and the bound proposed by Alshehri and Lykova, with a precise characterization of equality. We further express the logarithmic difference between these bounds as a nonnegative Green potential, thereby quantifying the discrepancy in terms of the derivative of the first coordinate of the prescribed $Γ$-inner function. Finally, we formulate a variational problem over rational $Γ$-inner interpolants satisfying the prescribed two-point conditions. We show that the supremum of the associated outer-factor quantities determines the maximal admissible modulus of the first coordinate among pentablock-valued interpolants whose last two components belong to this class. Equivalently, this extremal problem reduces to minimizing the corresponding Green potential. We conclude by discussing the remaining problem of characterizing unrestricted Schwarz interpolation for the pentablock and its connection with the Lempert function.
Functional Analysis.comment: This is the initial version. Final version will submit soon

Functional Analysis.title: The norm reveals projections in the positive unit sphere of an arbitrary C*-algebra
Functional Analysis.summary: We show how a simple metric condition in terms of the C$^*$-norm of an arbitrary C$^*$-algebra $A$ can be employed to determine those norm-one positive elements which are projections. Concretely, if we write $S_{A^+}$ for the intersection of the positive cone and the unit sphere of $A$, we establish that an element $a \in S_{A^+}$ is a projection if, and only if, $$\{a\} = \left\{x\in S_{A^+}: \|x-z\| = 1 \hbox{ for all } z\in S_{A^+}\hbox{ with } \|a-z\|=1 \right\}.$$ This proves a conjecture which has been previously confirmed for von Neumann algebras and unital C$^*$-algebras. In the setting of not necessarily unital JB$^*$-algebras, the Shirshov--Cohn theorem is invoked to obtain a similar metric characterisation of projections. In the wider setting of JB$^*$-triples, we show how a metric characterisation in terms of inner ideals can be established to determine non-zero tripotents.

Functional Analysis.title: New thoughts on fractional Sobolev spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We introduce the concept of a fractional upper gradient and employ it to characterize the $p$-Muckenhoupt weighted $s$-fractional $p$-Sobolev spaces on $\mathbb R^d$ where $d\in\mathbb N$, $1<p<\infty$ and $0<s<1$.

Functional Analysis.title: The Serre closure of Banach spaces
Functional Analysis.summary:
We determine the Serre closure of Banach spaces in the category of quasi-Banach spaces, that is, the smallest class of quasi-Banach spaces that contains all Banach spaces and is stable under subspaces, quotients, and extensions. Precisely, a quasi-Banach space $X$ belongs to this closure if and only if there exist constants $M$ and $k\in\mathbb N$ such that $$ \frac{\|x_1+\dots+x_n\|}{\|x_1\|+\dots+\|x_n\|}\leq M\log^k n $$ for every $n\geq 2$ and every $x_1,\dots,x_n\in X$; equivalently, $X$ is a quotient of an Orlicz sequence space $\ell(I,f_l)$, where $I$ is an index set and $f_l(t)$ is equivalent to $t\log^l(1/t)$ near zero.
  The proof combines geometrical estimates for quasi-Banach spaces and quasilinear maps with the study of higher order derived spaces associated to complex interpolation between $\ell_{2/3}$ and $\ell_2$. We provide examples of spaces in the Serre closure of Banach spaces that are not iterated extensions of Banach spaces and discuss some related problems.

Functional Analysis.title: $π$-Properties, Uniformly Convexity and Uniform Ball Coverings Properties
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we prove a sufficient condition for the uniform ball-covering property of closed operator subspaces invariant under selected truncations. We use uniform convexity of the range space and near-contractive finite-rank projection approximations to obtain quantitative coverings with finite-rank centres whenever the truncated images are separable. A weak-star version gives the same covering parameters for quotients by arbitrary weak-star closed subspaces. In the completely bounded setting, the covering parameters are independent of the matrix level. In particular, the duals of all closed subspaces of $S_1(\ell_2)$ admit coverings with centre norm $2$ and radius $1+\varepsilon$, for $0<\varepsilon<1$, at every matrix level. Applications include operator-valued Schur multipliers and, for $1<p<\infty$, prescribed-support Fourier multipliers on countable amenable groups and finitely generated free groups. The Fourier coverings have finite-support centres in the given operator or completely bounded norms. An endpoint example shows failure of the ball-covering property at $p=1,\infty$.

Functional Analysis.title: A point-free theory of quantitative homogenization
Functional Analysis.summary:
We introduce a purely operator-theoretic framework for quantitative
  homogenization that bypasses the traditional reliance on large-scale
  spatial regularity and probabilistic assumptions. Inspired by
  Tartar's vision of a point-free theory, we derive explicit norm
  resolvent estimates using only the algebraic structure of multiscale
  operators and the abstract geometry of Hilbert spaces. In this
  framework, the effective macroscopic dynamics and the abstract
  corrector emerge naturally from an orthogonal decomposition of the
  state space, governed algebraically by a Schur complement. To
  quantify the convergence rate, we introduce a frequency-splitting
  technique and a flux corrector obtained by inverting the microscopic
  derivative on the residual field; this controls the error for
  regular macroscopic data in terms of explicit,
  $\varepsilon$-independent operator norms.
  This abstract perspective places on one footing stationary,
  non-stationary, periodic, quasi-periodic, and stochastic
  homogenization. We demonstrate that the physical distinctions
  between these media---and their respective convergence rates---are
  captured by the behavior of the spectral measure of the microscopic
  derivative operator, evaluated on the residual field, near zero
  frequency; in the periodic case the rate $O(\varepsilon)$ is proved,
  while in the stochastic case the rates are conditional on a
  density-of-states hypothesis. Furthermore, our results apply for
  multiscale systems that do not uphold subadditivity of energy
  quantities or do not have a well-defined Brillouin zone.
Functional Analysis.comment: 62 pages. New results and details are added. Several errors are addressed

Functional Analysis.title: Uniform decay of function norms
Functional Analysis.summary: We introduce and study two new relations between function spaces over measure spaces of infinite measure, motivated by the question of establishing compactness. The first relation captures the uniform decay of function (quasi-)norms ``at infinity''. It appeared implicitly in the first author's recent work on the compactness of Sobolev embeddings of radially symmetric functions on $\mathbb{R}^n$. The second is a suitably localized version of the relation of almost-compact embeddings, which has been successfully used to study compactness in function spaces over measure spaces of finite measure, but becomes of no use in the case of infinite measure. Our framework is that of quasi-Banach function spaces, which need not be normable or rearrangement invariant. This level of generality leads us to introduce the notion of extremal fundamental functions associated with a (quasi-)Banach function space. We provide several concrete examples and establish an abstract compactness principle involving the new relations. Finally, we demonstrate a possible application of this principle to embeddings of inhomogeneous Sobolev spaces on $\mathbb{R}^n$.
Functional Analysis.comment: 37 pages, published in the Journal of Geometric Analysis

Functional Analysis.title: Comparisons of benchmark equivalence relations
Functional Analysis.summary:
We determine the Borel-reducibility comparison of each pair of $\mathbfΠ^0_3$ benchmark equivalence relations in Gao's monograph. The additional comparisons we prove are $E_\infty\leq_B c_0$, $E_\infty
leq_B\ell_p$ for $2<p<\infty$, $\ell_p
leq_B{\equiv_m}$ for $2<p<\infty$, $c_0
leq_B{\equiv_m}$, $c_0
leq_B\ell_\infty^+$ and $\equiv_m
leq_B\ell_\infty^+$. Together with the previous positive direction, these give $\ell_p\leq_B{\equiv_m}$ if and only if $p\leq2$. These answer several questions in Gao's monograph and Kanovei' monograph. We also prove that unitary equivalence of all bounded linear operators is not Borel reducible to $\equiv_m$. This answers a question of Ding and Gao. Equivalently, unitary equivalence of arbitrary representations of $F_\infty$ is strictly more complicated than that of arbitrary representations of $\mathbb Z$. This answers a question of Thomas.

Functional Analysis.title: $DW$-$L$-Weakly Compact Operators Between Banach Lattices
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper we introduce a class of operators which we call $DW$-$L$-weakly compact operators. They carry disjointly weakly compact subsets of a Banach lattice onto $L$-weakly compact sets. The class of $DW$-$L$-weakly compact operators is closely related to two recently introduced classes of operators: almost $L$-weakly compact operators and order $L$-weakly compact operators. We show that $DW$-$L$-weakly compact operators are precisely those operators which are both almost $L$-weakly compact and order $L$-weakly compact. The adjoint and the order structure of $DW$-$L$-weakly compact operators are also considered.

Functional Analysis.title: Normalised Hamiltonian Elliptic Systems: a Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality for bilinear mass
Functional Analysis.summary: We study Hamiltonian elliptic systems with prescribed bilinear mass $\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}uv=a>0$. We establish a Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality in the crossed gradient pairing and bilinear mass, on scaling-invariant component-bounded classes. It identifies the critical curve $1/p+1/q=N/(N+2)$ and the restricted energy trichotomy. For power nonlinearities, we establish uniqueness up to common translations and nondegeneracy of positive profiles throughout the Sobolev-subcritical hyperbola. Exact scaling then classifies positive normalised solutions and identifies the unique critical mass. In dimension two, we develop a bilinear exponential Gagliardo--Nirenberg estimate with a sharp gradient threshold and a truncated scalar refinement with the optimal quartic leading coefficient. Adapting variational ideas from [Cassani-Tarsi, Calc.Var.PDE (2015)] we combine a mass-normalising quotient, reduction over the full negative fibres and compactness below the concentration threshold to obtain least-energy positive radial solutions for pure exponential nonlinearities at every prescribed mass below the cubic limiting mass. Local perturbative branches and a small-frequency exponential branch yield explicit mass-response formulas.

Functional Analysis.title: Minimum attaining operators on reducing subspaces: Spectral structure and density
Functional Analysis.summary:
In this article, we introduce and study the class $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ of minimum attaining operators on a separable Hilbert space $H$ whose restrictions to every nonzero reducing subspace are minimum attaining. This class lies between the classes of absolutely minimum attaining operators and minimum attaining operators. We establish a spectral characterization of positive operators in $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$: a positive operator $T$ belongs to $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ if and only if $T=\sum_{λ\inΛ}λP_λ$, where $Λ\subseteq[0,\|T\|]$ is a countable well-ordered set, $(P_λ)_{λ\inΛ}$ is a family of mutually orthogonal nonzero projections, and $\sum_{λ\inΛ}P_λ=I$ in the strong operator topology.
  We also establish a connection between $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ and the class of operators attaining their norm on every nonzero reducing subspace. Further, we obtain stability results under suitable finite-rank and compact perturbations, and prove that $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ is norm dense in $\mathcal{B}(H)$. We also establish the norm density of operators in this class having a nontrivial invariant half-space. Finally, we characterize normal operators in $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$, obtain a corresponding characterization for multiplication operators on $L^2(\mathbb{T})$, and characterize the condition $\mathcal{R}_T=\mathcal{R}_{|T|}$ in terms of the von Neumann algebra generated by $|T|$, showing that this condition forces $T$ to be normal.
Functional Analysis.comment: Submitted to a journal. Some of the earlier results modified. Comments and suggestions are welcome

Functional Analysis.title: Group-Frames for Banach Spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: In the literature, frames generated by unitary representations of groups (known as group-frames) have been studied only for Hilbert spaces. We conduct the first study of frames for Banach spaces generated by isometrically invertible representations of discrete groups on Banach spaces. These frames are characterized using left-regular and right-regular representations, Gram matrices, and group matrices on classical sequence spaces. A sufficiently large collection of functional-vector pairs using the double commutant of the representation is identified to generate group-frames for Banach spaces. Subsequently, we study Schauder frames generated by time-frequency shift operators on finite-dimensional Banach spaces. We derive the Moyal formula, the fundamental identity of Gabor analysis, the Wexler-Raz criterion, and the Ron-Shen duality in functional form.

Functional Analysis.title: Morse theory methods for a class of quasi-linear elliptic systems of higher order
Functional Analysis.summary: We develop the local Morse theory for a class of non-twice continuously differentiable functionals on Hilbert spaces, including a new generalization of the Gromoll-Meyer's splitting theorem and a weaker Marino-Prodi perturbation type result. They are applicable to a wide range of multiple integrals with quasi-linear elliptic Euler equations and systems of higher order.
Functional Analysis.comment: Differences between this version and the published version [Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations 58 (2019), no. 4, Paper No. 134] are as follows: in addition to the passage from inequalities (2.7)-(2.8) through the end of the proof of Lemma 2.10, several typographical errors in other parts of the paper have also been corrected

Functional Analysis.title: Measure Convergence under Weak Domination for Unitarily Invariant Norms on Finite von Neumann Algebras
Functional Analysis.summary: The classical Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem (DCT) is a cornerstone in commutative measure theory, while its extension to the noncommutative setting has remained a longstanding challenge due to the barriers posed by the noncommutative structure. Let \(α\) be a unitarily invariant norm defined on a diffuse tracial von Neumann algebra \((\mathcal{M}, τ)\), let $L^α(\mathcal M, τ)$ be the completion of $\mathcal M$ with respect to the norm $α$(which includes all $L^p(\mathcal M, τ)$ as special cases). In this paper, by replacing ``almost everywhere convergence" with Nelson's convergence in measure, we establish a noncommutative analog of the dominated convergence theorem for $L^α(\mathcal M, τ)$ under a { significantly weaker dominating condition} than those previously considered. For instance, in a \(II_1\) factor \(\mathcal{M}\), if \(P\) is a projection with \(τ(P)=\frac{1}{n}\), then \(n^2 P\) ``dominates" every operator of norm \(\leq n\). As an application, we obtain a complete characterization of center-preserving $*$-automorphism of finite von Neumann algebras, which unifies and extends the earlier works of Kadison and Haagerup on the structure of automorphisms.

Functional Analysis.title: Hausdorff content $A_p$ weights: weighted maximal inequalities and fundamental structural properties
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $\mathcal H_{\infty}^δ$ denote the Hausdorff content of dimension $δ\in(0,n]$ defined on subsets of $\mathbb R^n$. The principal problem, considered in this paper, is to characterize the non-negative function $w$ for which the weighted $L^p$ inequality with $p\in(1,\infty)$ and the weighted weak $L^1$ inequality on Hardy-Littlewood maximal operators associated with Hausdorff content hold true. To achieve this, we introduce a class of Hausdorff content $A_p$ weights, denoted as $\mathcal A_{p,δ}$, and then show that, for any $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $δ\in(0,n]$, the weighted $L^p$ maximal inequality holds true if and only if $w\in\mathcal A_{p,δ}$, and the weighted weak $L^1$ maximal inequality holds true if and only if $w\in\mathcal A_{1,δ}$ by proposing a novel approach. As the second objective, applying this approach, the seminal structural properties of classical Muckenhoupt $A_p$ weights, such as the reverse Hölder inequality [R. R. Coifman and C. Fefferman, Studia Math. 51 (1974), 241-250], the self-improving property [B. Muckenhoupt, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 165 (1972), 207-226], and Jones' factorization theorem [P. W. Jones, Ann. of Math. (2) 111 (1980), 511-530], are all established for $\mathcal A_{p,δ}$. The main novelties of this paper lies in: (i) we discover $\mathcal A_{p,δ}$ weights with rich structural properties, that increase strictly on dimension exponent and hence reduce to the classical $A_p$ class at the endpoint dimension, forming proper subsets of it for smaller dimension exponent; (ii) by proposing a novel approach, this work naturally extends the classical theory beyond measure-theoretic frameworks, while also provides novel insights even when reduced to the classical $A_p$ weight case.

Functional Analysis.title: Wehrl-type entropy problem for compact connected semisimple Lie groups
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $G$ be a compact connected semisimple Lie group, and let $π:G\to U(V_λ)$ be a finite-dimensional irreducible unitary representation associated with the highest weight $λ$. We prove that coherent projectors are the unique minimizers of the Wehrl entropy over all density matrices on $V_λ$. Similar extremal properties hold for power functions in place of the entropy function. The proof uses a second variation at the extremizer by perturbation in directions associated with Killing fields, similar to the strategy of Frank and Lieb used in \cite{FrankLieb}. Then the problem reduces to the uncertainty principle characterizing coherent states. This solves the Wehrl-type entropy problem for arbitrary compact connected semisimple Lie groups.
Functional Analysis.comment: 11 pages. Reformulated the proof using minimum uncertainty. Simplified some arguments. Updated the exposition and references

Functional Analysis.title: Isometric Theory for Greedy-Type Properties with Enlarged Greedy Sums
Functional Analysis.summary: For a semi-normalized Markushevich basis, we study isometric almost-greedy inequalities in which a greedy sum of $φ(m)$ terms is compared with coordinate projections onto at most $m$ terms. Here $φ$ is any strictly increasing map of the nonnegative integers into themselves with $φ(0)=0$. We sandwich $φ$-almost greediness with constant $1$ ($φ$-AG$_1$) between two levels of symmetry for largest coefficients (SLC): $$φ\mbox{-SLC}_1\ \Longrightarrow\ φ\mbox{-AG}_1\ \Longrightarrow\ \mbox{weak }φ\mbox{-SLC}_1.$$ Both implications are equivalences if and only if $φ(1)\le2$. We then characterize $φ$-AG$_1$ by the weighted weak $φ$-SLC or a single homogeneous norm inequality, called Property $(F_φ)$.

Functional Analysis.title: Löwner equations and de Branges--Rovnyak spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We study one-parameter families of de Branges--Rovnyak spaces associated with the radial and chordal Löwner equations. Our approach is based on a little-known technique developed by the de Branges school. In this paper, we recast this technique in the theory of direct integrals and integral operators. As an application, we prove Fourier-type expansion theorems induced by the Löwner equations and give answers to a problem posed by Fricain--Hartmann--Ross.

Functional Analysis.title: A fractional modular Poincaré--Wirtinger-type inequality in Sobolev spaces with variable exponents
Functional Analysis.summary:
Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain and let $p:Ω\to[1,\infty)$ be a measurable, essentially bounded exponent; no regularity of $p$ -- in particular, no log-Hölder continuity -- is assumed. For a general non-negative measurable kernel $\mathcal{K}(x,y)$ admitting a radial bounding function $κ(x,r)$ in the second variable, we establish the fractional modular Poincaré--Wirtinger-type inequality $$
  \iint_{Ω\timesΩ}\mathcal{K}(x,y)\,|u(x)-u(y)|^{p(x)} d y\, d x
  \leqslant C\int_Ωc(x)\left(\int_Ω
  \frac{|\nabla u(z)|^{p(x)}}{|z-x|^{n-1+θ}}\, d z\right) d x, $$ valid for every $u\in W^{1,1}(Ω)$, in particular every $u\in W^{1,p(\cdot)}(Ω)$, and every $θ\in[0,1)$. Here $$ c(x)=\int_0^{D}r^{n+p(x)-2+θ}κ(x,r)\,d r, $$ $D$ is the diameter of any fixed ball containing $\overlineΩ$, and the constant $C$ depends only on $n,p^+,θ$ and the fixed domain $Ω$. For the fractional kernel $\mathcal{K}(x,y)=|x-y|^{-n-λp(x)}$ we obtain a variable-exponent Gagliardo-modular estimate. The proof replaces the starshaped chain decompositions used there by a combination of a Morrey-type estimate on starshaped domains, a positive-kernel proof of weighted Poincaré inequalities, and one reflection extension for the weights $|z-x|^{-(n-1+θ)}$. The constants are uniform down to exponent $1$, and the inequalities are understood in the extended nonnegative sense when either side is infinite.

Functional Analysis.title: An Ellipse Criterion for Exact Nonuniqueness in the Planar Interior Radon Problem
Functional Analysis.summary: We characterize exact nonuniqueness in the planar interior Radon problem for arbitrary pairs of open convex sets. There exists a nonzero smooth function compactly supported in the first set whose integral over every line meeting the second set vanishes if and only if an ellipse contains the closure of the second set and is compactly contained in the first set. The same criterion holds for a nonzero $L^1$ function whose essential support is compactly contained in the first set and whose Radon transform vanishes almost everywhere on those lines. For concentric open squares, the criterion gives the sharp threshold $1/\sqrt2$ for the inner-to-outer half-side ratio. This yields counterexamples to Conjecture 1.2 of Boman (2021) and to Theorem 40.1 of Boman (2025).

Functional Analysis.title: Finite-Branch Multipliers on a Hölder Algebra: Commutants, Norm Closures, and Essential Spectra
Functional Analysis.summary: Noninjective multiplication symbols allow commuting operators to mix function values along their fibers, while Hölder regularity constrains this mixing at branch points. We study these operators on the Banach algebra $A_β$, $0<β<1$, defined by a restricted interval-variation condition. For $u(t)=t(1-t)$, we determine the full commutant $\{M_u\}'=\mathscr C_β$, including operators whose reflection coefficients need not belong to $A_β$. Separately, we characterize the operator-norm closure $J_β$ of the regular multiplication--reflection subalgebra of $\mathscr C_β$, obtain two-sided norm-distance estimates, and find a complemented copy of $\ell^\infty/c_0$ in the Banach-space quotient $\mathscr C_β/J_β$. Every $T\in\mathscr C_β$ satisfies $σ(T)=σ_{\mathrm{ap}}(T)=σ_{\mathrm{usf}}(T)=σ_{\mathrm{ess}}(T)$, and Fredholmness is equivalent to invertibility. For multipliers with finitely many full bi-Lipschitz branches, we also characterize their full commutants and establish the same spectral equalities for every commuting operator. For the regular finite-branch algebra, we establish an exact norm-closure criterion using weighted local Hölder defects and separate row-difference conditions, even when several folds share a level.

Functional Analysis.title: Kwapień's property (K) in Lipschitz-free spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove that a Lipschitz-free space $\F(M)$ fails Kwapień's property (K) whenever its underlying metric space $M$ contains a bi-Lipschitz copy of $C\times K$, where $C\subset\R$ is closed with positive measure and $K$ contains a Cantor metric space. Consequently, this holds for every subset of $\R^n$, $n\geqslant2$, whose closure has positive measure, and for a compact planar set of Assouad dimension one. These Lipschitz-free spaces embed into no strongly weakly compactly generated space and no $L_1$-space; in the separable case their duals are not isomorphic to $\ell_\infty$. Combining our result with a decomposition of Aliaga and Medina, we show that $\F(\R^n\times\Z^m)$ is strongly weakly compactly generated if and only if it has (K), and this occurs precisely when $n\leqslant1$. In particular, $\F(\R^2)$ does not embed isomorphically into $\F(\R\times\Z)$, answering a question of Aliaga. The planar examples nevertheless have the Dunford--Pettis property and Pełczyński's property $(V^*)$ and are weakly sequentially complete.

Functional Analysis.title: Actions of acylindrically hyperbolic groups on $\ell^1$
Functional Analysis.summary: We construct explicit affine uniformly Lipschitz actions on $\ell^1$ for certain groups with hyperbolic features. For acylindrically hyperbolic groups, our actions have unbounded orbits, while for residually finite hyperbolic groups and for mapping class groups, the actions have proper orbits, with the induced $\ell^1$-metric quasi-isometric (respectively, almost quasi-isometric, up to a logarithmic factor) to the word metric. This allows us to construct proper continuous affine uniformly Lipschitz actions on $L^1$, with undistorted orbits, for all simple groups of real rank one.

Functional Analysis.title: A note on the Besov spaces ${\rm B}_1^{Φ_2}$
Functional Analysis.summary: Regarding the Besov space ${\rm B}_1^{Φ_2}$, defined by S. Geiss and Ylinen (Memoirs AMS 1335, 2021) by a coupling method, we prove for $ξ\in{\rm B}_1^{Φ_2} \cap L_2$ a distributional estimate in terms of the Lorentz-Zygmund space $L_{1,\infty}(\ln L)^{-1}$ for the Malliavin derivative ${\rm D}(T_uξ)$ uniformly in $u>0$, where $(T_u)_{u\ge }$ is the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semi-group. Here $ξ$ is not necessarily Malliavin differentiable in the ${\rm D}_{1,1}$-sense. This provides for Theorem 4.22 of the aforementioned reference an extension to the borderline case $p=1$.

Functional Analysis.title: Hyperbolicity Beyond Convexity in the Alexandrov-Fenchel Inequality
Functional Analysis.summary: We establish an Alexandrov--Fenchel type inequality in which one of the reference bodies is replaced by a function whose Hessian satisfies a balancing condition on its eigenvalues, without being required to be positive semidefinite. The proof hinges on a new extension of Alexandrov's inequality for mixed discriminants. As applications, we derive a log-concavity principle for linear functionals of area measures, answering a question of Colesanti, Hug, and Saorín-Gómez, as well as Brunn--Minkowski type inequalities for intrinsic volumes of mean section bodies, answering a question of Schuster.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Inhomogeneous Kinetic FPUT Equation near Rayleigh-Jeans Equilibria
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the nonlinear dynamics of the spatially inhomogeneous kinetic wave equation associated with the FPUT-$β$ problem. We prove global-in-time well-posedness near nonsingular Rayleigh-Jeans equilibria and their asymptotic stability in particular in weighted $L^\infty$ norms in space and momentum, for small initial perturbations orthogonal to the collision kernel at almost every spatial point. We describe the spectrum near the origin at small spatial frequencies, identifying two simple eigenvalues with fractional and diffusive orders $|ξ|^{8/5}$ and $ξ^2$, respectively. Combining this spectral analysis with energy estimates taking into account the transport effect, we establish algebraic decay for the linear semigroup despite the absence of a spectral gap for the collision operator. We then use these estimates to obtain nonlinear stability.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Asymptotic Geometry of Shifting Superlevel Sets for Elliptic Dirichlet Problems: Normal Decomposition, Geometric Energy, and Discrete Reflection Dynamics
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study elliptic superlevel geometry and return dynamics for the class $\mathcal{O}_{C}$. Let $C \subset \mathbb{R}^{N}$ be a compact strictly convex core, and $Ω\in \mathcal{O}_{C}$ a bounded domain whose boundary is a global normal graph over $\partial C$ with inward normals returning to $\operatorname{int} C$. For $-Δu = f$ in $Ω$ ($u=0$ on $\partialΩ$), with $f \geq 0$, $f \not\equiv 0$, $\operatorname{supp} f \Subset \operatorname{int} C$, we analyze the superlevel sets $Ω_{t} = \{u > t\}$ for $t \downarrow 0$.
  We prove that for small $t > 0$, $\partialΩ_{t}$ is a global normal graph given by $\partialΩ_{t} = \{c + d_{t}(c)ν(c) : c \in \partial C\}$, satisfying $\|d_{t} - d_{0}\|_{C^{1}} = O(t)$ and $d_{t} = d_{0} - t b_{0} + o_{C^{1}}(t)$, where $b_{0}$ depends on the Hopf derivative and transversality. Using normal-graph formulas, we show $Ω_{t} \in \mathcal{O}_{C}$.
  The return maps $F_{t} : \partial C \to \partial C$ are well-defined, satisfying $\|F_{t} - F_{0}\|_{L^{\infty}} = O(t)$ and $F_{t} = F_{0} + t \mathcal{A}_{0} + o_{L^{\infty}}(t)$. For any sequence $t_{n} \downarrow 0$, the non-autonomous system $x_{n+1} = F_{t_{n}}(x_{n})$ is asymptotically autonomous with background map $F_{0}$. These results bridge elliptic boundary-layer deformation and return-map dynamics relative to a convex core.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Long-time action stability for perturbed KdV near finite-gap tori
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove action and spectral stability near finite-gap tori of the periodic Korteweg--de Vries equation under autonomous analytic Hamiltonian perturbations of size $\varepsilon$. The estimates are uniform over prescribed compact families, without small-amplitude or nonresonance assumptions, and allow nearby initial data with infinitely many open gaps. Assuming a strong solution and a uniform higher Sobolev bound on $[0,T_0/\varepsilon]$, we permit one-derivative loss in the perturbing Hamiltonian's normal gradient. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ and initial normal Birkhoff size $r_0$, the tangential action variations and weighted sum of normal actions are bounded by $C_δ(r_0^2+\varepsilon^{2δ})$, while the spectral-gap variation in $\ell^2$ is bounded by $C_δ(r_0+\varepsilon^δ)$, for every $0<δ<1/4$. A key ingredient is coercivity of the negative Hessian of the nonlinear KdV Hamiltonian on the full $\ell^2$ action space at every finite-gap action. We combine this with resonance analysis and corrected action observables evaluated along the solution. The hypotheses are verified for several local and nonlocal Hamiltonian perturbations.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Scattering for the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map and the Steklov spectrum
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We develop scattering theory for Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) maps on asymptotically conic, unbounded domains $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^d$, that are only Lipschitz inside a compact set and whose boundary extends to infinity. Specifically, we prove a limiting absorption principle and demonstrate existence of the scattering matrix.
  As an application of the theory, we show that the eigenvalues of Steklov-type problems on curvilinear polygons, $\mathcal{P}$, are well approximated by the eigenvalues of a Dirac operator on $\partial\mathcal{P}$ whose transmission coefficients between edges meeting at a corner are given by the scattering matrix for DtN maps on asymptotically conic domains associated to the corners. Up to an arbitrary loss in the power of the eigenvalue, the error in the approximation is optimal among all possible asymptotics that use only local information about $\partial\mathcal{P}$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Existence of static axisymmetric solutions to the Einstein equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct smooth Riemannian metrics and scalar potentials that are invariant under a circle action and satisfy the static Einstein equations with positive cosmological constant. The underlying compact three-manifold is a ball with two disjoint open balls removed. The potential (or lapse function) is positive in the interior and vanishes at the boundary, consisting of three non-degenerate horizons. The areas of the two inner boundary components are controlled by two arbitrary parameters, namely the masses of the black holes, which are taken to be sufficiently small and comparable. Each inner horizon radius scales linearly with the individual mass parameters, while the separation of their reference centers scales as the cube root of the total mass. These two scales are assumed to be sufficiently small at different rates, whereas the cosmological length remains fixed. The main analytical challenge is to control the linearized equation and the nonlinear remainder simultaneously near the shrinking horizons, between the centers and in the outer region. Weighted Hölder estimates quantify the growth of the inverse and show that the error of an approximation joining Kottler collars to de Sitter space is small enough to close a contraction argument. Namely, we solve a reduced elliptic Einstein equation that is endowed with two obstruction tensors; varying the two axial positions removes their coefficients. The contracted Bianchi identity and an energy estimate for an auxiliary vector field (Killing field) introduced by the projection to vanish. Finally, for a fixed cosmological constant, the intrinsic metric of one of the two boundary components is sufficient to determine a static solution with simply connected interior and non-vanishing boundary gradient, up to isometry and multiplication of the potential by a positive constant.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Existence and Uniqueness of Local and Global Solutions for a Partial Differential-Algebraic Equation of Index One
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we use the theory of nonlinear semigroups to establish the existence and uniqueness of both local and global solutions for a partial differential-algebraic equation (PDAE) of index one. This method is applied to a reaction-diffusion system coupled with an elliptic equation in one dimension by transforming the PDAE into a system of linear evolution equations with a Lipschitz-continuous perturbation
Analysis of PDEs.comment: The authors are withdrawing this manuscript to revise the theoretical framework and correct incomplete proofs. Further validation and thorough auditing of the mathematical results are required

Analysis of PDEs.title: Lax Pair for the Kirchhoff-Pohozaev equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that the Kirchhoff-Pohozaev equation on any compact connected Riemannian manifold without boundary admits a Lax pair $(L,B)$, where $L$ is a self-adjoint finite-rank perturbation of the Laplace-Beltrami operator and $B$ is a skew-adjoint operator of finite rank, both depending analytically on the phase space variables. We study the spectrum of $L$ using the perturbative determinant which is known to determine its spectrum and to admit a product representation similar to that of the generating function in KdV. We use this to show that the dynamics of the integrals of motion constructed in \cite{BoitiManfrin2026,BHMP,campos} admits a Lax pair formulation with the same operator $L$ and to get a new proof of the involutivity of these integrals.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Mixing zone dynamics for the Saffman-Taylor instability with viscosity jump
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct mixing solutions to the incompressible porous media equation for fully unstable Muskat initial data. The mixing zone expands linearly in time around an evolving central interface. Our approach combines the $h$-principle with the inversion of the associated Birkhoff-Rott operator, required when the viscosities differ. A key ingredient is to formulate this inversion in terms of the Saffman-Taylor function rather than the vorticity. This considerably simplifies the analysis and may be of independent interest for the Muskat problem.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Regularity of the solution map for the Oldroyd--B model with fractional stress dissipation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The data-to-solution map of the incompressible Euler equations is continuous but not uniformly continuous on Sobolev spaces, whereas viscosity makes the Navier--Stokes solution map Lipschitz continuous on small data, uniformly in time. This paper identifies the behavior of the solution map for a hybrid system sitting between these two extremes: the incompressible Oldroyd--B model in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d=2,3$, in the high-Reynolds-number, high-Weissenberg-number regime. The velocity equation is a forced Euler equation and the only dissipation is a fractional diffusion $η(-Δ)^β$, $\frac12\leβ\le1$, acting on stress. We prove that, on the ball of small $H^s$ data ($s>1+\frac d2$) on which global solutions exist, the solution map is Lipschitz continuous with respect to the $H^{r}$-norm, $r=s-(2β-1)$, uniformly for all time, and Lipschitz into the natural dissipation spaces; the constant is explicit and tends to $\sqrt3$ as the size of the data tends to zero. Consequently the map is Hölder continuous into $C_b([0,\infty);H^{s'})$ for every $s'<s$, and is Lipschitz in $H^s$ itself when $β=\frac12$. Thus, although the velocity field is only transported, the solution map behaves like that of the Navier--Stokes equations rather than that of the Euler equations. The proof exploits the damped wave structure generated by the coupling between $u$ and $\nabla\cdotτ$ through a Lyapunov functional with a cross term $(δu,\nabla\cdotδτ)_{H^{r-β}}$, which transfers the stress dissipation to the velocity difference, together with a low-frequency interpolation argument that keeps all Gronwall coefficients integrable on $(0,\infty)$. The loss of $2β-1$ derivatives is exactly the gap between the hidden velocity dissipation of order $2(1-β)$ and the dissipation required by the Lipschitz estimate, and we show that it cannot be reduced by the energy method.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Slow blowup solutions for the focusing energy supercritical nonlinear Schrödinger equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We consider the focusing energy supercritical nonlinear Schrödinger equation \begin{equation*} i\partial_tψ+Δψ+|ψ|^{2p}ψ=0 \end{equation*} in dimensions $d\geq11$, with $p\in\mathbb N^\ast$, under the Joseph--Lundgren condition $2p+1>p_{JL}(d)$. For every $ν>ν_0(d,p)$, there exists a radial finite-time type II blow-up solution concentrating the ground state $Q$ in the form \begin{equation*} ψ(t,x)=λ^{\frac{1}{p}}(t)Q(λ(t)x)+ζ(t,x),\quad λ(t)=t^{-\frac12-ν}. \end{equation*} All homogeneous Sobolev norms $\|ψ(t)\|_{\dot H^s}$, $1\leq s<s_c$, remain bounded. The radiation converges to a limiting profile \begin{equation*}
  ζ^*\in \dot H^s(\mathbb R^d), \qquad s_c<s<s_c+2ν|λ_+|, \end{equation*} where $λ_+$ is determined by the leading correction in the asymptotic expansion of $Q$ at infinity. Our proof combines matched asymptotic expansions across three spatial scales with modified energy estimates. The key ingredient is the systematic treatment of the singular nonlinear background and coupled oscillations generated by the slow algebraic tail of $Q$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: An Alt-Caffarelli problem for elastic graphs
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study an Alt-Caffarelli-type free boundary problem for symmetric elastic graphs with fixed boundary height. Our results concern existence of minimizers and their description in terms of regularity and shape. It turns out that the weight coefficient in front of the measure term is decisive for existence. We identify a sharp threshold for this coefficient below which existence is guaranteed. Moreover, we find that all sign-changing minimizers are described by a system of three Eulerian elasticae, none of which are lines. Another result shows non-flatness of free boundary points, a classical question in the study of Alt-Caffarelli problems. These properties lead to a better understanding of the nonexistence phenomenon above the aforementioned weight threshold.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Positive solutions of Yamabe-type equations with general potentials
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth closed connected Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\ge3$, and let $ψ\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$. We prove that the equation $$ -\frac{4(n-1)}{n-2}Δ_g u+ψu=u^{\frac{n+2}{n-2}} $$ has a smooth positive solution if and only if its linear part has positive first eigenvalue. In dimensions $n\ge6$, the proof combines an energy estimate under exact local mass constraints with an intersection argument for finite cycles of atomic measures; dimensions $3\le n\le5$ follow from the theorem of Bahri and Brezis.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global Strong Solution to Multi-Dimensional Compressible Quantum Navier-Stokes Equation in Bounded Domains with Large Initial Data
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We consider the compressible quantum Navier-Stokes (QNS) system in a smooth bounded domain, supplemented with a curvature Navier-slip boundary condition for the velocity and a homogeneous Neumann boundary condition for the density. For arbitrarily large initial data away from vacuum, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions when the adiabatic index
  \[ γ\in[1,\infty)\quad\text{for }N=2, \qquad γ\in\left[1,3\right)\quad\text{for }N=3. \] The argument relies on the effective velocity $v=u+\nabla\logρ$, which reveals the parabolic structure of the system. Compared with previous works in the periodic and Cauchy cases, additional difficulties arise from the treatment of boundary terms. We also use a bootstrap argument between the density integrability and the weighted integrability of the effective velocity to enlarge the admissible range of $γ$ from $\left[1,11/4\right)$ to $\left[1,3\right)$. Combining this bootstrap argument with a De Giorgi iteration for the density upper bound and a Nash-Moser type iteration for the positive lower bound, we derive a priori estimates on every finite time interval and extend the local strong solution globally in time. As far as we know, this is the first result on global strong solutions with large initial data for the initial-boundary value problem (IBVP) of the QNS system in bounded domains with compatibility boundary conditions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the cutoff phenomenon for fast diffusion and porous medium equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The cutoff phenomenon, conceptualized at the origin for finite Markov chains, states that for a parametric family of evolution equations, started from a point, the distance towards a long time equilibrium may become more and more abrupt for certain choices of initial conditions, when the parameter tends to infinity. This threshold phenomenon can be seen as a critical competition between trend to equilibrium and worst initial condition. In this note, we investigate this phenomenon beyond stochastic processes, in the context of the analysis of nonlinear partial differential equations, by proving cutoff for the fast diffusion and porous medium Fokker-Planck equations on the Euclidean space, when the dimension tends to infinity. We formulate the phenomenon using quadratic Wasserstein distance, as well as using specific relative entropy and Fisher information. Our high dimensional asymptotic analysis uses the exact solvability of the model involving Barenblatt profiles. It includes the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dynamics as a special linear case.

Functional Analysis.title: Independent powers and bounded Fourier partial sums in $L^1$
Functional Analysis.summary: We construct a probability measure on the circle with independent convolution powers and uniformly bounded symmetric Fourier partial sums in $L^1$. Every positive convolution power is therefore singular with respect to Haar measure. The measure is Rajchman. The construction answers a question of Andersson concerning measures with bounded Fourier partial sums outside the radical of $L^1$, and contrasts with his theorem that the classical examples of Weiss, Katznelson, and Brown-Hewitt have convolution squares in $L^2$. Our proof combines sparse probability blocks, an endpoint $L\log L$ estimate, and a diagonal generalized Riesz product. Exact factorization of local moments permits the simultaneous separation of all convolution powers by Brown's singularity criterion. By the classical spectral theory of independent-power measures, its spectrum is the closed unit disc. In particular, it has non-natural spectrum and induces a non-decomposable convolution operator on $L^1$. The image of the measure in $M(\mathbb T)/L^1(\mathbb T)$ has spectral radius one, and the closed unital algebra it generates in $M(\mathbb T)$ is isometrically isomorphic to $\ell^1(\mathbb N_0)$.

Functional Analysis.title: On $c_0$ quotients of nonseparable Bourgain-Pisier $\mathscr{L}_\infty$-spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: Lopez-Abad extended the Bourgain-Pisier construction to Banach spaces of arbitrary density: every Banach space $X$ embeds isometrically into an $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-space $Y$ such that $Y/X$ has the Radon-Nikodym and Schur properties. We study $c_0$ quotients of these spaces. For every $X$ of uncountable density $κ$, we describe a realization of the construction that admits an explicit surjection $T: Y \to c_0$, given by coordinate functionals built along the construction, whose kernel is an $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-space of density $κ$. We also note that an $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-space with a non-Grothendieck quotient has a $c_0$ quotient, and that every Lopez-Abad space has an $\ell_2$ quotient; all of them have $c_0$ quotients if no infinite-dimensional Banach space is both Schur and Grothendieck, a question we leave open. In an appendix we characterize when the kernel of a quotient map from an $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-space onto $c_0$ is an $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-space, give a quotient map from $C[0,1]$ onto $c_0$ whose kernel is not, and show that every non-Grothendieck $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-space admits one whose kernel is. This version corrects errors in version 1.

Functional Analysis.title: On the isomorphism of the spaces $\mathcal{k}$ and $\mathcal{K}$
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $1 \leqslant p \leqslant q < \infty$, let $\mathsf{X}$ be a separable $\mathcal{L}_p$-space and let $\mathsf{Y}$ be a separable $\mathcal{L}_q$-space. We show that the space $\mathfrak{L}(\mathsf{X},\mathsf{Y})$ of bounded linear operators from $\mathsf{X}$ into $\mathsf{Y}$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{L}(\ell_p,\ell_q)$ if, and only if, $\mathsf{Y}$ is complemented in its bidual. We also show that $\mathfrak{L}(\mathsf{Z},\ell_{\infty})$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{L}(c_0,\ell_{\infty})$ for every separable $\mathcal{L}_{\infty}$-space $\mathsf{Z}$. This extends and complements the earlier result of Arias and Farmer [On the structure of tensor products of $\ell_p$-spaces, Pacific J. Math.]. Based on this general result, we give a completely different proof of the main result of Astashkin, Leśnik and Maligranda [Isomorphic structure of Cesàro and Tandori spaces, Canad. J. Math.], which states that the space $\mathcal{K}$ and its sequence counterpart $\mathcal{k}$ are isomorphic. Furthermore, we complete the picture by showing that the spaces $\mathcal{k}$ and $\mathcal{K}$, although isomorphic, are not isometric. Along the way, we show that for every infinite compact metrizable space $K$ the $\ell_{\infty}$-sum of copies of the space $\mathscr{M}(K)$ of regular Borel measures on $K$ is isomorphic to $( \bigoplus_{n=1}^{\infty} L_1[0,1])_{\ell_{\infty}} \approx \mathfrak{L}(\ell_1,L_1[0,1])$. This provides an abstract blueprint for another result of Astashkin, Leśnik and Maligranda, namely that $\mathcal{K}$ is isomorphic to $( \bigoplus_{n=1}^{\infty} \mathscr{M}[0,1])_{\ell_{\infty}}$. Finally, we show that there are models of set theory without the Axiom of Choice in which the spaces $\mathcal{k}$ and $\mathcal{K}$ are no longer isomorphic. This last part was inspired by Väth's paper [The dual space of $L_{\infty}$ is $L_1$, Indag. Math. (N.S.)].

Functional Analysis.title: Higher-order Persistence Diagrams
Functional Analysis.summary: Persistent homology tracks when topological features appear and disappear across filtered data and represents the lifetime of each feature by a persistence interval. In multiple instance learning, when the instances in a bag use filtrations over the same ordered parameter space, we can compare relationships between persistence intervals across instances. No existing method is designed to aggregate collections of persistence diagrams in multiple instance learning into a single persistence diagram of implications between intervals. We introduce higher-order persistence diagrams to represent relationships between persistence intervals and recursively construct each higher-order persistence interval from a pair of lower-order persistence intervals. We then aggregate these relationships across the persistence diagrams in a bag. Explicit construction of this aggregate is computationally expensive, so we introduce harmonic aggregation to compute coordinates of the aggregate from the lower-order persistence diagrams without explicitly constructing it. Computing a harmonic aggregation coordinate has lower asymptotic computational complexity than explicitly constructing the aggregate. We evaluate harmonic aggregation against persistence landscapes, persistence images, and PersLay on random network model and real-world graph-classification benchmarks, and find that harmonic aggregation has the highest accuracy on the random network model benchmark and on most real-world data benchmarks. Source code is available at https://github.com/cfanning8/higher-order-PDs.

Functional Analysis.title: On the cutoff phenomenon for fast diffusion and porous medium equations
Functional Analysis.summary: The cutoff phenomenon, conceptualized at the origin for finite Markov chains, states that for a parametric family of evolution equations, started from a point, the distance towards a long time equilibrium may become more and more abrupt for certain choices of initial conditions, when the parameter tends to infinity. This threshold phenomenon can be seen as a critical competition between trend to equilibrium and worst initial condition. In this note, we investigate this phenomenon beyond stochastic processes, in the context of the analysis of nonlinear partial differential equations, by proving cutoff for the fast diffusion and porous medium Fokker-Planck equations on the Euclidean space, when the dimension tends to infinity. We formulate the phenomenon using quadratic Wasserstein distance, as well as using specific relative entropy and Fisher information. Our high dimensional asymptotic analysis uses the exact solvability of the model involving Barenblatt profiles. It includes the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dynamics as a special linear case.

Functional Analysis.title: On cutoff via rigidity for high dimensional curved diffusions
Functional Analysis.summary: We consider overdamped Langevin diffusions in Euclidean space, with curvature equal to the spectral gap. This includes the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process as well as non-Gaussian and non-product extensions with convex interaction, such as the Dyson process from random matrix theory. We show that a cutoff phenomenon or abrupt convergence to equilibrium occurs in high dimension, at a critical time equal to the logarithm of the dimension divided by twice the spectral gap. This cutoff holds for Wasserstein distance, total variation, relative entropy, and Fisher information. A key observation is a relation to a spectral rigidity, linked to the presence of a Gaussian factor. A novelty is the extensive usage of functional inequalities, even for short-time regularization, and the reduction to Wasserstein. The proofs are short and conceptual. Since the product condition is satisfied, an Lp cutoff holds for all finite p. We moreover discuss a natural extension to Riemannian manifolds, a link with logarithmic gradient estimates in short-time for the heat kernel, and ask about stability by perturbation. Finally, beyond rigidity but still for diffusions, a discussion around the recent progress on the product condition for non-negatively curved diffusions leads us to introduce a new curvature product condition.
Functional Analysis.comment: 19 pages, post-publication version, fix some problems

Functional Analysis.title: Remarks on the Brascamp--Lieb inequality
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove several variants of the Brascamp--Lieb inequality which are adapted to additional symmetries, weights, and non-Euclidean radial structures. First, an improved Brascamp--Lieb inequality for even functions yields a strengthened Prékopa--Leindler theorem for even strongly log-concave functions. We also record a Legendre-transform proof of a generalized log-Sobolev inequality for log-concave functions. Further results include a Brascamp--Lieb inequality with a concave weight, an unconditional second-order Poincaré inequality, a rotation-trick improvement for arbitrary even log-concave measures, and a Poincaré-type inequality associated with smooth norms.
Functional Analysis.comment: 42 pages, the majority of the paper written before spring 2026

Functional Analysis.title: Operator systems in étale groupoid C*-algebras
Functional Analysis.summary: We study operator systems arising from positivity domains of étale groupoids with compact unit space. Extending Kavruk's enough unitaries principle we show that such operator systems are hyperrigid in the C$^*$-algebra they generate.
