We focus on operator systems of positivity domains in UHF algebras and, by identifying them with Cantor graph operator systems, we show that they are hyperrigid. Furthermore, we show that in general, such a characterization is not possible when the étaleness condition of the underlying groupoid is removed, due to the failure of reduced spectral and compact operator synthesis.

Functional Analysis.title: $(p,q)$-weighted dual curvature measures
Functional Analysis.summary: We study (p,q)-weighted dual curvature measures associated with a fixed nonnegative locally integrable Borel density satisfying a trace-regularity condition. These measures arise naturally from a variational formula for Wulff shapes. We establish the trace-regularity condition when g is pointwise α-homogeneous for some α\in R, or when g is radially non-increasing and continuous. For nontrivial even densities in either class, we prove existence results for the even version of the associated Minkowski problem under suitable assumptions. We also establish uniqueness when the prescribed measure has finite support, under a strict positivity assumption on the density and additional restrictions on the parameters. In the case of Lebesgue measure, our curvature measures reduce to those introduced by Lutwak, Yang, and Zhang, and our variational formulas recover their corresponding variational formula. For Gaussian measure, our results are related to those of Feng, Hu, and Xu, and Feng, Li, and Xu. Finally, we investigate the affine properties of the new measures and the associated mixed volumes.

Functional Analysis.title: A Banach space that distinguishes two maximal operators
Functional Analysis.summary: Maz'ya and Shaposhnikova introduced a non-classical maximal operator $M^\diamond$ as the maximal convolution with the vector-valued signum kernel truncated to centered balls. We construct a translation-invariant Banach space of locally integrable functions on which $M^\diamond$ is bounded, but the sharp maximal operator $M^\sharp$ is not. This answers one of Maz'ya's questions from a collection of 75 open problems in analysis.
Functional Analysis.comment: v2: 14 pages, minor changes suggested by the referees

Functional Analysis.title: Sharp noncommutative Hilbert and Riesz inequalities: classification and spectral corrections
Functional Analysis.summary: For every $1<p<\infty$, with $p^*=\max\{p,p/(p-1)\}$, we determine the sharp Hilbert norm $C_p=\cot(π/(2p^*))$ on $L^p(\mathbb{R};\mathcal{S}_p)$ and the sharp uniform bound $D_p=\csc(π/p)$ for retained and strict Riesz projections of maximal subdiagonal algebras in finite tracial von Neumann algebras. The Hilbert value is also the common Fourier--Schur completely bounded norm. For finite matrices, a nonnegative logarithmic determinant defect connects Heinävaara's tracial joint spectral measure to eigenvalues. The resulting transfer identity classifies finite signed real ridge inequalities on nilpotents and identifies their least additive eigenvalue corrections. A dual theorem characterizes weak-* limits of weighted angular measures of finite nilpotents. In general finite tracial algebras, separate positive-kernel and sharp determinant-covariance comparisons yield the Riesz bounds. Consequences include the sharp Volterra constant, Riesz--Titchmarsh and shifted-transform formulas, joint real-pencil norms, and exact triangular and operator-valued Fourier Riesz norms.
Functional Analysis.comment: 50 pages. Substantially expanded from v1: sharp uniform bounds for retained and strict Riesz projections of maximal subdiagonal algebras in finite tracial von Neumann algebras, via determinant covariance and positive-kernel comparison; sharp triangular truncation bounds and exact operator-valued Fourier norms; weaker regularity for nonhomogeneous spectral transfer. Title and abstract revised

Functional Analysis.title: Fourier quasicrystals with positive integer masses are sections of Lee-Yang cycles
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove that Fourier quasicrystal measures with positive integer masses are precisely the nonzero real sections of effective Lee-Yang cycles by matrices with positive maximal minors, with masses given by weighted local intersection degrees. For Delone support, the reduced support of the cycle can be chosen strict. For unit masses, the cycle can be chosen reduced, with local intersection degree one at every root. Every integer-mass FQ measure has support equal to the common complex zero set of finitely many real-valued trigonometric polynomials. These results answer Questions (1), (2), and (4) of Alon, Kummer, Kurasov, and Vinzant. We recover a finite-dimensional torus from the spectrum and prove that its canonical analytic set is algebraic. A support-height theorem for holonomic sequences provides a linear spectral bound, from which we reconstruct the complex branches and their integer coefficients using fiber moments. Singular sections carry their natural local intersection degrees; discarding these can destroy the Fourier quasicrystal property.

Functional Analysis.title: Well located Banach spaces - A combined approach to L_1- preduals and Hilbert space
Functional Analysis.summary:
In the description of L_1- preduals on the one hand and of Hilbert spaces, on the other, one encounters the surprising appearance of similar classes of operators in terms of their extendibility properties in the setting of these two classes of spaces. It also turns out that the extension properties are closely tied to how the two classes of spaces are positioned inside the ambient spaces. It is well known that in the case of all subspaces being positioned inside a larger space Z as a complemented subspace leads to Z being (isomorphically) a Hilbert space whereas in the case of a Banach space X which is complemented inside all its superspaces, it turns out that X is an injective Banach space.
  In this paper, we shall be concerned mostly with such properties as demanding that X sit inside the ambient space as a locally complemented subspace (and sometimes as a Lipchitz retract). It turns out that the class of Banach spaces X determined by the indicated properties are precisely the class of L_1- preduals in the former case and of Hilbert spaces, in the latter. As an important consequence of this approach, we are led to several new characterisations of Hilbert spaces in terms of the extendibility of bounded linear maps coming from well-known operator (nonlinear operator) ideals.

Functional Analysis.title: The Strong Mankiewicz Property for Closed Convex Body in Normed Spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: Mori and Ozawa raised a fundamental open question: whether every convex body in a normed space enjoys the strong Mankiewicz property (SMP). The SMP states that every surjective isometry from the convex body onto a convex subset of an arbitrary real normed space is necessarily real-affine, with no interior assumption imposed on the target convex set. In the present work, we settle this problem affirmatively.

Functional Analysis.title: The $C_p$ conjecture of Muckenhoupt
Functional Analysis.summary: We give an affirmative answer to Muckenhoupt's $C_p$ conjecture: for $1<p<\infty$, the $C_p$ condition is necessary and sufficient for the weighted $L^p(w)$ norm inequality relating the Hilbert transform and the Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator. We also show that the $C_p$ condition is necessary and sufficient for the weighted Fefferman--Stein inequality.

Functional Analysis.title: Uniform Continuity of Boundary Crossing for Convex Sets
Functional Analysis.summary: Let C be an inhabited, bounded, open, convex subset of a Banach space, and phi the pointwise continuous mapping taking a pair of points, one inside C and one outside, to the point where the segment joining those points meets the boundary of C. We prove constructively that phi is uniformly continuous on the Cartesian product of a set well contained in C and the metric complement of C.

Functional Analysis.title: Noncommutative Mean Value Theorems for Free Noncommutative Functions
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we study noncommutative analogues of the classical Cauchy and Lagrange mean value theorems in the setting of free noncommutative function theory. For noncommutative functions on a uniformly open noncommutative set, we prove a Cauchy-type mean value inequality involving the right noncommutative difference operator $Δ_R$ and the G-derivative, and we establish a mean value theorem for noncommutative curves. Furthermore, we characterize uniform comparison (Lipschitz-type) inequalities at all matrix levels and prove a factorization theorem for noncommutative functions. The proofs combine the Hahn--Banach theorem, the fundamental theorem of calculus along a line segment, and the direct-sum compatibility of noncommutative functions.

Functional Analysis.title: Hyponormal and subnormal dual Toeplitz operators
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we completely characterize hyponormal dual Toeplitz operators with general bounded measurable symbols by using the Douglas theorem in [R. G. Douglas, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 17 (1966), 413-415]. As an application, the hyponormality of dual Toeplitz operators with radial symbols and polynomial symbols in $z$ and $\bar{z}$ is characterized concretely. Moreover, we obtain complete characterizations for both subnormal dual Toeplitz operators with harmonic polynomial symbols and $\varTheta$-class dual Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols.

Functional Analysis.title: Maximal Spaceability of the set of non-absolutely summing operators in quasi-Banach spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: For every $0<p<1$, we establish maximal spaceability of the bounded operators on $\ell_p$ which fail to be $(r,s)$-absolutely summing for all $1\le s\le r<\infty$, using the coordinate-disjointization construction and Maddox's theorem. We give detailed isometric estimates and prove a corresponding maximal spaceability theorem inside the compact operators. The compact result is based on an explicit diagonal multiplier and a single weakly $1$-summable sequence witnessing the simultaneous failure of all admissible absolute summability conditions. A diagonal characterization, a logarithmic compact example, and extensions to operators with values in quasi-Banach spaces containing a copy of $\ell_p$ are also obtained. The constructed subspaces are isomorphic to $\ell_p$ and have maximal algebraic dimension whenever the ambient operator spaces have dimension $\mathfrak c$.
Functional Analysis.comment: Accepted for publication in the Journal of the Iranian Mathematical Society (JIMS)

Functional Analysis.title: Spectrality of convolution and product measures: a block decomposition approach
Functional Analysis.summary: We study the spectrality of convolution and product measures. Let~$μ$~be a compactly supported Borel probability measure on~$\Bbb{R}^d$~such that ~$\mathcal{Z}(\widehatμ)\cup\{0\}=T$~is an additive subgroup, and let~$ν$~be a Borel probability measure on~$\Bbb{R}^d$. We prove that~$μ*ν$~is spectral if and only if~$T$~is a spectrum of~$μ$, ~$ν$~is spectral, and~$suppν$~is contained in a translate of the annihilator of~$T$. Moreover, every spectrum of~$μ*ν$~decomposes into full cosets of~$T$, and every choice of one point from each coset is a spectrum of~$ν$. We also obtain a convolution-factor criterion which strengthens a result of Wu. As applications, we characterize the spectrality of~$L_{[0,1]}*ν$~and prove that the spectrality of~$L_{[0,1]^d}*ν$~implies that of~$ν$~without a compact support assumption. For product measures, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for an orthogonal set to be a spectrum by relating its block structure to spectra of the factors. No compact support assumptions are required.

Functional Analysis.title: A Near-Optimal Lower Bound for $\ell_p$-Subspace Embeddings, $1\leq p<2$
Functional Analysis.summary: For $d \geq 2$, $p \geq 1$ and $ε> 0$, let $N_p(d,ε)$ be the smallest integer $N$ such that for every integer $n$ and every $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$, there exists a matrix $Φ\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times n}$ satisfying $(1-ε)\lVert Ax\rVert_p\leq \lVertΦA x\rVert_p\leq (1+ε)\lVert Ax\rVert_p$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$. For every constant $p\geq 1$ with $p\not\in 2\mathbb{Z}$, when $d\gtrsim_p \log(1/ε)$, the bound \[ N_p(d,ε) \gtrsim_{p} \frac{d}{ε^2 \operatorname{polylog}(d/ε)} \] is established. This improves the previous lower bound $Ω(1/(ε^2\operatorname{polylog}(1/ε)))$ due to Li et al. (SICOMP 2021) and is optimal up to logarithmic factors for $1\leq p<2$. The central technical idea originated from ChatGPT 6 Pro.
Functional Analysis.comment: Simplified the construction of hard instance

Functional Analysis.title: Block-equivalent finite Gabor frames
Functional Analysis.summary: We study finite systems of vectors whose frame operator matrices are unitarily equivalent, via explicit and computationally efficient unitary transformations, to block-diagonal matrices. We call such systems block-equivalent. We show that a Gabor system $\mathcal{G}=\mathcal{G}(g,L\times K)\subset \mathbb C^N$ is block-equivalent when either the modulation set $L$ or the translation set $K$ is a subgroup of $\mathbb Z_N$. We also characterize situations in which the frame operator matrix becomes diagonal. Finally, we show that geometric conditions on subsets of $\mathbb Z_N$ force certain diagonals of the frame operator matrix of $\mathcal{G}$ to vanish, yielding additional sparsity and block structures.

Functional Analysis.title: Fejér--Riesz factorization for positive noncommutative trigonometric polynomials
Functional Analysis.summary:
We prove a Fejér-Riesz type factorization for positive matrix-valued noncommutative trigonometric polynomials on $\mathscr{W}\times\mathfrak{Y}$, where $\mathscr{W}$ is either the free semigroup $\langle x \rangle_g$ or the free product group $\mathbb{Z}_2^{g}$, and $\mathfrak{Y}$ is a discrete group. More precisely, using the shortlex order, if $A$ has degree at most $w$ in the $\mathscr{W}$ variables and is uniformly strictly positive on all unitary representations of $\mathscr{W}\times\mathfrak{Y}$, then $A=B^{*}B$ with $B$ analytic and of $\mathscr{W}$-degree at most $w$; this degree bound is optimal, and strict positivity is essential. As an application, we obtain degree-bounded sums-of-squares certificates for Bell-type inequalities in $\mathbb{C}[\mathbb{Z}_2^{*g}\times \mathbb{Z}_2^{*h}]$ from quantum information theory.
  In the special case $\mathscr{W}=\mathbb{Z}^h$ we recover, in the matrix-valued setting, the classical commutative multivariable Fejér-Riesz factorization. For trivial $\mathfrak{Y}$ we obtain a ``perfect'' group-algebra Positivstellensatz on $\mathbb{Z}_2^{*g}$ that does not require strict positivity; this result is sharp, as demonstrated by counterexamples in $\mathbb{Z}_2*\mathbb{Z}_3$ and $\mathbb{Z}_3^{*2}$.
  To establish our main results two novel ingredients of independent interest are developed: (a) a positive-semidefinite Parrott theorem with entries given by functions on a group; and (b) solutions to positive semidefinite matrix completion problems for $\langle x \rangle_g$ or the free product group $\mathbb{Z}_2^{*g}$ indexed by words in $\mathscr{W}$ of length $\le w$.

Functional Analysis.title: Spectral embedding through weak* limit of finite-dimensional approximations
Functional Analysis.summary:
The scope of this text is to study a process that induces another proof of the Spectral Embedding Theorem: that any densely defined symmetric operator can be extended by a multiplication operator through an embedding of the Hilbert space into an $L_2$ space. Furthermore, that process is meant to be used for specific operators, where natural spectral embeddings or equivalences may be found.
  That process has previously been considered in arXiv:2411.06281 and in arXiv:2511.18189, where it has been introduced through nonstandard techniques. Our contribution aims to be the reformulation of the theory through classical analysis arguments, without the use of nonstandard techniques nor ultraproducts.
Functional Analysis.comment: 37 pages. We corrected typos in version 2

Functional Analysis.title: Banach-Cesaro positive operator-valued measure
Functional Analysis.summary: We construct a family of bounded, finitely additive, covariant positive operator-valued measures (POVMs) on the real line by applying generalised Banach-Cesaro asymptotic averaging to locally finite covariant POVMs. In contrast to the strictly shift-invariant case, where countably additive operator measures are restricted to scalar multiples of a single fixed operator, the introduced covariant setting allows for non-commuting averaged operator values while successfully normalising the total mass. We develop an integration theory for complex-valued functions by taking the completion of simple integrable functions with respect to the continuous operator norm induced by the positive integral of their absolute values. The integration spaces for the original and the averaged measures are shown to possess distinct null classes. Finally, we introduce the operator-valued Fourier transform on these integration spaces and analyze the core algebraic constraints imposed by the covariance property on the exponential multipliers.

Functional Analysis.title: A Borsuk-Ulam theorem for adaptive continuous measurements
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove a Borsuk-Ulam theorem for adaptive measurements: if $2^n\le m$, then any $n$ adaptively chosen continuous functionals take identical values at two antipodal points of any sphere in $\mathbb{R}^m$. Consequently, at least $\lceil\log_2(m+1)\rceil$ adaptive continuous measurements are needed to learn the vectors of a ball in $\mathbb{R}^m$ with an error smaller than its radius, which matches the recently obtained upper bound up to one measurement. The bound extends to Bernstein widths in Banach spaces. The main idea of the proof was found by Claude Fable 5, an AI model developed by Anthropic, and we document the development in a last section.

Functional Analysis.title: The Geometry of Limits in ReLU Function Spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We study the geometry and closure of spaces of functions realized by ReLU neural networks of fixed architecture. We first establish a general result about limits of continuous piecewise-linear (CPWL) functions: the minimum number of convex sets on which a function is affine is lower semicontinuous under pointwise convergence. The proof uses a connection to hypergraph coloring and a compactness principle, and yields quantitative bounds on the polyhedral complexity of continuous limits. We then characterize the functions realizable by shallow ReLU networks with vector-valued outputs, extending a known scalar-valued characterization. Using this and the geometry of limiting hyperplane arrangements, we prove that fixed-width shallow scalar ReLU realization spaces are closed in the weighted supremum norm on the whole input space. In contrast, we construct an explicit sequence of networks with architecture $(2,3,2\mid1)$ whose limit is not realizable by that architecture. Non-closedness holds both globally in weighted supremum norm and under uniform convergence on compact sets with nonempty interior, disproving a conjecture of Petersen, Raslan, and Voigtlaender. Finally, we show that non-closedness for a fixed scalar-output ReLU architecture necessarily involves a \emph{blow-up residue}, in which diverging output coefficients amplify an emerging linear dependence among hidden features. Together, these results provide geometric and functional-analytic tools for studying the boundaries and degenerations of ReLU realization spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: On the power of adaption and randomization 2: Non-symmetric convex sets
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $S:X\to Y$ be a bounded linear operator between real Banach spaces, and let $F\subset X$ be nonempty, bounded and convex. We prove $$a_{2n-1}(S,F)\le 27n\min \{ e^{\rm ran}_n (S,F), e^{\rm ada}_n (S,F)\}.$$ Here $a_k$ is the minimal worst-case error of continuous affine algorithms of rank at most $k$, and $e_n^{\rm ran}$ and $e_n^{\rm ada}$ are the minimal errors of adaptive randomized and deterministic algorithms using at most $n$ continuous linear measurements. This shows that the gain of adaption and randomization, and even nonlinearity, is limited by a factor $27n$ for approximation in convex sets. We discuss the optimality of the result by examples.

Functional Analysis.title: Compactness of composition operators on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we present a complete characterization of the compactness of arbitrary finite linear combinations of composition operators acting on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees. In particular, we obtain a characterization of compactness for linear combinations satisfying the CNC. As an application, we give an affirmative answer to a conjecture raised by Choe et al. [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. Ser. B 9(2022), 733--756] concerning such Hardy spaces. Furthermore, we establish the phenomenon of (double) difference cancellation for linear combinations of composition operators by constructing explicit examples.

Functional Analysis.title: Dirichlet problem on locally finite graphs (revised and extended version)
Functional Analysis.summary: We study existence and uniqueness of solutions to the vertex-weighted Dirichlet problem on locally finite graphs. Let $B$ be a subset of the vertices of a connected graph $G$. The Dirichlet problem asks for a function whose discrete Laplacian is prescribed on $V\setminus B$ and whose values are prescribed on $B$. Each infinite connected component of $G\setminus B$ is called an end of $G$ relative to $B$. On finite graphs we show that the solution is the limit of an averaging process, with an explicit geometric rate given by the spectrum of the random walk, and is also the limit of the heat flow and the minimizer of an energy functional. On infinite graphs we prove two existence theorems: one with no assumption on vertex degrees, under a finite-width condition and summable data, and one for bounded data on graphs of bounded degree, where the solution is also unique among bounded functions. If there are no ends, the Dirichlet problem has exactly one solution. If there are $l$ ends, the solution set, when nonempty, has dimension at least $l$; each end carries a positive harmonic function vanishing on $B$. Calling an end parabolic when the random walk started in it hits $B$ almost surely, we show that this function can be taken bounded exactly on non-parabolic ends and is necessarily unbounded on parabolic ones, a discrete analogue of a theorem of Li and Tam. Consequently, bounded solutions are unique if and only if every end is parabolic.
Functional Analysis.comment: This is a revised and extended verison of an earlier published article

Functional Analysis.title: Linear Preservers of Semipositivity and Minimal Semipositivity
Functional Analysis.summary: We classify all real linear into preservers of semipositivity on $M_{m,n}(\mathbb{R})$, $m,n\ge2$, for arbitrary source and target pairs of proper cones, without assuming invertibility or a prescribed form. The classification consists of product maps $L(A)=XAY$ and degenerate maps $L(A)=Ψ(u^TA)$, subject to explicit necessary and sufficient cone conditions. For square minimal semipositivity with respect to the standard nonnegative orthant, preservation instead forces the operator to be invertible: for $n\ge2$, the linear into preservers are exactly the maps $L(A)=XAY$ and $L(A)=XA^TY$ with $X,Y$ invertible and $X^{-1},Y^{-1}\ge0$. We also classify all linear preservers of orthant semipositivity from $M_{2,2}(\mathbb{R})$ to $M_{1,3}(\mathbb{R})$ into three disjoint classes, two of which lie outside product form.
Functional Analysis.comment: 14 pages; added a classification of linear preservers of square minimal semipositivity; title and abstract updated

Functional Analysis.title: The closed convex hull of all associative copulas is a Z-set in the family of all bivariate Schur concave copulas, and related results
Functional Analysis.summary: Very recently, Problem 2.5 stated by Mesiar and Sarkoci in \cite{MeSa} and originally formulated by Durante was answered in the negative by Šeliga \cite{Sel}. The author showed that the closed convex hull of all bivariate associative copulas is a proper subset of the family of all Schur concave copulas, and even computed the exact uniform distance of his counterexamples to the closed convex hull (so that the Hausdorff distance between the two families is at least $\frac32-\sqrt{2}$). Using the fact that every bivariate associative copula can be represented as a (finite or countably infinite) ordinal sum of Archimedean copulas and the minimum copula $M$, and working with the Markov kernels of Archimedean copulas, we first give an alternative, simple proof of the strict inclusion. We do so by showing that convex combinations of associative copulas can assign only very little mass to \new{staircase-shaped unions of small squares covering} certain line segments parallel to the main diagonal, a result we later extend to so-called chains and staircases. Building on the first observation, we then go one step further and show that, from a topological perspective, the closed convex hull of all associative copulas is a very small subset of the Schur concave family, namely a so-called $Z$-set, and that the family of associative copulas is, in turn, a $Z$-set in its closed convex hull.

Functional Analysis.title: Mixed-norm Herz-type Triebel-Lizorkin spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: Based on mixed-norm Herz spaces, we introduce a new class of mixed-norm Herz-type Triebel-Lizorkin spaces. We establish their $\varphi$-transform characterization in the sense of Frazier and Jawerth and prove Sobolev embedding theorems for these spaces. The resulting embedding theorems extend and improve several known results for mixed-norm Triebel-Lizorkin spaces.
Functional Analysis.comment: We have divided the original preprint arXiv:2406.14727 into three parts. The first part is entitled "Mixed-Norm Herz-Type Triebel-Lizorkin Spaces", the second "Mixed-Norm Herz-Type Spaces", and the third "Jawerth-Franke Embeddings of Mixed-Norm Herz-Type Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin Spaces"

Functional Analysis.title: Mixed-norm Herz-type Besov spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we introduce mixed-norm Herz-type Besov spaces and establish their $\varphi$-transform characterization in the sense of Frazier and Jawerth. We also prove Sobolev embedding theorems for these spaces. The resulting embeddings extend and improve several known embedding results for mixed-norm Besov spaces.
Functional Analysis.comment: Due to the technical nature of the subject, we have divided the work into three parts: "Mixed-Norm Herz-Type Besov Spaces", "Mixed-Norm Herz-Type Triebel-Lizorkin Spaces", and "Jawerth-Franke Embeddings for Mixed-Norm Herz-Type Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin Spaces". This division allows for a clearer and more systematic presentation of the results and proofs

Functional Analysis.title: Ordinary algebras of complex-valued functions
Functional Analysis.summary: A classical theorem due to Gleason, Kahane, and Zelazko states that every complex unital Banach algebra is ordinary, meaning that any linear functional mapping elements into their spectrum is a character. While Roitman and Sternfeld extended this property to algebras with bounded spectra-showing in particular that the algebra C(X) of continuous functions is ordinary when X is pseudocompact-the general case of C(X) for arbitrary topological spaces X appears to be open, as we could not locate any reference in this direction. In this paper, we show that the pseudocompactness condition is unnecessary, that is, C(X) is ordinary for every topological space X. This fact is obtained as a consequence of a more general result characterizing positive characters on a purely algebraic generalization of unital C*-algebras, which we introduce under the name of AC*-algebras. As applications, we obtain two necessary and sufficient conditions for a Tychonoff space X to be realcompact in terms of 1-evaluating linear functionals on C(X) and their continuity with respect to the compact-open topology. Finally, we establish a Banach--Stone type theorem showing that two realcompact spaces X and Y are homeomorphic if and only if C(X) and C(Y) are linearly isomorphic via a map that preserves invertibility.

Functional Analysis.title: Mass concentration and ground states of Fermi systems in Hartree--Fock model with potentials
Functional Analysis.summary: Understanding the onset and mechanism of collapse at critical attractive interaction is a fundamental problem in the variational theory of finite fermionic systems. In this paper, we study this problem within the Hartree--Fock framework under various trapping potentials. By establishing a finite-rank Hartree-type Gagliardo--Nirenberg--Sobolev inequality, we identify a critical threshold $\mathcal{K}^{(N)}$ governing the existence of ground states. We then determine the concentration behavior of ground states as the interaction parameter approaches $\mathcal{K}^{(N)}$. To reveal how the geometry of the trap influences this critical phenomenon, we consider three representative classes of potentials: polynomial-type potentials, ring-shaped potentials, and potentials whose zero set has nonempty interior. For each class, we derive the concentration scale and sharp asymptotics of the least energy. The resulting regimes are qualitatively different, showing that both the location and the rate of concentration are selected by the local geometry of the potential near its minimum set. In contrast to scalar Hartree problems, the nonlocal interaction is coupled here with pairwise $L^2$-orthogonality constraints, and their interplay creates substantial difficulties in the compactness and blow-up analysis.

Functional Analysis.title: Coordinate systems and maximal order complexity in Banach lattices
Functional Analysis.summary: We resolve three questions arising from the study of coordinate systems and order convergence in Banach lattices. Firstly, every order (respectively, $σ$-order) basis $(e_n)$ for a Banach lattice $X=[e_n]$ is automatically a Schauder basis. In fact, the associated partial sum projections satisfy a maximal inequality, and hence every such basis is uniform. Secondly, we show that there is a separable Banach lattice $X$ in which the set $$ X_{\downarrow0}=\{(x_n)\in X^{\mathbb N}:x_1\geqslant x_2\geqslant\ldots\geqslant 0=\inf_nx_n\} $$ is $\mathbfΠ^1_1$-complete. Finally, we construct a separable Banach lattice $Y$ for which the set $Y^{\uparrow\infty}$ of increasing positive sequences which are not order bounded is $\mathbfΠ^1_1$-complete. It follows that neither $X_{\downarrow0}$ nor $Y^{\uparrow\infty}$ can be described in any simpler way than by the nonexistence of positive lower and upper bounds, respectively.
Functional Analysis.comment: 16 pages, lean code available at https://github.com/pedrotradacete/DSTBL3

Functional Analysis.title: Quantum harmonic analysis and the Differential operators on weighted Bergman spaces of bounded symmetric domains
Functional Analysis.summary: We develop quantum harmonic analysis (QHA) for operators on the parametrized Bergman space $\mathcal{A}^2_ν(Ω)$ of a bounded symmetric domain $Ω$, extending the theory previously known for the unit ball. Building on this framework, we introduce a class of differential operators acting on operators on $\mathcal{A}^2_ν(Ω)$. Combining these tools, we advance the theory of Toeplitz operators on $\mathcal{A}^2_ν(Ω)$: we establish Toeplitz approximation results via the $α$-Berezin transform, construct a differential operator $D_α$ that shifts the $α$-Berezin transform, and obtain several characterizations of the radial Toeplitz algebra -- including one via the uniformly continuous radial operators, and one via the domain of $D_α$.

Functional Analysis.title: Noncommutative algebraic sets are not generically nc manifolds
Functional Analysis.summary: A consequence of implicit function theorem is that any algebraic set is a complex manifold except at some singular points which form a strictly lower dimension algebraic subset. Accordingly, an non commutative implicit function theorem of Agler-McCarthy might suggest that a nc algebraic set is generically an nc manifold. However, in this paper, a type of nc polynomials is shown, whose zero locus has larger dimension than the nc manifold given by implicit function theorem.

Functional Analysis.title: Orthograph related to mutual (strong) numerical radius orthogonality on operator algebra
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $\mathcal{B} (H)$ and $\mathcal{B} _s(H)$ be the algebra of all bounded linear operators on a complex Hilbert space $H$ and the Jordan algebra of all self-adjoint operators in $\mathcal{B} (H)$, respectively. In this paper, the orthographs by (strong) numerical radius orthogonality relation on $\mathcal{B} (H)$ or $\mathcal{B} _s(H)$ is introduced, and then the graph-theoretic properties of these orthographs, such as isolated vertices, connected components and the diameters, are discussed.

Functional Analysis.title: On metric space expansions
Functional Analysis.summary:
When finding an original proof to a known result describing expansions on compact metric spaces as surjective isometries, we reveal that relaxing the condition of compactness to total boundedness preserves the isometry property and nearly that of surjectivity.
  While a counterexample is found showing that the converse to the above descriptions do not hold, we are able to characterize boundedness in terms of specific expansions we call anticontractions.

Functional Analysis.title: On the non-hypercyclicity of normal operators, collections of their exponentials, and symmetric operators
Functional Analysis.summary: We give a simple, straightforward proof of the non-hypercyclicity of an arbitrary normal operator $A$ (bounded or unbounded) in a complex Hilbert space as well as of the collection $\left\{e^{tA}\right\}_{t\ge 0}$ of its exponentials, which, under a certain condition on the spectrum of $A$, is the $C_0$-semigroup generated by it. We also establish non-hypercyclicity for symmetric operators.

Functional Analysis.title: Geometric operators and the third problem of Halmos
Functional Analysis.summary: In 1970, P. R. Halmos raised ten open problems on operator theory. The third problem of Halmos is the following: if an intransitive operator has an inverse, is its inverse also intransitive? This question is reduced to the case of conjugate bi-geometric operators in arXiv: 2610.11202. In the framework of conjugate bi-geometric operators, using tools from complex geometry, operator theory, and function theory, this paper gives an affirmative answer to the third problem of Halmos in the following cases: (a) bundle-preserving operator;(b) subexponential growth of operator norms. These two cases cover a large class of operators.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp Stability of Brenier Potentials and its Link to Poincaré Inequalities
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove a new functional inequality for uniformly log-concave measures, stronger than the Poincaré inequality. This new inequality bounds the variance of differences of convex functions and is motivated by the stability theory of optimal transport: for a fixed uniformly log-concave source measure, it provides a sharp stability bound for Brenier potentials with respect to variations of the target measure. Applying this inequality to Gaussian measures, we recover the fact that the Bures-Wasserstein distance between two positive semidefinite matrices is equivalent to the Frobenius distance between their square roots. Our proofs hinge upon linearization arguments for the Monge-Ampère equation governing the quadratic optimal transport problem.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Nonuniqueness of Solutions to 2D Incompressible Euler Equations with Unbounded Vorticity
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct two distinct solutions of the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation with the same initial vorticity in $\bigcap_{1\le p<\infty}L^p(\mathbb R^2)$. The vorticities are compactly supported in space and have mean zero, so the corresponding velocities have finite energy. The nonuniqueness mechanism is a cascade of transitions in quadrupole dynamics across infinitely many scales.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 86 pages, 1 figure, Comments welcome, Lean formalisation coming soon at https://web.math.princeton.edu/~hc9325/

Analysis of PDEs.title: Applications of the fixed point theorem for mappings contracting perimeters of triangles: ODEs, PDEs, integer and difference equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Mappings contracting perimeters of triangles are Banach contractions whenever every point of the underlying metric space is an accumulation point. Consequently, applying the perimeter-contraction theorem on a complete metric space without isolated points yields an existence result already covered by Banach's fixed point theorem. This observation applies, in particular, to operators associated with differential and integral equations acting on standard nontrivial function spaces, such as spaces of continuous functions $C[a,b]$, Lebesgue spaces $L_p$, and Sobolev spaces $W^{k,p}$, equipped with their usual norm metrics. Thus, applications extending beyond Banach's theorem for the same operator and metric require a complete invariant domain containing some number of isolated points. Such a domain may be a closed subset of a standard function space, despite the absence of isolated points in the ambient space. The main goal of this paper is to illustrate applications of the fixed point theorem for mappings contracting perimeters of triangles in settings where the associated operators are not Banach contractions. The differential-equation examples admit interpretations as stylized models combining continuous evolution, nonlocal measurement, and quantized feedback. The integer and difference-equation examples illustrate the effects of rounding on equilibria and periodic responses.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Diffusive-dispersive traveling waves and kinetic relations. Generic flux with multiple inflection points
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the broad class of scalar hyperbolic conservation laws with generic non-convex fluxes, which may thus have an arbitrary finite number of inflection points. We investigate the properties of classical and nonclassical shock waves realized as traveling-wave limits of a linear diffusive-dispersive regularization and provide a phase-plane classification beyond the case of a single inflection point. Within the speed range of the generalized Maxwell construction, our main result classifies the left outgoing profiles by their limiting equilibria. In an elementary bowtie configuration, we prove the existence of nonclassical shock profiles with arbitrarily many oscillations. For nested configurations, we order the saddle connections on each entry interval, taking account of inaccessible saddles. We show that the number of oscillations present in the non-classical shock depends on the diffusion-dispersion ratio, and tends to infinity along the elementary families of saddle connections as this ratio tends to zero. Our construction is based on a generalization of Maxwell's equal area rule, which provides us with an invariant region in the phase space for the study of diffusive-dispersive traveling waves.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A dichotomy for minimal submanifolds
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We survey a circle of recent results showing that a minimal submanifold obeys a dichotomy: either it fills up space, spreading out like a space-filling curve, or it is confined, and confinement forces quantitative restrictions. On the confined side these restrictions are both geometric and function-theoretic: Euclidean volume growth, an optimal rate of convergence of the density, complex-curve rigidity for stable surfaces in $\bf{R}^4$, and a Liouville theorem forcing slowly growing harmonic functions on minimal disks to be constant. A prototypical restriction is Euclidean volume growth, which in these results is forced by the geometry rather than assumed. The mechanism is a volume doubling theorem that converts geometric confinement into quantitative rigidity: a stationary integral varifold trapped in a thin slab at a given scale cannot double its volume by more than a universal factor. We explain how this principle, and the height-excess bounds behind it, produce Euclidean volume growth for submanifolds of sublinearly growing height in every dimension and codimension, the optimal density rate in a slab, the complex-curve and Liouville rigidity above, a higher-codimension Bernstein theorem for disks, one-sided volume bounds, and an optimal stable Bernstein theorem in all dimensions generalizing Moser, Bombieri-De Giorgi-Miranda, Caffarelli-Nirenberg-Spruck and Ecker-Huisken. We describe three regimes with sharp borderlines. In narrow cones the volume grows polynomially with exponent $n+O(\varepsilon^2)$, and the order $\varepsilon^2$ is attained; in wide cones the growth can be arbitrarily fast. For holomorphic curves in $\mathbb{C}^2$, there are also three regimes and
  the borderline is determined by the Kähler angle.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Escape of mass for finite-area hyperbolic surfaces
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let $M$ be a noncompact finite-area hyperbolic surface. We give a lower bound for the $L^2$ norm of eigenfunctions and Eisenstein series in a compact part of the surface. This extends a result of Soundararajan [arXiv:0901.4060] to the nonarithmetic setting. The crucial components of the proof are a long-time Egorov's theorem designed for this setting, a nonlinear uncertainty principle of Cohen--Dyatlov [arXiv:2609.30261], and an application of Weyl's method for exponential sums.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Boundary Plateau Laws II
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Given a straight line $\ell \subset \mathbb R^3$, we classify $2$-dimensional cones in $\mathbb R^3$ which contain $\ell$ and are Almgren minimizing with respect to $\ell$. The main idea of this paper is due to an LLM, and the paper was written by an LLM, under the guidance of the authors.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Boundary Plateau Laws I
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We give a complete list of the possible local shapes of soap films where they wet the whole wire. In rigorous terms, given a straight line $\ell \subset \mathbb R^3$, we study $2$-dimensional cones in $\mathbb R^3$ which contain $\ell$ and are Almgren minimizing with respect to $\ell$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Local regularity for solutions to singular and degenerate quasilinear parabolic equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The main purpose of this paper is to prove local Hölder continuity for weak solutions to quasilinear parabolic equations of $p$-Laplace type under finite integrability assumptions on the forcing, covering the supercritical singular range and the entire degenerate regime. The key ingredient is an $L^\infty$-valued temporal Hölder estimate of the solution after any fixed positive waiting time, which is achieved by coupling a time-rescaling argument with De Giorgi iteration. We also provide counterexamples involving forcing terms with weaker spatial integrability to show that even bounded continuous solutions with compatible data may possess no positive temporal Hölder exponent. In particular, these examples establish the sharpness of the spatial integrability threshold in the degenerate case. Finally, a separate counterexample is constructed to demonstrate that the temporal Lipschitz endpoint can fail for bounded continuous forcing when it depends on time.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the distribution kernels of Toeplitz operators on CR manifolds
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the distribution kernel of a Toeplitz operator associated with a classical pseudodifferential operator on a compact, embeddable, strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold. The main result consists of a formula for the values at the diagonal of the second coefficient in the expansion of the symbol of the kernel. We also establish asymptotic expansions for Toeplitz operators on the positive part of a compact not necessary strictly pseudoconvex CR orbifold under certain natural assumptions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global Hölder solvability for parabolic equations with interior Morrey data
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove global Hölder solvability for uniformly parabolic divergence-form equations with locally finite measure data under an interior Morrey growth condition and a capacity density condition on the spatial domain. The parabolic distance to the initial and lateral boundary is assumed bounded on the source support. For nonnegative data, we establish necessity results that demonstrate the sharpness of the growth and domain assumptions. We also derive estimates for divergence forcing, prove solvability for equations with lower-order terms, and obtain convergence rates in periodic homogenization.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Observability of wave equations with time- and space-dependent potentials: a counterexample under GCC and a positive criterion on the disk
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We show that the geometric control condition (GCC) does not guarantee internal observability for a wave equation with a smooth time-dependent potential. On a bounded connected domain with analytic boundary, we construct a nonempty open observation set such that the pair satisfies GCC and the free Dirichlet wave is observable. For this same domain and observation set, we construct a smooth $2π$-periodic potential for which there exists a nonzero smooth Dirichlet wave that vanishes on the observed cylinder for all time. The wave is the unique mild solution in the space $X_Ω=L^2(Ω)\times H^{-1}(Ω)$ on every finite time interval, so no finite observation horizon yields an observability inequality for this fixed potential.
  The construction starts from a real-valued local counterexample to unique continuation across a noncharacteristic hyperplane. This local statement is of independent interest, since earlier constructions for the wave operator use complex-valued waves and potentials. The global counterexample is then obtained by joining flat oscillatory solutions along the edges of a polygonal observation set, repairing their sum at the vertices without changing its zero set, and using a spatial transition to a common time-independent pair near the boundary. The planar construction also yields counterexamples in every space dimension $n\ge3$.
  For comparison, and to identify a geometry that supplies both propagation and continuation, we show on the unit disk that an observation region containing a central disk and a neighborhood of an embedded cross-cut yields observability for every weak wave at sufficiently large observation time, with constants uniform over bounded measurable potentials. The proof uses a cut, logarithmic polar coordinates, and a Carleman weight whose favorable flux is confined to the observed artificial boundary.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Lojasiewicz Estimates for a Regularised Baby-Skyrme Model
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate the structure of degree $1$ minimisers of a Baby-Skyrme energy of maps $u:Σ\to S^2$ regularised by a Sacks-Uhlenbeck perturbation, and we establish quantitative convergence rates to a simple bubble tree consisting of a single degree $1$ bubble and a constant base map.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp Estimates for Jacobi Heat Kernels in Double Conic Domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the even and odd Jacobi heat kernels defined in the context of the multidimensional double cone and its surface, the multidimensional hyperboloid and its surface, and the multidimensional paraboloid and its surface. By integrating the framework of Jacobi polynomials on these domains, as analyzed by Xu, with contemporary methods developed by Nowak, Sjögren, and Szarek for obtaining sharp estimates of the spherical heat kernel, we establish genuinely sharp estimates for the even and odd Jacobi heat kernel in the double conic settings, and for the even Jacobi heat kernel on hyperbolic settings. We also discuss the limitations encountered in extending these results to the remaining settings.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Revised version. Corrected the sharp heat kernel estimates near the antipodal regime and made several related consistency corrections

Analysis of PDEs.title: Bubble Tree Convergence for Minimisers of a Regularised Baby-Skyrme Model
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study degree $1$ minimisers $u: (Σ,g) \to S^2$ for a Baby-Skyrme model with a Sacks-Uhlenbeck regularisation term $E^α(u) = \frac{1}{2} \int_Σ (1+\vert \nabla u \vert^2)^{α+1} -1 dv_g$ and establish convergence of degree $1$ minimisers to a simple bubble tree as $α\to 0$. We also obtain a new no-neck result for the classical Sacks-Uhlenbeck energy $E^α$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A periodic minimal hypersurface in Euclidean 4-space with Clifford cone singularities
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let $σ(t)=\operatorname{sl}(\varpi t)$ be the lemniscatic sine, normalized to have period $2$. We study the zero set $\mathscr{M}$ of $S(x)=σ(x_1)σ(x_3)-σ(x_2)σ(x_4)$ in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$. We show that $\mathscr{M}$ is a complete embedded minimal hypersurface with infinitely many isolated singularities, which are exactly the vertices of the regular honeycomb of $\mathbb{R}^{4}$ by $24$-cells. Near every singular point $\mathscr{M}$ is an analytic image of the Clifford cone, and $\mathscr{M}$ is a stationary integral varifold with density $π/2$ at each singularity. The isometry group of $\mathscr{M}$ is generated by the translations of the root lattice $D_4$ and a hyperoctahedral group of order $384$ fixing the centre of a $24$-cell; it has index three in the symmetry group of the honeycomb, acts transitively on the singular points, and contains a symmetry which is not visible from the defining equation. Seen from the centre of a $24$-cell, $\mathscr{M}$ is the zero set of a theta series of a translate of the Hurwitz quaternions, which makes the whole symmetry group manifest; the sections of $\mathscr{M}$ by a family of parallel hyperplanes are triply periodic surfaces with cubic symmetry which change topology through conical points. Finally, $\mathscr{M}$ is obtained from a union of $2$-planes by attaching cones over $2$-tori, and its quotient by the lattice of periods is a compact minimal hypersurface in a flat $4$-torus with exactly three singular points and infinite Morse index; we show that its regular part is one-sided and compute its Euler characteristic and integral homology.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp Planar Anisotropic Capillarity Outside Convex Obstacles and Two-Point Rigidity of Transported Boundary Images
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For a convex surface tension $\varphi$ and the wall-energy density $σ(n)=-λ\,\varphi(-n)$, we prove sharp capillary inequalities outside arbitrary convex planar obstacles for $-1<λ\leq0$ and every finite-perimeter competitor of finite positive volume, including non-even and crystalline tensions. Equality holds precisely for translated dilates of Wulff caps in minimum-volume directions, with the entire truncating facet resting on a flat supporting face. A uniform quantitative estimate controls component concentration, shape up to translation, and directional cap-volume excess. The proof combines exact filling, planar completion, and quantitative Wulff stability. For the transport $DΦ$, $Φ=\varphi^2/2$, the zero-adhesion boundary-image estimate characterizes centered ellipsoids among even anisotropies with $Φ\in C^3$ away from the origin and positive definite Hessian. Two-point slab tests with arbitrary boundary data suffice: their projection balances yield a cubic identity forcing $Φ$ to be quadratic. Facets and smooth perturbations provide counterexamples to the transported estimate, including failures at prescribed adhesion levels in $(-1,1)$. Strict finite deficits persist under Hausdorff perturbations of the Wulff body. The classification concerns an unrestricted boundary-data property, stronger than the image estimate needed only for traces of auxiliary Neumann solutions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Volumetric density estimates for nonlocal minimal surfaces
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this article, we prove that viscosity subsolutions to nonlocal mean curvature-type equations satisfy universal volumetric estimates at all scales provided their boundary has zero Lebesgue measure. Our results hold for a general class of symmetric kernels including kernels that are comparable to the fractional Laplacian. Furthermore, we prove that subsolutions with low density (with respect to a universal constant) necessarily have `fat boundary', that is, have topological boundary with positive Lebesgue measure.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp Poincaré inequality for $W_0^{2,p}$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The first eigenvalue of the $p$-bilaplacian over a domain $Ω$ is the inverse of the Poincaré constant for $W_0^{2,p}(Ω)$. In dimension two, we prove that it is minimised by disks under area constraint, thereby obtaining a sharp uniform Poincaré inequality.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp Bounds for Toral Eigenfunctions and Threefold Additive Energy on Circles
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For the lattice circle $P_n=\{z\in\mathbb{Z}^2:|z|^2=n\}$, we prove that the threefold additive energy $J_3(P_n)\le C|P_n|^3$, with an absolute constant $C$. This establishes the optimal bound suggested by Krishnapur--Kurlberg--Wigman and Bombieri--Bourgain. We also prove a uniform weak $L^6$ bound for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions on the square torus, and hence uniform $L^p$ bounds for every $1\le p<6$. This extends the classical $L^4$ bounds of Cooke and Zygmund and establishes Bourgain's conjecture in this range. Applications include mean-square convergence for $L^{6/5}$ observables and a logarithm-free remainder in the nodal length variance of arithmetic random waves.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Shape differentials and sensitivity of the heat equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider Dirichlet and Neumann problems for the heat equation in a domain containing an interior hole. The domain has a fixed outer boundary and a variable inner boundary determined by a diffeomorphism $φ$. We analyze the maps that assign to the infinite-dimensional shape parameter $φ$ the corresponding solutions, and we prove that they are smooth. Motivated by applications to inverse problems, we then compute the differentials with respect to $φ$ of the Dirichlet-to-Neumann and Neumann-to-Dirichlet maps.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A semigroup approach for rough partial differential equations with jumps
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish an infinite-dimensional sewing lemma for discontinuous paths on a scale of Banach spaces. This allows us to construct Young and rough convolutions with jumps. Based on this we analyze the local and global well-posedness of semilinear parabolic rough partial differential equations (PDEs) with jumps in mixed space-time regularity spaces.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Homogenization of the Stokes equations with slender bodies
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper we study the convergence of solutions of the Stokes equations in a domain perforated by slender bodies placed on a fixed periodic grid of size $2ε$ as the size of the bodies goes to zero and the number of bodies goes to infinity. We assume that the width $b_ε$ of the bodies vanishes faster than the length $a_ε$ of the particles. We identify the critical scaling regimes for $a_ε$ and $b_ε$ and prove that in this case the system is effectively described by the Brinkman equations.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 45 pages, 2 figures, Keywords: Homogenization, slender bodies, Brinkman limit

Analysis of PDEs.title: Homogenization of the Stokes equations in a domain perforated by a thin truss
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the homogenization problem of the stationary Stokes equations in a periodically perforated domain whose solid structure consists of a thin truss. That is, the width $a_ε$ of the truss tends to zero faster than the period size $ε$. We identify the different scaling regimes and derive the corresponding effective equations. In the critical regime, we obtain the Brinkman equations, while in the subcritical regime, we recover the unchanged Stokes equations. In a subrange of the supercritical regime, we derive Darcy's law as the effective equation. Furthermore, we explicitly compute the effective coefficients in the Darcy and Brinkman limits. Moreover, as a tool in the analysis, we establish the analogous homogenization result for a periodic forest of cylinders. Finally, we also consider the homogenization result for a fence of cylinders.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 66 pages, 12 figures, Keywords: Homogenization, connected structures, Stokes-Brinkman-Darcy limits

Analysis of PDEs.title: Minimal submanifolds confined in space
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
Already in $\mathbb{R}^4$, there are many minimal hypersurfaces but few structural results. The half-space theorem fails there: higher-dimensional catenoids are among the many examples contained in a slab. Nevertheless, we show that in any dimension and codimension, the height of a minimal submanifold controls its volume growth: confinement to a narrow cone forces polynomial growth, and sublinear height forces Euclidean growth, the slowest possible. Thus volume bounds, which regularity theory assumes, follow from height alone.
  The key is a volume doubling theorem that converts geometric confinement into quantitative rigidity: if an $n$-dimensional stationary integral varifold lies in a thin slab at a given scale, then its volume doubling ratio at that scale is bounded by a universal constant. Iterating this gives the polynomial growth bounds above. Sublinear height is exactly the borderline for Euclidean growth: examples grow at least like $r^{n+4ε^2/5}$ in cones of aperture $ε$. From Euclidean volume growth, we obtain an optimal Bernstein theorem, in all dimensions, for stable minimal hypersurfaces with sublinear height growth, generalizing results of Moser, Bombieri--De Giorgi--Miranda, Trudinger, Caffarelli--Nirenberg--Spruck, and Ecker--Huisken.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Classification of boundary blow-ups for the Mumford-Shah functional with Dirichlet boundary conditions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We classify boundary blow-ups of minimizers of the Mumford-Shah functional on bounded planar domains with Dirichlet boundary conditions. At every point where the discontinuity set meets the boundary of the domain, we prove that the discontinuity set of each blow-up is the tangent line to the boundary at that point. This settles the conjecture formulated by the author in 2024.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Short-wave signal versus indirect prey-taxis
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We address a short-wave asymptotic for one class of quasi-linear second-order PDE systems involving the cross-diffusion described by the so-called Patlak-Keller-Segel law. It is common to employ these equations for modeling the predator-prey community with the prey-taxis, which means the interactions of two species of particles or cells or anything else through which the species called "predators" is capable of moving directionally while searching for the other species called "prey." However, we suppose the predators to be sensitive not to the prey density but to a cue produced by the prey. Additionally, the production of the cue is assumed to be sensitive to the intensity of an external field, which is independent of the community state. This is what we call the external signal. It can be due to the spatiotemporal inhomogeneity of the environment arising from natural or artificial reasons. We assume that the external signal takes a general short-wave form and construct a complete formal asymptotic expansion for the short-wave solutions (modulo solving a chain of the so-called slow systems) with no restrictions on the spatial dimension or kinetics of inter- or intra-specific reactions. Further, we apply the short-wave asymptotic to studying the stability or instability induced by the external signal following Kapitza's theory for the upside-down pendulum. Applying the general results to some special classes of external signals, we get examples of suppressing the taxical transport, examples of the robustness of the species equilibrium to the signal up to a very strong stabilization or, oppositely, destabilization, and something like blurring the borderline in the parametric space between the areas of stability and instability of this equilibrium.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Regularity Effects on the Small-Diffusion Asymptotics of the Principal Eigenvalue: Non-convergence and Convergence
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the asymptotic behavior as \(d\to0^+\) of the principal eigenvalue \(λ(d)\) of the one-dimensional elliptic problem \[ \begin{cases} -dφ''(x)-2αm'(x)φ'(x)+c(x)φ(x) =λ(d)φ(x), & x\in(a,b),\\ φ'(a)=φ'(b)=0, \end{cases} \] where \(α>0\) is fixed, \(m\in C^{1,1}([a,b])\), and \(c\in C([a,b])\). We assume that \(m'=0\) only at \(x_0\in(a,b)\), where \(m\) attains a strict minimum. Within this class, we construct a counterexample $m\in C^{1,1}$ for which \(λ(d)\) has two distinct subsequential limits as \(d\to0^+\), leading to the non-convergence of $λ(d)$. We then consider another class of $C^{1,1}$ advection functions for which $m'(x)/(x-x_0)$ has positive one-sided limits at $x_0$. For this class, we prove that $λ(d)$ converges as $d\to0^+$. Thus, \(C^{1,1}\) regularity alone does not ensure convergence of the principal eigenvalue, even when \(m\) has exactly one strict interior critical minimal point.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A new approach to compactly supported stationary Euler flows
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct smooth, compactly supported stationary Euler flows in two and three dimensions. The three-dimensional flows are axisymmetric with swirl, and their pressure varies along some streamlines. The planar flows are not locally radial. Both constructions start from simple radial profiles, which we perturb by solving scalar elliptic equations on fixed domains. We choose these equations so that their solutions can be exactly constant on open sets and meet these constant regions smoothly. Comparison arguments produce the constant regions, while an a priori regularity theorem ensures that all derivatives vanish where a solution meets them. This gives compact support and smoothness without having to describe the boundary of the support.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Solutions of the Riemann problem for the Self-Organized Hydrodynamics model
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The present paper is devoted to exhibit solutions of the Riemann problem for the Self-Organized Hydrodynamics model. The 2 x 2 system under consideration is strictly hyperbolic. With ambiguous non-conservative products, we adopt a non usual Generalized Rankine-Hugoniot jump condition to suitably define the shock wave solutions. This jump condition is obtained from the information given by the travelling wave solutions of the viscous extension of the system that involves the diffusion terms arising from the physics of the problem. We are then able to determine the simple waves of the non-conservative system studied here and we are able to construct some solutions of the Riemann problem of interest.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Genus Increase in Closed Mean Curvature Flows
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct closed mean curvature flows with arbitrarily large genus increase in every smooth Riemannian three-manifold, giving counterexamples to Ilmanen's genus-reduction conjecture. We prove that a compact hypersurface with a single isolated conical singularity and a power rate of convergence to its cone admits a mean curvature flow whose forward rescaled limit is a prescribed expander in the tangent space at the singular point, smoothly asymptotic to that cone. Combining this theorem with closed mean curvature flows with prescribed tangent flows (arXiv:2405.15577, arXiv:2607.23879) and the noncompact counterexample (arXiv:2605.09657) gives the desired examples.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 21 pages. Comments are welcome! v2: Added the Riemannian case

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global Existence and Scattering of a Class of Two-Dimensional Euler--Poisson--Korteweg Systems
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For a class of two-dimensional Euler--Poisson--Korteweg systems of quantum hydrodynamic type, we establish global existence and scattering for small, smooth, spatially localized perturbations of a constant equilibrium with irrotational velocity. This extends the three-dimensional well-posedness result of Song [Math. Ann. 392 (2025), 2157--2224] to two dimensions. Our proof follows the space-time resonance approach developed by Deng, Ionescu, Pausader, and Pusateri for the three-dimensional gravity-capillary water-wave system. The new ingredients are twofold. First, to allow non-neutral initial data, we exploit the absence of space resonances and of time resonances---including those arising after the second and third iterations---and the improved approximate-finite-speed-of-propagation bounds. Second, in the energy estimates, we adapt the almost orthogonality argument used in the works of Ionescu--Pausader and Guo--Ionescu--Pausader to the regime in which the input and output frequencies are all comparable to $1$. In this regime, time resonances may occur and the relevant curvature quantity may vanish.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The homogeneity function of the fractional $p$-Laplacian and optimal asymptotic exponents for critical Hardy-Sobolev equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let $N \geq 2$, $s\in (0,1)$, and $p \in (1, \infty)$ with $N>sp$. For the fractional $p$-Laplacian, the power function $|x|^{-γ}$ with $0<γ<\frac{N}{p-1}$ satisfies $$(-Δ_p)^s \big(|x|^{-γ}\big)=Φ(γ)|x|^{-γ(p-1)-sp} \, \text{ in }\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\{0\}.$$ Starting from the power function formula of Del Pezzo and Quaas (2026), we derive a paired integral representation of $Φ$, and show that $Φ$ is strictly increasing and then strictly decreasing, with a unique maximum at $\frac{N-sp}{p}$. This maximum $\barμ:=Φ(\frac{N-sp}{p})$ equals one half of the sharp fractional Hardy constant. Consequently, for every $0<μ<\barμ$, the equation $Φ(γ)=μ$ has exactly two roots $0<γ_{-}(μ)<\frac{N-sp}{p}<γ_{+}(μ)<\frac{N-sp}{p-1}$. These roots determine the homogeneous solutions $|x|^{-γ_{-}(μ)}$ and $|x|^{-γ_{+}(μ)}$ of the Hardy equation \begin{equation*} (-Δ_p)^s u - μ\frac{u^{p-1}}{|x|^{sp}}=0 \quad \text{in }\mathbb R^N\setminus\{0\}, \; u> 0 \text{ in } \mathbb{R}^N \setminus \{0\}. \end{equation*} For $0<μ<\barμ$, we then study the following critical Hardy-Sobolev equation \begin{align}\tag{$\mathcal{P}$}\label{P} (-Δ_p)^s u-μ\frac{u^{p-1}}{|x|^{sp}} = u^{\frac{Np}{N-sp}-1} \text{ in } \mathbb{R}^N, \; u > 0 \text{ in } \mathbb{R}^N. \end{align} Let $p \geq 2$ and $U$ be a positive, radially symmetric, nonincreasing finite-energy weak solution to \eqref{P}. We prove that there exists $C>0$ for which \begin{align*} U(x) \leq C|x|^{-γ_-(μ)}\;\text{as }|x| \rightarrow 0,\quad \text{ and } \quad U(x)\le C|x|^{-γ_+(μ)} \; \text{as }|x| \rightarrow \infty. \end{align*} Further, we show that $γ_-(μ)$ and $γ_+(μ)$ are the optimal exponents describing the singularity at the origin and the decay at infinity respectively.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Quantitative periodic homogenization and uniform regularity for nonlocal equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this work, we study quantitative homogenization for a class of nonlocal equations with periodically oscillating Hölder continuous coefficients. For Dirichlet problems in bounded $C^{1,α}$ domains, we prove $L^2$ convergence rates that are expected to be optimal. In addition, we establish interior Lipschitz estimates and optimal boundary Hölder estimates for weak solutions, with constants independent of the period of oscillation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniform parameter bounds for weighted exponential equations on simply connected domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider positive solutions of \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} -Δu=pλh(x)u^{p-1}\mathrm{e}^{u^p}&\text{in }Ω,\\ u>0&\text{in }Ω,\\ u=0&\text{on }\partialΩ, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $p\in[1,2]$, $λ>0$, $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ is a smooth bounded simply connected domain and $h\in C^2(\overlineΩ)$ is positive on $\overlineΩ$. The cases $p=1$ and $p=2$ correspond to the Liouville and Moser-Trudinger equations, respectively. We prove that the normalized parameter \begin{equation*} β=\frac{λp^2}{2}\left(\int_Ωh(\mathrm{e}^{u^p}-1)\mathrm{d}x\right)^{\frac{2-p}{p}}\left(\int_Ωhu^p\mathrm{e}^{u^p}\mathrm{d}x\right)^{\frac{2(p-1)}{p}} \end{equation*} is bounded by a constant depending only on $Ω$ and $h$, uniformly over all $p\in[1,2]$, $λ>0$ and positive solutions. At $p=2$, this excludes positive constrained critical points of the weighted Moser-Trudinger functional at sufficiently large Dirichlet energies. For $p=2$ and $h\equiv1$, we further prove that the energy converges uniformly to $4π$ as $λ\to0$ when $Ω$ is convex. We also develop a boundary exclusion argument for positive weights that rules out boundary blow-up for $1<p<2$ without a priori energy bound.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Tumor growth models with nutrient consumption
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the saturation free boundary of the cell density and its interaction with the nutrient depletion interface in a coupled parabolic model for tumor growth with sublinear reactions. We establish a sharp quadratic--superquadratic growth dichotomy along the saturation interface and quantify the degeneration of quadratic profiles as they approach the joint saturation--depletion boundary. We further show that intrinsic regularity of the saturation interface can occur only at joint free boundary points, where half-space blow-ups of either component determine a unique joint blow-up profile. Finally, we prove a local backward coincidence between the joint and nutrient free boundaries near regular points, which yields spatial and temporal regularity of the joint interface.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Phase separation in multiply periodic materials with fine microstructures
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study a Cahn-Hilliard model for phase separation in composite materials with multiple periodic microstructures. These are modeled by considering a highly oscillating potential. The focus of this paper is in the case where the scales of the microstructures are smaller than that of phase separation. We provide a compactness result and prove that the Γ-limit of the energy is a multiple of the perimeter. In particular, using the recently introduced unfolding operator for multiple scales, we show that the taking the limit of all of the scales together is equivalent to taking one limit at the time, starting from the smaller scale and keeping the larger fixed.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp Variational estimates for Schrödinger equation in $\mathbb{R}^{2}$
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
For $p\geq2$ and $r\geq 1$, we prove the sharp strong $r$-variation estimate for solutions to the free Schrödinger equation
  $$
  \bigl\|V^r_{[0,1]}\{e^{itΔ}f\}\bigr\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^2)}
  \lesssim
  \|f\|_{H^s(\mathbb R^2)}.
  $$
  The estimate holds if $s> s(p,r)$ and fails if $s< s(p,r)$, where $$s(p,r)=\max\left\{ \frac{2}{r}+\frac{1}{p}-\frac12,\, \frac{2}{r}-\frac{2}{p},\, \frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{r},\, \frac{2}{p}-\frac13,\, 1-\frac{2}{p} \right\}.$$
  In particular,
  $s(3,\infty)=1/3$. Thus our result yields a sharp variational extension of the two-dimensional Schrödinger maximal estimate of Du, Guth, and Li [{Ann. Math.}, 186, 607--640 (2017)]. The proof employs fractal restriction estimates to eliminate the regularity loss originating from the summation in the variation norm.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 35 pages, We have revised the proofs of Lemma 3.1, modified the definition of $g_{R,j}$ in Theorem 4.1 and corrected some typographical errors

Analysis of PDEs.title: GBDT with nontrivial seeds: explicit solutions of the focusing NLS equations and the corresponding Weyl functions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Our GBDT (generalised Bäcklund-Darboux transformation) approach is used to construct explicit solutions of the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation in the case of the exponential seed $a \exp\{2 i (cx +dt)\}$. The corresponding Baker-Akhiezer functions and evolution of the Weyl functions are obtained as well. In particular, the solutions, which appear in the study of rogue waves, step-like solutions and $N$-modulation solutions of the NLS equation are considered. This work is an essential development of our joint work with Rien Kaashoek and Israel Gohberg, where the seed was trivial, as well as several other of our previous works.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: This paper essentially develops some ideas from our paper arXiv:2002.04975. Some references and Remark 2.2 are added in the second version

Analysis of PDEs.title: Large-bulk-viscosity limit for two-dimensional compressible micropolar fluids with vacuum
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the Cauchy problem for the two-dimensional compressible micropolar fluid system on the torus $\mathbb T^2$. The initial density is bounded and nonnegative and may contain vacuum, while the initial velocity and microrotation belong to $H^1(\mathbb T^2)$. For sufficiently large bulk viscosity $ν$, we prove the global-in-time existence of solutions without a smallness assumption on the $H^1$ size of the data, provided that the initial compressible component is well prepared in the sense that $\sqrtν\|\operatorname{div}u_0\|_{L^2}$ is uniformly bounded. The proof combines the effective viscous flux with a coupled energy scheme that exploits the vorticity--microrotation dissipation at both the basic and material-derivative levels. For the linear pressure law, we also prove uniqueness in the stated solution class by means of a coupled backward parabolic problem, logarithmic interpolation, and Osgood's lemma. For fixed initial data with $\operatorname{div}u_0=0$, we also justify the limit $ν\to\infty$: every sequence of the corresponding solutions admits a subsequence converging to a solution of the two-dimensional inhomogeneous incompressible micropolar system.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniqueness of the blow-up for some Alt-Phillips cones
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We establish uniqueness of blow-ups, with sharp quantitative convergence, for several classes of singular minimizing cones in the Alt-Phillips problem, in the range $γ\in(0,2)$. As a consequence, we obtain uniqueness at every free boundary point in dimensions $d=2,3,4$ for $γ\in(1,2)$, and in dimensions $d\geq 5$ for $γ\in\left(1,\frac32\right)$.
  The proof of uniqueness is based on three new logarithmic epiperimetric inequalities. The sharp distinction between polynomial and logarithmic convergence is governed by a finite-dimensional integrability condition (sub-integrability) for the spherical linearized problem.
  We prove this sharpness for the radial cone and its cylindrical extensions through an explicit integrability and bifurcation analysis, showing in particular that logarithmic convergence may be sharp even in dimension two. In contrast, we show that the one-dimensional cone is exceptional: although the integrability condition fails, the convergence is polynomial.
  Finally, we characterize the minimality of the radial cone in terms of $d$ and $γ$ by means of a one-dimensional calibration argument, exhibiting in dimension $d\geq6$ a nontrivial regime in which the radial cone is stable but not minimizing.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global Well-Posedness and Large Time Asymptotic Behavior of Strong Solutions to the Compressible Viscous Non-Resistive MHD Equations with Vacuum
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we consider the Cauchy problem to the compressible viscous non-resistive magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) system in $\mathbb{R}^3$, in which the velocity is planar while the magnetic field is vertical. For regular initial data with small energy but possibly large oscillations, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong solution with vacuum. In addition, the large-time behavior of the solution is investigated. A key ingredient is an application of the Bourgain--Brezis divergence estimate to handle the total pressure $ρ^γ+m^2$ for any adiabatic index $γ>1$. This enables us to control both components of the total pressure, $ρ^γ$ and $m^2$, by a single estimate that remains valid in the presence of vacuum. To the best of our knowledge, our result is the first one on global solvability to the compressible, viscous, non-resistive MHD system in the special 2$\frac12$-dimensional whole space allowing vacuum.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global well-posedness and scattering of energy-critical defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation on high-dimensional hyperbolic spaces
A Li-Yau gradient estimate for the Finslerian logarithmic Schrödinger equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish a local Li--Yau type gradient estimate for a nonlinear parabolic equation with logarithmic reaction on a forward complete Finsler metric measure manifold. The coefficients may depend on both space and time. The estimate uses a weighted Ricci curvature lower bound and explicit cutoff bounds for the divergence-form linearized Laplacian. We explain the role of this localization assumption when the reference direction varies with the solution. Applications include a local Harnack inequality for the equation with a potential and an upper bound for positive stationary solutions under a suitable cutoff exhaustion. An appendix gives a variational existence proof for positive bounded initial data, with quantitative bounds on every finite time interval, which is new as far as the authors know.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Extended stability timescales for the 2D3C rotating stratified Boussinesq equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the time evolution of a vertical-slice model for incompressible inhomogeneous rotating fluids perturbed around a stably stratified rest state with linear buoyancy profile. For $\varepsilon$-small localized initial data with vanishing potential vorticity, we prove that solutions remain of size $O(\varepsilon)$ up to times of order $\varepsilon^{-\frac43}$, and up to times of order $\varepsilon^{-2}$ in a regime where the Brunt--Väisälä frequency and the Coriolis parameter are comparable. The first result relies on linear dispersion with amplitude decay rate $\langle t\rangle^{-\frac12}$, while the second exploits the absence of three-wave resonances via a normal form transformation. Our results remain valid for small nonzero initial potential vorticity, whose size is propagated by means of an intrinsic change of coordinates.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Topology, Morse Index, and Area of Minimal Surfaces in Three-Manifolds
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that, in every closed Riemannian three-manifold $(M^3,\bar g)$, there exists a constant $C=C(M,\bar g)>0$ such that every closed smoothly embedded minimal surface $Σ\subset M$ satisfies $b_1(Σ;\mathbb{Z}_2)\le C\bigl(\operatorname{Ind}(Σ)+\operatorname{Area}(Σ)\bigr)$, establishing Song's additive genus-index-area conjecture.
