For closed connected orientable two-sided minimal immersions, we prove the universal inequality $γ(Σ)\le8\operatorname{Ind}(Σ)$ in positive Ricci curvature and the estimate $γ(Σ)\le C(M,\bar g)\operatorname{Ind}(Σ)$ in positive scalar curvature. In the latter case, we also bound both area and total curvature by $C(M,\bar g)(1+\operatorname{Ind}(Σ))$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Emergence of large densities in a chemotaxis system with signal-dependent motility
A class of degenerate elliptic problems involving the Grushin operator: critical mass and ground states
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the following degenerate elliptic equation with combined nonlinearities and prescribed mass \begin{equation*} \begin{aligned} \begin{cases} -Δ_γu+ωu+|u|^{p-2}u=|u|^{q-2}u \ \ \mbox{in }\mathbb{R}^{N}, \\ \int_{\mathbb{R}^{N}} |u|^{2} \mathrm{d}z=c, \end{cases} \end{aligned} \end{equation*} where $Δ_γ$ is the Grushin operator and $ω\in\mathbb{R}$ appears as an unknown Lagrange multiplier. We characterize the critical mass threshold and the energy ground state solutions. Firstly, we prove the existence of optimizers for the Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality involving the Grushin operator together with estimates for the related best constant. Secondly, we characterize the critical mass by the best constant of Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality and prove the existence of $x$-radial energy ground state solutions. Finally, we describe the relation between the $x$-radial action and energy ground state solutions, and the optimizers of Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality. The strategy developed here is based on the interplay between the mass-preserving scaling and a sharp Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality. It therefore suggests possible extensions to other prescribed-mass problems with competing homogeneous terms and threshold-mass phenomena.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Inverse stability for hyperbolic equations with different initial conditions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish Lipschitz stability for both the potential and the initial conditions from a single boundary measurement in the context of a hyperbolic boundary initial value problem. In our setting, the initial conditions are allowed to differ for different potentials. Compared to the traditional B-K method, our approach does not require the time reflection step. This advantage opens a route towards applying our method to the fixed angle inverse scattering problem, which remains unresolved for the single incident wave case. To achieve our result, we impose a pointwise comparison estimate on the Laplacian of the differences of the initial conditions, together with a positivity condition on one of the initial positions. The assumption generalizes previous stability results that usually assume the difference to be zero. We propose the initial-potential problem and establish a Lipschitz stability, then propose an iterative reconstruction scheme and show its geometric convergence. The initial-potential problem serves as an attempt to relate initial boundary value problem to the scattering problem, and to explore the possibility of relaxing the positivity requirement on the initial data. We also establish a new pointwise Carleman estimate, whose proof is significantly shorter and the reasoning is much clearer than existing proofs.

Analysis of PDEs.title: $L^\infty$ blow-up in the fourth-order Jordan-Moore-Gibson-Thompson equation
Elliptic Superlevel Sets in the Class $\OO_C$: Boundary-Layer Geometry and Stability of the Return Map
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study elliptic superlevel geometry and return dynamics for the class $\mathcal{O}_{C}$. Let $C \subset \mathbb{R}^{N}$ be a compact strictly convex core, and $Ω\in \mathcal{O}_{C}$ a bounded domain whose boundary is a global normal graph over $\partial C$ with inward normals returning to $\operatorname{int} C$. For $-Δu = f$ in $Ω$ ($u=0$ on $\partialΩ$), with $f \geq 0$, $f \not\equiv 0$, $\operatorname{supp} f \Subset \operatorname{int} C$, we analyze the superlevel sets $Ω_{t} = \{u > t\}$ for $t \downarrow 0$.
  We prove that for small $t > 0$, $\partialΩ_{t}$ is a global normal graph given by $\partialΩ_{t} = \{c + d_{t}(c)ν(c) : c \in \partial C\}$, satisfying $\|d_{t} - d_{0}\|_{C^{1}} = O(t)$ and $d_{t} = d_{0} - t b_{0} + o_{C^{1}}(t)$, where $b_{0}$ depends on the Hopf derivative and transversality. Using normal-graph formulas, we show $Ω_{t} \in \mathcal{O}_{C}$.
  The return maps $F_{t} : \partial C \to \partial C$ are well-defined, satisfying $\|F_{t} - F_{0}\|_{L^{\infty}} = O(t)$ and $F_{t} = F_{0} + t \mathcal{A}_{0} + o_{L^{\infty}}(t)$. For any sequence $t_{n} \downarrow 0$, the non-autonomous system $x_{n+1} = F_{t_{n}}(x_{n})$ is asymptotically autonomous with background map $F_{0}$. These results bridge elliptic boundary-layer deformation and return-map dynamics relative to a convex core.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Transference principles for divergence sets of dispersive equations and their applications
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this article, we study the fractal refinement of the Carleson's problem: (1) We introduce an equivalence relation on linear dispersive PDEs on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ based on the high-frequency oscillation of their Fourier multipliers, proving that equations in the same class share the same Hausdorff dimension of divergence sets. As applications, we estimate these dimensions for abstract dispersive families. Consequently, we recover known $1$-dimensional results for linearized Boussinesq and Beam propagations, while establishing new results for the both of them in higher dimensions and for Klein-Gordon propagations in all dimensions. (2) Next, we study the effect of radial symmetry by obtaining dimension estimates for fractional Schrödinger equations with concave phase and radial initial data. Applying a transference principle, dimension estimates are extended to families of abstract dispersive equations. As special cases, we recover the known result for the Beam propagation and also obtain new results for the linearized Boussinesq and the Klein-Gordon propagations in the radial setting. (3) We study analogues of (2) for the $3$-dimensional real hyperbolic space by obtaining dimension estimates for a wide class of dispersive propagations: the Schrödinger, fractional Schrödinger (with convex and concave phases), Beam, linearized Boussinesq, Wave and Klein-Gordon equations. This is the first result of its kind, outside the setting of flat Euclidean geometry. Our arguments are based on an inter-spatial transference principle of geometric-analytic flavour. In the process, we also obtain quantitative results on the singular sets of Sobolev functions, in the spirit of Žubrinić, which may be of independent interest.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Principal profiles, characteristic communication and critical asymptotics for cooperative nonlocal systems on the circle
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study cooperative nonlocal transport on a circle with species-dependent constant velocities and arbitrary $L^1$ probability kernels. For periodic coefficients, the period map is a compact perturbation of the no-jump map. We construct separate receiving and sending characteristic scans: under a two-tree condition based at one active component, a positive Floquet profile exists exactly when the full period map has strictly larger spectral radius than its no-jump part. The other jump rates may vanish. The scans provide an integral minorant and positive jump return; a separate coefficient inequality verifies the spectral gap. Smooth locking examples distinguish communication from frozen-time mixing, while a resonant example separates positive return from spectral separation. Autonomous nonzero velocities and union-graph connectivity yield a simple principal pair; one active component suffices for exponential mixing. We also prove local perturbation results. For quadratic self-regulation, the same principal projection gives a transverse response whose averaged cubic coefficient is a nonnegative asymptotic variance. It determines both the critical $t^{-2}\log t$ correction and the second-order period-averaged amplitude of the positive branch.

Analysis of PDEs.title: An inverse moving point source problem in inhomogeneous acoustic media: uniqueness, stability and reconstruction
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper is concerned with the simultaneous recovery of the trajectory and intensity of an unknown moving point source in an inhomogeneous acoustic medium. We prove that the whole-boundary measurements over a finite time interval uniquely determine the moving source. Furthermore, under suitable propagation and rank assumptions, Lipschitz stability of determining both the trajectory and intensity is derived using waveforms measured at four fixed receivers outside the source region. A novel Volterra--Euler reconstruction scheme is developed for solving the inverse problem, and the error estimate is derived for the proposed scheme. Numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed numerical method.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global regularity for a class of degenerate/singular Monge-Ampère equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the global regularity of solutions to the homogeneous Dirichlet problem for a class of Monge-Ampère equations, which become degenerate or singular on the boundary due to the zero boundary value and the distance function. The degeneracy and singularity are described by the index - the sum of the powers of the distance function and the solution. We give a complete classification of the index, and prove that the solution is globally Hölder continuous, log-Lipschitz continuous, $C^{1,η}$, $C^{2,α}$ and $W^{2,p}$ respectively, depending on the size of the index. We also obtain estimates related to the five regularity results. All these results are optimal.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 32 pages, no figures. Submitted for publication

Analysis of PDEs.title: Regularization and Full Support for the CBO Equation with Measure Initial Data
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove global well-posedness and regularization for the isotropic consensus-based optimization equation with initial probability measures of finite fourth moment. Under suitable weight decay assumptions, after any nonconstant consensus motion, both the density and the consensus trajectory become smooth, and all spatial Sobolev norms are locally bounded in time. The proof uses a Fourier commutator estimate, localization and iteration, followed by a nonlinear time bootstrap. Counterexamples show that smoothing can fail at a stationary consensus point. For non-Dirac initial data, we also prove positivity away from the consensus point and full support at every positive time in all dimensions.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: add remark 1.4 and expand the introduction

Analysis of PDEs.title: Dissipative weak solutions to the three-dimensional stochastic Euler equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper is concerned with the dissipative weak solutions to the three-dimensional stochastic Euler equations. For any $γ\in \left[ {0,\frac{1}{5}} \right)$, we establish the existence of $γ$-Hölder continuous weak solutions that exhibit a strict energy dissipation in expectation. For any $γ> \frac{1}{3}$, we prove that the three-dimensional stochastic Euler equations do not possess dissipative solutions satisfying the corresponding spatial $γ$-Hölder regularity. It is well known that the stochastic forcing inevitably gives rise to additional stochastic effects to the Reynolds stresses, which cannot be treated by the differential estimates in the classical convex integration scheme introduced by Buckmaster, De Lellis, Isett and Székelyhidi (Ann. Math., 182(1):127--172, 2015). To address this difficulty, we develop a novel material integration technique into the stochastic convex integration scheme, so that those stochastic Reynolds stresses are quantified.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Large deviations from a stable steady state for damped dispersive PDEs with vanishing random kicks
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the behaviour of stationary measures for a class of dispersive PDEs damped by a linear zero-order term and perturbed by a small kick noise. Under some natural assumptions on the law of the noise, we prove that any family of stationary measures satisfies the large deviation principle in the vanishing noise limit. The result highlights the role of nonlinear smoothing and applies to the nonlinear Schrödinger and Korteweg-de Vries equations, and to a variety of random perturbations including Gaussian and exponential variables.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Existence of a third self-similar solution of the Yang--Mills equation in high odd dimensions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In a recent paper~\cite{BGW}, Bizoń, Glogić, and Wasserman (BGW) reduced the classification of smooth self-similar Yang--Mills profiles in odd spatial dimensions $d\ge11$ to an algebraic problem of counting roots of an explicit polynomial in a prescribed interval. Two roots correspond to explicit profiles. BGW conjectured that there is exactly one additional root and verified this in a range of odd dimensions. Here, we prove the existence of an additional root, and hence of a third smooth self-similar profile, in every odd dimension $d\geq11$. The proof combines an endpoint sign calculation for the resonance polynomial with an algebraic argument showing that the third root is distinct from the two explicit ones. Uniqueness remains open in general.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Costa surface with a free-boundary hole: an embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface with three ends
Analysis of PDEs.summary: An exterior free-boundary minimal surface is a properly immersed minimal surface outside the unit ball whose compact boundary lies on the unit sphere and meets it orthogonally. By Mazet and Mendes, in $\mathbb{R}^3$ every such surface with one regular end is a catenoidal piece, and every stable one with parallel embedded regular ends is catenoidal. We construct connected embedded examples with three ends from the Costa surface $M$, placed so that its central saddle point is at the origin. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ we perturb $\varepsilon^{-1}(M\setminus B_\varepsilon)$ into a properly embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface of genus one with one boundary circle and three ends, two catenoidal and one planar. The construction is a small-hole perturbation. The only error of the initial surface is in the boundary condition. The symmetry group of the Costa surface removes all obstructions: at the hole it forbids the logarithmic and the tilting modes, and globally it kills the bounded Jacobi fields of the Costa surface, which is nondegenerate by Nayatani. In the conformal compactification the Jacobi operator is smooth also at the ends, so the linear analysis takes place on a compact torus with one small hole. The same construction applied to the Costa-Hoffman-Meeks surfaces gives such examples of every genus $k\geq1$, of index at least $2k+3$. We also report numerical experiments with two independent implementations of the Costa surface. They confirm the period condition, the symmetries, the boundary error, the index and nullity of the Jacobi operator and the absence of an equivariant kernel. They also compute the free-boundary correction near the hole, which gives pictures of the surfaces.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 26 pages, 7 figures. Interactive 3D models: https://surfaces.igorkozyrev.com/#costa . The scripts for the numerical experiments are attached as ancillary files (anc/scripts)

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp well-posedness and soliton resolution for the half-wave maps equation in $H^{1/2}_\bullet$
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We prove sharp well-posedness and soliton resolution for the half-wave maps equation on the real line $\R$ in \(H^{1/2}_\bullet\). This regularity threshold for global well-posedness is optimal, as we show by constructing examples of ill-posedness in \(H^s_\bullet\) for any \(s<1/2\). Moreover, with the spectral assumption satisfied by a dense set of initial data in the energy space, we prove that solutions in \(H^{1/2}_\bullet\) asymptotically decouple as an infinite superposition of solitons. Our results extend the known global well-posedness and finite soliton resolution for rational data in \(H^\infty_\bullet\) to sharp global well-posedness and soliton resolution for general data in \(H^{1/2}_\bullet\).
  Different from rational solutions, general data can also involve an infinite discrete spectrum, which makes the reduction analysis framework on the finite rank no longer applicable. For sharp well-posedness, we present a new isometry criterion and stability results for resolvent transform in the explicit formula. For soliton resolution, we develop a spectral method for this equation based on direct resolvent analysis and a novel trace norm estimate that upgrades energy convergence to uniform convergence. Our argument also yields sharp well-posedness and soliton resolution for the generalized half-wave maps equation with targets in the complex Grassmannians, extending the classical sphere-valued case.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Fluid Problems Posed on Closed Hypersurfaces: Circumventing the Saddle-Point Structure
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For a $d$-dimensional closed hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$, we reformulate the (stationary) tangent Stokes, transient tangent Stokes, and transient tangent Navier-Stokes equations by replacing the divergence equation with a pressure Poisson equation, thereby circumventing their saddle-point structure. The pressure Poisson equation hinges on a commutator identity between the divergence and the surface diffusion operator, whose lower-order term depends on the Ricci curvature, and requires no boundary conditions for the pressure. We show that the reformulated operator is the composition of a linear, block-triangular data map with the primal operator. Consequently, each reformulation is well-posed if and only if the primal problem is, and solving it with arbitrary data amounts to solving the primal problem with a modified divergence datum. For hypersurfaces of class $C^2$ and data of the pressure Poisson equation in $H^{-1}$, the tangent Stokes reformulations can be posed in $H^1$-based spaces, which paves the way for conforming discretizations that do not require a discrete inf-sup condition.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Time-Periodic Chemotaxis in Shifting Environments: Propagation and Planar Forced Waves in $\R^N$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study time-periodic Keller--Segel dynamics in a translating KPP environment. In the parabolic--elliptic regime, we prove global boundedness, identify the sharp speed \(c_*=2\sqrt{\bar a\,\bar r}\), establish persistence in the interior region \(|s|<c_*\), \(s\cdot e<c\), and derive the complementary sharp upper bounds; for a moving favorable slab, the sign of a principal Floquet exponent determines persistence or extinction under the stated weighted-resolvent condition. For every fixed \(τ\ge0\), under constant population diffusivity and sufficiently weak taxis, we further construct locally unique planar forced time-periodic waves in \(\mathbb R^N\). The main new analytic mechanisms are an exact Yukawa first-contact estimate, which controls the chemotactic drift at the KPP leading-edge scale without losing the sharp propagation threshold, and a two-sided weighted Fredholm--monodromy continuation framework for the temporally nonlocal signal equation, with explicit control of the far-field spectral gaps and the translational neutral mode. To the best of the author's knowledge, planar forced time-periodic waves in \(\mathbb R^N\) for shifting Keller--Segel systems have not been investigated in any previous studies; earlier forced-wave results are confined to substantially more restrictive settings, in particular one-dimensional parabolic--elliptic models. Thus the present construction provides the first multidimensional planar forced-wave theory for a time-periodic shifting Keller--Segel system with temporal signal memory.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Energy equality and renormalization of Navier-Stokes-Vlasov equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study weak solutions of the incompressible and the compressible Navier--Stokes--Vlasov systems on a bounded domain, where a viscous fluid is coupled to a dispersed particle phase through a drag force; the fluid obeys the no-slip boundary condition and the particles are subject to specular reflection. For solutions with Besov regularity, we show that the Vlasov equation is renormalizable in the sense of DiPerna--Lions, and we give regularity thresholds for the validity of the global energy equality. If the distribution function $f$ belongs to $B_p^{α,\infty}$ in space and velocity with time integrability $p$, and the fluid velocity $\mathbf{u}$ belongs to $B_q^{β,\infty}$ jointly in space and time with integrability $q$, then the energy equality holds provided $α+β>1$ and $β$ exceeds an explicit bound depending on $p$, $q$ and the dimension, under a natural integrability assumption on the pressure; an analogous criterion holds for the compressible system when the density is bounded from above and below. The condition $αp>1$ imposed on $f$ is not merely technical: it is exactly the range in which the macroscopic momentum flux possesses a boundary trace, so that the specular reflection condition passes to the macroscopic energy balance. When the particle phase is absent, our thresholds coincide with the criteria $β>\frac12+\frac1q$ and $β>\frac3q$ obtained by Yu for the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations alone. The proofs combine a boundary cutoff argument with commutator estimates based on a scale-localized Besov modulus, together with a boundary-strip analysis.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Submitted to Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal

Analysis of PDEs.title: On Solutions for Singular Toda System on Surfaces with Boundary
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper studies a singular Toda system with linear source terms on a compact surface $Σ$ with boundary $\partialΣ$. The aim is twofold. First, using isothermal coordinates and reflection arguments near the boundary, we perform blow-up analysis obtaining a compactness result. Second, by assuming that $\partialΣ$ has at least two connected components, we prove a general existence result via a min-max scheme combined with a retraction argument.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Silent Orbits and Cancellations in the Wave Trace
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper shows that the wave trace of a bounded and strictly convex planar domain may be arbitrarily smooth in a neighborhood of some point in the length spectrum. In other words, the Poisson relation, which asserts that the singular support of the wave trace is contained in the closure of $\pm$ the length spectrum, can almost be made into a strict inclusion. To do so, we construct large families of domains for which there exist multiple periodic billiard orbits having the same length but different Maslov indices. Using the microlocal Balian-Bloch-Zelditch parametrix for wave invariants developed in our previous paper, we solve a large system of equations for the boundary curvature jets, which leads to the required cancellations. We call such periodic orbits silent, since they are undetectable from the ostensibly audible wave trace. Such cancellations show that there are potential limitations in using the wave trace for inverse spectral problems and, more fundamentally, that the Laplace spectrum and the length spectrum are inherently different mathematical objects, at least insofar as the wave trace is concerned.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 74 pages, 9 figures, to appear in Analysis & PDE

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global Well-posedness and Asymptotic Extinction for Keller-Segel Systems with Superlinear Noise
Analysis of PDEs.summary: It is well known that solutions to deterministic Keller--Segel chemotaxis systems can blow up in finite time under certain conditions. To investigate whether noise can prevent such blow-up, we study parabolic--elliptic and fully parabolic Keller--Segel systems on smooth bounded domains with pointwise superlinear multiplicative Itô noise $σ_0u^r\,\mathrm dW_t$, where $W$ is a real Brownian motion. Our results show that superlinear multiplicative noise can prevent finite-time blow-up in Keller--Segel systems. For $r>3/2$, we prove global existence and pathwise uniqueness of nonnegative mild solutions in arbitrary spatial dimension, for every $σ_0>0$. At $r=3/2$, both systems are globally well-posed in two dimensions for every positive noise intensity; in arbitrary dimension, the parabolic--elliptic system is global under $σ_0^2\ge2χ$. For $r>3/2$ in the fully parabolic case, the proof combines a logarithmic estimate for the time derivative of the chemical signal with comparison of the local solution to the solution of a scalar stochastic differential equation. The two-dimensional case follows from mass quadratic variation, deterministic maximal regularity, and localized energy estimates. We also establish almost-sure $L^1$ extinction and algebraic decay of fractional mass moments.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Large data global strong solutions to the quantum Navier-Stokes equations with degenerate viscosity
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This work is devoted to study the Cauchy problem for the quantum Navier-Stokes equations in $\mathbb R^N$, $N=2,3$, with density dependent viscosities $μ(ρ)=ρ,λ(ρ)=0$, quantum capillarity $κ(ρ)=1/ρ$, which was derived by Dunn and Serrin (see Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 88(2):95-133, 1985) as a phase transition model. For arbitrarily large initial data satisfying suitable regularity and decay assumptions, with density positive at every finite point and vanishing at infinity, we prove the existence and uniqueness of global strong solutions without symmetry assumptions. The admissible pressure range is $γ\ge 1$ in two dimensions and $1\leγ< 8/3$ in three dimensions. On every finite time interval, the density remains pointwise comparable to its initial profile, and both the effective velocity and the logarithmic density gradient remain bounded. The central estimates require no uniform positive lower bound for the density. When $γ>1$, a suitable combination of the density and effective velocity equations allows the maximum principle to yield an $L^\infty$ bound for the effective velocity using only an upper bound for the density. We then introduce the relative density with respect to a fixed profile determined by the initial data. In the isothermal case $γ=1$, we combine estimates for this relative density with a scalar inequality involving the effective velocity and the logarithmic density to close the coupled estimates and obtain the effective velocity bound. Combining the relative-density bounds with weighted gradient estimates and localized De Giorgi iteration, we control the logarithmic density gradient and close the higher-order estimates.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Local rigidity of conformally Euclidean metrics for the anisotropic Helmholtz equation at fixed energy
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove local rigidity of smooth conformally Euclidean metrics $g_0$ on smooth compact domains $M\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge3$, for the anisotropic Helmholtz equation $(-Δ_g -k^2)u =0$ at a fixed energy $k^2>0$ which is not a Dirichlet eigenvalue of $-Δ_{g_0}$ in $M$. Any smooth metric sufficiently close to $g_0$ in $H^s(M)$, with integer $s>n/2+1$, and having the same Dirichlet-to-Neumann map, is its pullback by a smooth diffeomorphism fixing the boundary pointwise. The proof uses a Helmholtz embedding to fix the gauge and a compactness argument together with a characterization of the kernel of the linearization.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A self-contained proof of the variational characterization of the principal eigenvalue of $-Δ+q$ under general Robin boundary conditions of non-classical type
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we are going to deliver a completely self-contained proof of the variational characterization of the principal eigenvalue of $-Δ+q$ in $Ω$ under Robin boundary conditions of non-classical type, $\frac{\partial u}{\partial n}+β(x)u=0$ on $\partialΩ$, where $β(x)$ is allowed to change sign on $\partialΩ$. The classical case occurs in the very special case when $β\geq 0$ on $\partialΩ$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: $L^p$-theory for the exterior Stokes problem with Navier's type slip-without-friction boundary conditions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we consider the stationary Stokes equations in an exterior domain three-dimensional under a slip boundary condition without friction. We set the problem in weighted Sobolev spaces in order to control the behavior at infinity of the solutions. In this work, we try to investigate the existence and uniqueness up to an element of a nontrivial kernel of the weak solutions related to this problem in $L^p-$theory when $p>3$. Our proofs are based on obtaining inf-sup conditions that play a fundamental role.

Functional Analysis.title: Sharp Stability of Brenier Potentials and its Link to Poincaré Inequalities
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove a new functional inequality for uniformly log-concave measures, stronger than the Poincaré inequality. This new inequality bounds the variance of differences of convex functions and is motivated by the stability theory of optimal transport: for a fixed uniformly log-concave source measure, it provides a sharp stability bound for Brenier potentials with respect to variations of the target measure. Applying this inequality to Gaussian measures, we recover the fact that the Bures-Wasserstein distance between two positive semidefinite matrices is equivalent to the Frobenius distance between their square roots. Our proofs hinge upon linearization arguments for the Monge-Ampère equation governing the quadratic optimal transport problem.

Functional Analysis.title: Applications of the fixed point theorem for mappings contracting perimeters of triangles: ODEs, PDEs, integer and difference equations
Functional Analysis.summary: Mappings contracting perimeters of triangles are Banach contractions whenever every point of the underlying metric space is an accumulation point. Consequently, applying the perimeter-contraction theorem on a complete metric space without isolated points yields an existence result already covered by Banach's fixed point theorem. This observation applies, in particular, to operators associated with differential and integral equations acting on standard nontrivial function spaces, such as spaces of continuous functions $C[a,b]$, Lebesgue spaces $L_p$, and Sobolev spaces $W^{k,p}$, equipped with their usual norm metrics. Thus, applications extending beyond Banach's theorem for the same operator and metric require a complete invariant domain containing some number of isolated points. Such a domain may be a closed subset of a standard function space, despite the absence of isolated points in the ambient space. The main goal of this paper is to illustrate applications of the fixed point theorem for mappings contracting perimeters of triangles in settings where the associated operators are not Banach contractions. The differential-equation examples admit interpretations as stylized models combining continuous evolution, nonlocal measurement, and quantized feedback. The integer and difference-equation examples illustrate the effects of rounding on equilibria and periodic responses.

Functional Analysis.title: Foundations of Double Operator Integrals with a Variant Approach to the Nonseparable Case
Functional Analysis.summary: We aim to give a self-contained and detailed yet simplified account of the foundations of the theory of double operator integrals, in order to provide an accessible entry point to the theory. We make two new contributions to these foundations: (1) a new proof of the existence of the product of two projection-valued measures, which allows for the definition of the double operator integral for Hilbert-Schmidt operators, and (2) a variant approach to the integral projective tensor product on arbitrary (not necessarily separable) Hilbert spaces using a somewhat more explicit norm than has previously been given. We prove the Daletskii-Krein formula for strongly differentiable perturbations of a densely-defined self-adjoint operator and conclude by reviewing an application of the theory to quantum statistical mechanics.
Functional Analysis.comment: 52 pages, typos corrected, introduction expanded, comments welcome

Functional Analysis.title: A Framework for Supervised and Unsupervised Learning via Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
Functional Analysis.summary:
We introduce a unified framework for supervised and unsupervised learning through density estimation using reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHSs). To this end, we introduce the notion of a nested RKHS, that is, an increasing sequence of RKHSs whose union is dense in an ambient $L^2$-space. This construction allows us to exploit the computational structure of RKHS methods at each finite approximation level while preserving the approximation power of the entire $L^2$-space.
  We first study statistical learning in a fixed RKHS. In both unsupervised and supervised settings, we establish strong convergence results for empirical averages of random elements taking values in an RKHS continuously embedded in $L^2$. We then use the nested RKHS structure to combine these statistical convergence results with the density of the union of the RKHSs in the ambient $L^2$-space. We apply this construction to probability density estimation and binary Bayesian classification. For density estimation, we construct explicit empirical estimators of the orthogonal projections of the target density onto the RKHSs and establish their almost sure convergence. A diagonal selection procedure then yields a sequence of estimators converging almost surely to the target density in $L^2$.
  For binary Bayesian classification, we formulate the approximation of the Bayes target as the minimization of suitable population and empirical risk functionals. We prove consistency of the empirical minimizers and use the nested structure to obtain convergence towards the Bayes target in $L^2$. We further provide a geometric interpretation in terms of hyperplanes and weighted distances in the ambient $L^2$-space. Finally, we show that the population risk admits a direct probabilistic interpretation in terms of the probability of misclassification.
Functional Analysis.comment: Enhanced bibliography, a few updates, more detailed proofs

Functional Analysis.title: From one particle to N particles: uniform transport-information and log-Sobolev inequalities for Coulomb gases on the torus
Functional Analysis.summary: We study how a functional inequality satisfied by the one-particle conditional distributions of a Gibbs measure, with a constant independent of the positions of the other particles, can be propagated to the whole N -particle system, with a constant independent of N , when the interaction is singular. Our model is the Coulomb gas on the torus T 3 in the mean-field regime. We distinguish two mechanisms. The first one is a dependent tensorization, governed by Dobrushin-Wu interdependence coefficients. It yields uniform Poincar{é} and transport-information W 2 I inequalities with fully explicit constants. We explain why this mechanism does not extend to the log-Sobolev inequality: the Zegarlinski-type coefficients, which require pointwise bounds on the interaction, are infinite. The second mechanism is a tensorization with a defect. Using a uniform bound on the partition function due to Duerinckx and Jabin, it yields a uniform log-Sobolev inequality for the Coulomb gas on T 3 at small charge. We identify the assumptions on the interaction under which each mechanism applies. All the results are then extended to the two-dimensional Coulomb gas and to periodic Riesz gases 1/|x|^s , 0 < s $\le$ 1. The extension to d $\ge$ 4 is also discussed.

Functional Analysis.title: On Some Lie Group Invariant noncommutative functions
Functional Analysis.summary: We study noncommutative polynomials and functions invariant under linear actions of infinite (compact Lie) groups, with a focus on $SU(2)$ acting on two noncommuting variables. For $SU(2)$, we give a complete description of the invariant noncommutative polynomials: there are no invariants of odd degree, and in degree $2n$ the invariants are exactly the span of the $S_{2n}$-orbit of $(XY-YX)^n$. We also construct an explicit basis recursively from the operation $(A,B)\mapsto XAYB-YAXB$, and show that the space of degree-$2n$ invariants has dimension equal to the $n$-th Catalan number. All proofs proceed by direct computation with the Haar integral.

Functional Analysis.title: The Beurling-type theorem for powers of weighted Bergman shifts
Functional Analysis.summary:
Let $\mathcal{B}_α$ denote the shift operator on the weighted Bergman space $A^2_α(\mathbb{D})$. We prove that, for every integer $k\geq1$, the Beurling-type theorem holds for $\mathcal{B}_α^k$ on $A^2_α(\mathbb{D})$
  if and only if $-1<α\leq1$. We also show that, for every $α>-1$, there exists a finite Blaschke product $B$ such that $M_{B}$ admits a cyclic invariant subspace but fails the wandering subspace property.

Functional Analysis.title: Characterization of Fourier transform of Hilbert space Valued functions
Functional Analysis.summary:
The aim of this paper is to obtain the characterization of Fourier transform for functions taking values in a separable Hilbert space $H$, defined on the groups $G=\R^n,\,G=\Z/n\Z$. In the first part of the paper, we consider the Fourier transform as a bijective mapping on $S_H$, the space of all $H$-valued smooth rapidly decaying functions on $\R^n$, which naturally extends bijectively to the dual space $S_H'$. Within this framework, we characterize the Fourier transform in terms of the convolution theorem, supplemented by additional structural properties of the Fourier transform. In the second part of the paper, we consider the discrete setting, where the Fourier transform is an operator on $L^1(\Z/n\Z, H)$, and we provide corresponding characterization based on its essential properties.
  In contrast to the classical setting, a key assumption in our framework involves the interplay between two distinct convolution operations. As a consequence, the structure of our proof diverges notably from the classical case and introduces additional complexities.

Functional Analysis.title: A BMO-type representation formula for the total variation of SBV functions in Heisenberg groups
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove a formula for the total variation of SBV functions in sub-Riemannian Heisenberg groups arising as the limit of certain BMO-type functionals.

Functional Analysis.title: A characterization of equality between de Branges--Rovnyak and Dirichlet spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We characterize when a de Branges--Rovnyak space coincides with a harmonically weighted Dirichlet space. We obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for this identification, which settles a long-standing open problem. We illustrate the result with several examples, that include measures supported on uncountable sets.

Functional Analysis.title: The sharp exponent for the Banach--Mazur distance to the cube
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $R_\infty(n)$ be the maximal Banach--Mazur distance from an $n$-dimensional real normed space to $\ell_\infty^n$. We prove that $R_\infty(n)\ge cn^{2/3}(\log(2n))^{-10}$. Together with the upper bound of Friedland, Naor, and Youssef, this gives $R_\infty(n) = n^{2/3+o(1)}$. The examples are polars of symmetric Gaussian polytopes with $2n$ generators, and the lower bound holds with exponentially high probability. A joint minimization over coefficient representations and positive weights yields an exact second-variation identity and sparse coefficients. A Gaussian projection argument controls all low-rank completions of the recorded matrix. An adaptive choice of exceptional generators then reduces the remaining case to a fixed-shift Gaussian small-ball estimate over two finite nets.

Functional Analysis.title: Rigidity of Exact Contractivity in the Complex Polynomial Bohnenblust--Hille Inequality
Functional Analysis.summary: The complex polynomial Bohnenblust--Hille inequality bounds the coefficient $\ell_{2m/(m+1)}$ norm of a complex $m$-homogeneous polynomial by its supremum norm, with a constant independent of the number of variables. For each fixed integer $N\ge3$, we characterize the choices of $N$ degree-$m$ monomials for which the inequality holds with optimal constant $1$ for every polynomial supported on them, provided $m$ exceeds an explicit threshold depending only on $N$. This holds precisely when their exponent vectors contain no nontrivial three-term arithmetic progression; equality for a nonzero polynomial then holds only for monomials. We also prove that, in the same degree range, every polynomial with at most $N$ nonzero coefficients that violates the constant-one inequality has a unique coefficient of maximal modulus, whose exponent is the center of such a progression in its support. Exact contractivity also follows from a comparability condition on the two largest coefficients, with a degree threshold that necessarily depends on the number of nonzero monomials.

Functional Analysis.title: Boundary Geometry Determines Optimal Shallow ReLU Approximation under Weighted Coefficient Constraints
Functional Analysis.summary: We study how boundary geometry affects $L^q$ approximation by shallow ReLU neural networks on convex bodies $K\subset\mathbb R^d$. The target classes are unit balls of weighted variation spaces that can enlarge classical spaces by incorporating domain geometry into constraints on output coefficients. We establish upper and lower bounds for arbitrary convex bodies and determine the optimal polynomial approximation exponents for all planar convex bodies and their products with polytopes, including cubes and circular cylinders. For $C^2$ convex bodies, we determine the optimal exponents in a dimension-dependent range of $q$ extending beyond $2$. When all principal curvatures are positive, the result extends to every finite $q\ge2$. For these classes, the dependence of the optimal exponent on the domain is captured by a single geometric growth exponent associated with small boundary caps. We also identify sharp weight thresholds for retaining the classical approximation exponent and improve previous weights on Euclidean balls while preserving the classical $L^2$ approximation rate. When the target is given as a finite ReLU network, the upper bounds can be realized by a compressed network using only the original neurons, without increasing the weighted coefficient sum. These results show that boundary geometry can change the optimal exponent even when dimension, error norm, and weighting rule are fixed.

Functional Analysis.title: A Bounded Closed Convex Set in $c_0(\mathbb{C})$ without Modulus Support Functionals
Functional Analysis.summary: We construct a bounded closed convex set in $c_0(\mathbb{C})$ on which no nonzero continuous complex-linear functional attains its maximum modulus. Consequently, this answers in the negative the two longstanding questions raised by Deville, Godefroy and Zizler in \cite[p. 35]{DGZ}. The construction uses a small perturbation of the identity on $c_0(\mathbb{R})$.

Functional Analysis.title: An $L^p$ Version of Raeburn's Symmetric Imprimitivity Theorem
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $1\leq p<\infty$. We prove an $L^p$-operator analogue of Raeburn's symmetric imprimitivity theorem for countable discrete groups. Let $A$ be an $L^p$-operator algebra with a contractive two-sided approximate identity, admitting a nondegenerate isometric representation on a $σ$-finite $L^p$-space. Given commuting free and proper actions of groups $G$ and $H$ on a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff space $Z$, together with commuting isometric actions on $A$, we show that the two corresponding full crossed products, and likewise the two reduced crossed products, are Morita equivalent as Banach algebras. The proof is organized through the linking groupoid. Its main analytic ingredient is a coefficient-valued spatial matrix dilation; in the reduced case we prove that this dilation preserves regularity after a Borel reindexing of the opposite corner. A pairing-valued approximate identity yields fullness and nondegeneracy.

Functional Analysis.title: Diffraction of rotated measures
Functional Analysis.summary: Consider a translation-bounded measure on the line. We can rotate the measure, distributing the mass proportionally to the area, to create a two-dimensional rotationally invariant translation-bounded measure. We show that the diffraction of the two-dimensional object is the normalised rotation of the diffraction of the original measure. We discuss some examples and generalisation beyond $d=2$.

Functional Analysis.title: Demi Weak Dunford-Pettis Operators
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, our main goal is to introduce the class of Demi Weak Dunford-Pettis operators. We also investigate its relationship with the classes of weak Dunford-Pettis and demi Dunford-Pettis operators, as well as conditions under which this class coincide with the classes of demi Dunford-Pettis and demicompact operators. In the final section, we study some properties of this new class in the setting of Banach lattices.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Critical Robin Problems on Manifolds with Noncompact Boundary
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We work on connected, noncompact $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds $(\mathcal{M}, g), n \geq 3$, that are complete with respect to $d_g$ and have noncompact boundary and bounded geometry. We study the existence of positive solutions in $C^{\infty}(\mathcal{M}) \cap L^{2^*}(\mathcal{M}) \cap L^{\infty}(\mathcal{M})$ to the Yamabe problem: $$ \left\{\begin{aligned} -Δ_g u+\frac{n-2}{4(n-1)} R_g u & =\mathscr{C}_0 u^{\frac{n+2}{n-2}} \quad \text { in } \mathcal{M}, \\ \frac{\partial u}{\partial ν}+\frac{n-2}{2(n-1)} H_g u & =\mathscr{C}_1 u^{\frac{n}{n-2}} \quad \text { on } \partial \mathcal{M}, \end{aligned}\right. $$ where $\mathscr{C}_0=Y_{\mathscr{C}}(\mathcal{M}), \mathscr{C}_1=Y_{\mathscr{C}}(\mathcal{M}) \mathscr{C} \bar{d}^{\frac{2}{n-2}}$, the parameter $\mathscr{C} \geq 0$ is fixed, and $$ Y_{\mathscr{C}}(\mathcal{M}):=\inf _{u \in C_c^{\infty}(\mathcal{M}) \backslash\{0\}} \frac{E_g(u)}{\left(\|u\|_{L^{2^*}(\mathcal{M})}^{2^*}+\mathscr{C}\|u\|_{L^{2^{\#}}(\partial \mathcal{M})}^{2^*}\right)^{2 / 2^*}} . $$ Here $E_g$ is the associated quadratic energy. We assume $Y_{\mathscr{C}}(\mathcal{M})<Y_{\mathscr{C}, \infty}(\mathcal{M})$ and $Y_{\mathscr{C}, \infty}(\mathcal{M})>0$, where $Y_{\mathscr{C}, \infty}$ is the corresponding variational level at infinity.
  We approach this problem using nonnegative solutions $u_j \in W_{\partial}^{1,2}\left(B_g(\mathcal{O}, j)\right), j \in \mathbb{N}, j \geq j_0$, for which we prove that $$ \sup _{j \geq j_0}\left\|u_j\right\|_{L^{\infty}\left(B_g(\mathcal{O}, j-1)\right)}<\infty . $$ For $\mathscr{C}>0$, we also prove that, along a subsequence, $\left\|u_j\right\|_{L^2{ }_{\left(B_g(\mathcal{O}, j) \cap \partial \mathcal{M}\right)}} \rightarrow \bar{d}$, with $0<\bar{d} \leq \mathscr{C}^{-1 / 2^*}$. For $\mathscr{C}=0$, we set $\bar{d}=0$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: $L^p$-theory for the exterior Stokes problem with Navier's type slip-without-friction boundary conditions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we consider the stationary Stokes equations in an exterior domain three-dimensional under a slip boundary condition without friction. We set the problem in weighted Sobolev spaces in order to control the behavior at infinity of the solutions. In this work, we try to investigate the existence and uniqueness up to an element of a nontrivial kernel of the weak solutions related to this problem in $L^p-$theory when $p>3$. Our proofs are based on obtaining inf-sup conditions that play a fundamental role.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Nonuniqueness of the $2$D Euler Evolutions with $L^1\cap L^p$ Vorticity
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For each prescribed $1<p<\infty$, we construct a compactly supported initial vorticity in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)\cap L^p(\mathbb{R}^2)$ that admits two distinct evolutions under the unforced two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation on $[0,1]$. Both vorticities are strongly continuous in $L^1\cap L^p$ and are transported exactly by their respective almost-everywhere invertible, measure-preserving regular Lagrangian flows. The construction couples unstable four-vortex configurations across increasingly small spatial scales, realizing them through concentrated signed vortex patches. At each finite cutoff, a prepared reference evolution remains close to rotating configurations, while a second evolution differs initially only at the finest scale. In the second evolution, the finest configuration consists of separating dipoles whose remote strain activates the instability of the next larger configuration. This process propagates through successive scales with summable transition times. As the cutoff tends to infinity, the two families of initial data converge strongly, along a subsequence, to the same datum, while a nonzero difference survives at a fixed larger scale and is detected by a fixed smooth observable at a positive limiting time. Quantitative concentration and relative comparison estimates establish this cascade for exact Euler patch solutions. Strong compactness through inverse-flow stability then preserves both exact vorticity transport and the positive-time distinction between the two limiting evolutions. The initial datum and construction parameters may depend on $p$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Sharp Uniqueness-Nonuniqueness Dichotomy for Neutral Vortex Arrays in $2$D Euler Equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish a sharp uniqueness--nonuniqueness criterion for the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equations within a class of stationary arrays of disjoint neutral vortices. Let $Θ$ be any finite nondecreasing envelope for the vorticity $L^p$ norms, and set $I_Θ=\int_{p_0}^\infty Θ(p)^{-1}\,dp$. If $I_Θ=\infty$, every array in the corresponding class admits a unique Euler evolution, even among bounded energy-admissible weak velocity solutions. If $I_Θ<\infty$, there exists a compactly supported array in the same class admitting two distinct unforced Lagrangian Euler evolutions from the same initial datum. The criterion holds for arbitrary nondecreasing envelopes $Θ$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp lifespan estimates for heat equations with Hörmander operators
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study the Cauchy problem $u_t-\mathcal L u=h(t)u^p$, $u(0)=\varepsilon u_0\ge0$, where $p>1$, $h\ge0$ is only locally integrable, and $\mathcal L=\sum_{j=1}^mX_j^2$ is a homogeneous Hörmander sum of squares on $\mathbb R^n$ of homogeneous dimension $q$. Diffusion spreads the solution out and weakens the nonlinearity, while the reaction $h(t)u^p$ may force blow-up. We prove that the outcome is decided by the single quantity $\mathcal{H}_{p,h}(T)=\int_0^Th(t)(1+t)^{-\frac q2(p-1)}\,d t$, in which the reaction at time $t$ is weighted by the factor by which diffusion has weakened the solution: small data are global if $\mathcal{H}_{p,h}(\infty)<\infty$, while otherwise the lifespan $T_\varepsilon$ satisfies $c\,\varepsilon^{-(p-1)}\le\mathcal{H}_{p,h}(T_\varepsilon)\le C\,\varepsilon^{-(p-1)}$ for small $\varepsilon$. Our technique of proof is based on a backward-semigroup functional combined with a Gaussian-envelope energy and an ODE cap telescoped along interlaced geometric grids. The result contains the Euclidean, Heisenberg, Carnot and Grushin cases, yields explicit lifespan laws for power, logarithmic, exponential, periodic and intermittent coefficients, and exhibits effects with no autonomous counterpart, such as a lifespan with no power law in $\varepsilon$. We also prove regularity and a priori estimates for classical solutions and discuss what remains true for a general nonlinearity $f(u)$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Joint inviscid, incompressible, and continuous phenotype limit in nonlocal models of tissue growth
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider a multispecies Brinkman tissue-growth system proposed by Debiec, Mandal, and Schmidtchen [J. Differential Equations 2025]. This system adopts a power pressure law determined by the total spatial density and models the effect of phenotype-dependent growth rates on the density dynamics of cells with different phenotypes. We examine the simultaneous vanishing-viscosity, stiff-pressure, and continuous-phenotype limit of this system. For families of bounded weak solutions with suitable initial conditions, every sequence converges, up to a subsequence, to a continuous-phenotype incompressible Darcy system, which presents a novel biological model. This result not only addresses connections between Brinkman tissue-growth systems with discrete phenotypes and those with continuous phenotypes, but also demonstrates the robustness of such connections under both the incompressible and inviscid limits.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: added a proof of vanishing defect measure, reorganized the manuscript

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global Well-Posedness of Landau Equation in Bounded Domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove global well-posedness of the Landau equation near a Maxwellian in bounded $C^3$ domains with in-flow or diffuse-reflection boundary conditions for $-3\leqγ\leq1$, including Coulomb interactions. Small compatible Gaussian perturbations generate global strong solutions, with uniqueness and continuous dependence among weak solutions. The proof combines energy estimates, the comparison principle, interior and weighted boundary estimates for velocity derivatives up to second order, and a logarithmic estimate for solution difference.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the existence of minimizers for the generalized liquid drop model
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider a broad class of generalized liquid drop models in which a perimeter term competes with repulsive nonlocal interactions with finite first moments. For all such kernels satisfying the natural physical assumption of reflection positivity we show existence of minimizers for all masses, in the (super-)critical regime. Moreover, in the subcritical regime we give the first quantitative estimate of the range of masses for which existence holds, which converges to the whole positive real line as one approaches the critical regime. This result builds on the nonlocal curvature approach introduced and developed in the periodic setting in \cite{dr24}.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Existence and uniqueness of radial bound states with prescribed number of nodes for nonlinear dispersive equations on spherically symmetric manifolds
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Standing waves $e^{iωt}u(x)$ of nonlinear dispersive equations, such as the nonlinear Schrödinger and Klein--Gordon equations, have a profile $u$ that solves the semilinear elliptic equation $Δu+f(u)=0$. We prove the existence of radial bound states with a prescribed number of nodal surfaces for this equation on a large class of spherically symmetric manifolds and for a broad class of nonlinearities $f$. Under further assumptions on the metric, we prove uniqueness of such bound states for the model nonlinearity $f(u)=|u|^{p-1}u-u$. Both existence and uniqueness results apply to the hyperbolic spaces $\mathbb{H}^n_λ$ of any curvature $-λ^2$ and dimension $n\geq 3$, and to some manifolds with a singularity at the origin.

Analysis of PDEs.title: An alternative proof of the Keel--Tao endpoint Strichartz estimates
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we give an alternative proof of the abstract endpoint Strichartz estimates proved by Keel and Tao. Our method is based on the near-far decomposition technique, which was developed in a recent work by Toyoshima and the author.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Quantitative propagation of chaos on arbitrary finite time intervals for the three-dimensional repulsive Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove quantitative propagation of chaos in total variation for repulsive Vlasov--Riesz--Fokker--Planck (VRFP) equations on $\mathbb{T}^d$ and $\mathbb{R}^d$ with unregularized interaction potentials with singularity $|x|^{-s}$, $0<s<d/2$. On every finite time interval on which the limiting classical solution satisfies the stated regularity assumptions, the particle marginals with a product initial law converge at an algebraic rate in the particle number, with constants growing at most exponentially in the marginal order. For the three-dimensional repulsive Vlasov--Poisson--Fokker--Planck (VPFP) equation on $\mathbb{R}^3$, a weighted $C^m$ initial probability density, $m\ge3$, with Gaussian velocity decay and polynomial spatial decay of order $M>3$ gives convergence to the global classical solution on every finite time interval. The proof combines conditioning of the initial product law with weighted BBGKY estimates. A decomposition of the potential and a bounded modification of the far-field force yield weighted bounds growing geometrically in the marginal order on the prescribed interval. A centered second-moment estimate permits summation of the error hierarchy, and a synchronous coupling transfers the estimate to the original dynamics.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp $L^2$ stability for anisotropic radial Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequalities
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish quantitative stability for radial Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequalities involving the anisotropic radial derivative and the Minkowski functional of a smooth, strictly convex body in $\mathbb R^N$, $N\ge2$. Here, the convex body need not be origin-symmetric. For the $L^2$-Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequality, we establish the sharp stability constant $|b+1-a|$ for $a\ne b+1$, and classify all equality cases in the natural weighted completion spaces, by optimizing over the angular coefficients and a common dilation parameter. We also obtain the sharp stability constants $2$ and $4$ for the scale-invariant and scale-noninvariant $L^2$-Heisenberg inequality, respectively. For $2\le p<\infty$, we also establish weighted stability of the anisotropic radial $L^p$-Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequalities when $a\neq b+1$ and $(b+1-a)(N-p(b+1))\geq0$, and the anisotropic radial $L^p$-Heisenberg inequalities. As a byproduct, we establish weighted $L^p$-Poincaré inequalities for Gamma measures, which serve as the main tool for our stability estimates.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Stationary Structures of the Boussinesq equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate the steady configurations supported by the inviscid two-dimensional Boussinesq equations in the periodic channel. We show steady laminar velocity fields (closed non-contractible fluid trajectories) coupled to non-decreasing density stratifications are necessarily stratified shear flows. The direction of density monotonicity along level sets is in fact fundamental: in striking contrast with the Euler equations, we exhibit laminar non-stagnant non-shear stationary solutions in the periodic channel. We also provide distinct flexibility and rigidity results (laminar persistence or appearance of islands for nearby non-shear solutions) close to stratified shear flows according to their stagnation points. As a by-product of our analysis, we establish a uniform Crandall-Rabinowitz bifurcation theorem that might be of independent interest.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Relativistic collision geometry and global near-vacuum solutions at critical transverse regularity
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish global well-posedness near vacuum for the relativistic Boltzmann equation with soft and hard potentials in the range $γ\in(-2,1]$. The initial data have critical Besov regularity of order $2/r$ in the transverse spatial variables for an admissible range of $r$ depending on $γ$, together with weighted integrability in the longitudinal and momentum variables. The proof combines a fixed-direction div--curl lemma with bilinear collision estimates. In particular, to control the gain term, we combine localization to spherical caps with energy-weighted angular estimates. The key relativistic estimate controls the singularity associated with the first component of the post-collisional relative velocity. These bounds yield the required time decay.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Nonuniqueness and failure of positivity preservation for doubly critical semilinear heat equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
At the Fujita exponent $p=1+2/N$ we construct a strictly positive mild solution of $u_t-Δu=|u|^{p-1}u$ in $\mathbb R^N$ whose initial trace in $L^1$ is zero. In similarity variables the solution approaches a Gaussian profile, and $$\|U(t)\|_1\sim C_N(\log(1/t))^{-N/2},\qquad
  \|U(t)\|_\infty\sim c_Nt^{-N/2}(\log(1/t))^{-N/2},$$ with explicit constants $C_N$ and $c_N$. In particular, uniqueness fails at the borderline logarithmic rate, and the solution lies outside every stronger logarithmic uniqueness class; this answers two questions raised by Miyamoto [J. Evol. Equ. 21 (2021), 151--166, Remark~1.6]. We also prove that, up to time translation, this is the only ancient solution of fixed sign of the rescaled equation that decays in a Gaussian weighted supremum norm. On a bounded smooth domain the whole-space solution can be localized at finitely many interior points, with independently chosen signs, on top of an arbitrary bounded initial datum. The resulting solutions are classical for $t>0$ and continuous at $t=0$ in $L^1$. Consequently, uniqueness fails for every bounded datum, and positivity is lost for every bounded nonnegative datum, $u_0\equiv1$ included. These results provide affirmative answers to Open Problems~3 and~4 posed by Brezis and Cazenave in [J. Anal. Math. 68 (1996), 277--304].

Analysis of PDEs.title: Drift-diffusion equations with saturation on $\mathbb{R}^d$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study a class of nonlinear drift--diffusion equations on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with saturation-type mobilities, not necessarily concave. Under structural assumptions on the mobility and potentials, bounded-domain approximations and local Caccioppoli estimates yield weak solutions for all positive times and an $L^1$-contraction estimate. The same estimates provide local space--time compactness of time translates, whose subsequential limits are weak solutions. Under additional confinement assumptions, uniform mass-tail estimates yield a mass-preserving, free-energy dissipating $C_0$-semigroup of $L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$-contractions. In this confining setting, every trajectory converges strongly in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to a stationary state with the same mass, and the resulting time-limit operator is an $L^1$-contraction. Under the same assumptions, we also identify the unique global and $L^1$-local minimiser of the free energy at each fixed mass and prove that it is stationary under the semigroup.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Boundary-Driven Nonequilibrium for the Coulomb Landau Equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish a nonlinear theory of the Coulomb Landau equation in smooth bounded domains with non-isothermal diffuse reflection. We construct a stationary state, prove its perturbative uniqueness and global nonlinear stability, and establish exponential convergence when the wall temperature approaches its stationary profile exponentially. We also establish stationary and global nonlinear well-posedness for prescribed inflow, together with asymptotic stability. The analysis combines a critical kinetic integrability gain with finite-exponent velocity-gradient estimates near grazing, allowing the nonlinear Coulomb estimates to close without $L_x^\infty$ control of velocity gradients.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: This arXiv preprint provides a detailed companion to the more concise journal-submission version of the same title. This version is not intended for separate journal publication. 413 pages. v2: minor revisions; results unchanged

Analysis of PDEs.title: Second variation of the fractional torsion energy and linear stability of the ball
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We compute the second shape derivative of the fractional torsion. It is an explicit quadratic form on the boundary, which involves a Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator for half-harmonic functions blowing up at the boundary. We deduce an explicit formula for volume preserving variations on the ball and show
  that as in the local case, the shape Hessian is negative and coercive in \(H^{1/2}\) modulo translations.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The fractional Faber--Krahn inequality in sharp quantitative form
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the fractional Laplacian satisfies the sharp quantitative Faber--Krahn inequality. This was conjectured by Brasco, Cinti and Vita, who proved the inequality with a sub-optimal exponent. The proof adapts to the non-local setting the level-set argument recently introduced by Guerra, Machado and Ramos for the Laplacian. It is carried out on the horizontal level sets of the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension of the torsion function, where the asymmetry appears only as a boundary value at the corner of the extension variables.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A decay estimate for cubic defocusing non-linear Schrödinger equation in three dimensions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this short note, we prove a decay estimate for non-linear solutions of the 3D cubic defocusing non-linear Schrödinger equation.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 16 pages. [v3] Final version. Published in J. Evol. Equ

Analysis of PDEs.title: Energy equality and renormalization of Navier-Stokes-Vlasov equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study weak solutions of the incompressible and the compressible Navier--Stokes--Vlasov systems on a bounded domain, where a viscous fluid is coupled to a dispersed particle phase through a drag force; the fluid obeys the no-slip boundary condition and the particles are subject to specular reflection. For solutions with Besov regularity, we show that the Vlasov equation is renormalizable in the sense of DiPerna--Lions, and we give regularity thresholds for the validity of the global energy equality. If the distribution function $f$ belongs to $B_p^{α,\infty}$ in space and velocity with time integrability $p$, and the fluid velocity $\mathbf{u}$ belongs to $B_q^{β,\infty}$ jointly in space and time with integrability $q$, then the energy equality holds provided $α+β>1$ and $β$ exceeds an explicit bound depending on $p$, $q$ and the dimension, under a natural integrability assumption on the pressure; an analogous criterion holds for the compressible system when the density is bounded from above and below. The condition $αp>1$ imposed on $f$ is not merely technical: it is exactly the range in which the macroscopic momentum flux possesses a boundary trace, so that the specular reflection condition passes to the macroscopic energy balance. When the particle phase is absent, our thresholds coincide with the criteria $β>\frac12+\frac1q$ and $β>\frac3q$ obtained by Yu for the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations alone. The proofs combine a boundary cutoff argument with commutator estimates based on a scale-localized Besov modulus, together with a boundary-strip analysis.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Submitted to Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal

Analysis of PDEs.title: Index and nullity of critical spherical catenoids in hyperbolic three-space
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that every critical spherical catenoid in a geodesic ball of hyperbolic three-space has Morse index four and nullity two. This resolves Medvedev's index conjecture throughout the parameter range of the catenoid family. The kernel consists precisely of the normal components of rotations that preserve the center of the ball and tilt the axis of the catenoid. As consequences, the radius of the supporting ball increases strictly along the family, and each critical spherical catenoid admits a smooth family of free boundary constant mean curvature deformations in its supporting ball. The proof combines a global boundary inequality obtained from a Wronskian, a positive Dirichlet eigenfunction supplied by the time component of the unit normal, and a Riccati comparison for the angular mode $k=2$. A ground-state identity then yields positivity of every angular mode $k\ge2$.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 14 pages. v2: added a corollary on equivariant nondegeneracy and free boundary CMC deformations (Corollary 11) and a self-contained proof that $r(a) \to 0$ as $a \to 1/2$ (Lemma 10); references added. Main theorem unchanged

Analysis of PDEs.title: Local $Tb$ theorems in non-homogeneous metric spaces, and applications to caloric measure
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We prove a local $Tb$ theorem with testing conditions on metric balls, for possibly non-doubling measures of polynomial growth on geometrically doubling metric spaces. It resolves the maximal-truncation version of Hofmann's local $Tb$ problem for all $1<p,q\leq\infty$, without assuming antisymmetry of the Calderón-Zygmund kernel. Our theorem allows accretive systems of complex testing measures satisfying a quantitative small-set condition; these measures need not be absolutely continuous with respect to the underlying measure. Testing requires only a one-level $L^0$ bound for maximal truncations, with an alternative for balls on which the underlying measure concentrates in a set of small relative diameter. We also remove antisymmetry from the known buffered and unbuffered fixed-truncation criteria. The proof combines a mixed corona decomposition adapted to the two testing systems with two-measure $L^2$ estimates for suppressed operators.
  As an application in the parabolic space $\mathbb P^n$, local time-directed $A_\infty$-type conditions on caloric and adjoint caloric measure imply $L^2(σ)$-boundedness of the spatial gradient of the heat single layer potential for boundary measures $σ$ with upper parabolic $(n+1)$-growth. This gives a parabolic counterpart of the harmonic-measure theorem of Mourgoglou and Tolsa without Ahlfors regularity, corkscrew or Harnack chain assumptions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Blow up and Concentration without Quantization: sharp Harnack type inequalities
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Motivated by the Onsager statistical mechanics description of turbulent Euler flows with point singularities, we refine the blow up analysis for sequences of solutions of a class of perturbed singular Liouville equations which share the phenomenon of ``blow up and concentration without quantization". The problem is delicate because we are dealing with the exact threshold value above which one meets the well known ``concentration without quantization" phenomenon, as recently pushed forward in [C.S. Lin, G. Tarantello, {\em C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris} (2016)] and in [Y. Lee, C.S. Lin, G. Tarantello, W. Yang, {\em Comm. PDE.} (2017)]. We overcome these difficulties by developing different strategies for ``fast" and ``slow" blow up, combining refined Pohozaev identities, elliptic estimates and ``Sup+CInf" inequalities in the same spirit of [C.C. Chen, C.S. Lin, {\em Comm. An. Geom.} (1998)]. In the process, we also derive a new sharp Harnack type inequality by using a moving-plane method, following the ideas in [D. Bartolucci, C.C. Chen, C.S. Lin, G. Tarantello, {\em Comm. P.D.E.} (2002)].
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 42 pages. Compared with the previous version, we have reorganized the paper, ruled out the possibility $λ_\infty=16π$ in CASE (I) of Theorem 3.1 and made minor simplifications and clarifications to some of the proofs to improve their readability. Moreover, we have added a section on the use of artificial intelligence. Comments are welcome!

Analysis of PDEs.title: Topological defect trains excited by a boundary discontinuity in the two-dimensional complex Ginzburg-Landau equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: With numerical simulations of the complex Ginzburg-Landau equation in a two-dimensional space, we find that a stationary but non-zero Dirichlet boundary condition with a discontinuity can drive a periodic train of evenly spaced topological defects that drift along and in proximity to the boundary.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A particle system approach towards the global well-posedness of master equations for potential mean field games of control
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper studies the $N$-particle systems as well as the HJB/master equations for a class of generalized mean field control (MFC) problems and the corresponding potential mean field games of control (MFGC). A local in time classical solution for the HJB equation is generated via a probabilistic approach based on the mean field maximum principle. Given an extension of the so called displacement convexity condition, we obtain the uniform estimates on the HJB equation for the $N$-particle system. Such estimates imply the displacement convexity/semi-concavity and thus the prior estimates on the solution to the HJB equation for generalized MFC problems. The global well-posedness of HJB/master equation for generalized MFC/potential MFGC is then proved thanks to the local well-posedness and the prior estimates. In view of the nature of the displacement convexity condition, such well-posedness is also true for the degenerated case. Our analysis on the $N$-particle system also induces an Lipschitz approximator to the optimal feedback function in generalized MFC/potential MFGC where an algebraic convergence rate is obtained. Furthermore, an alternative approximate Nash equilibrium is proposed based on the $N$-particle system, where the approximation error is quantified thanks to the aforementioned uniform estimates.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Brownian motion in Minkowski normed spaces
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
A Minkowski normed space is the Euclidean space equipped with a (possibly asymmetric) uniformly convex and smooth norm, forming a particular class of Finsler manifolds.
  We construct a stochastic process with one-dimensional time marginal densities given by the fundamental solution to the nonlinear Finsler heat equation in Minkowski normed spaces.
  This process is constructed as a solution to a singular McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equation and constitutes a nonlinear Markov process in the sense of McKean.
  We show that solutions to this stochastic differential equation are pathwise unique, and, thus, probabilistically strong solutions, though the equation has singular coefficients beyond the subcritical regime.
  Since our construction is a natural extension of the construction of standard Brownian motion from the standard heat kernel, we call this process \emph{Brownian motion in Minkowski normed spaces.}
  Furthermore, we obtain a universality property, namely that whichever Minkowski norm is chosen, the radial part of this process is the standard Bessel process.
  To the best of our knowledge, this is the first construction of stochastic processes associated with nonlinear heat equation in Finslerian spaces.

Analysis of PDEs.title: $γ$-Valued Stein--Tomas Restriction for Schatten Classes
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let $Σ\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a compact $C^2$ hypersurface with nonvanishing Gaussian curvature. We prove the sharp matrix-dimension-independent Schatten-valued Stein--Tomas range \[ R_Σ:L^p(\mathbb R^3;S^a)\longrightarrowγ(L^2(Σ),S^a), \qquad 1<a<\infty,\quad 1\le p\le\min\{a,4/3\}. \] The core endpoint is $E_Σ:γ(L^2(Σ),S^4)\to L^4(\mathbb R^3;S^4)$. After squaring the quartic norm, multiplication lands in the Hilbert--Schmidt class. A local coarea argument splits resonant quartets according to the shorter adjacent frequency chord, producing a dimension-free row/column estimate for elliptic and hyperbolic curvature. We also show that Gaussian type $4/3$ alone does not characterize the corresponding endpoint for arbitrary Banach spaces. Applications include matrix Herglotz waves, a two-dimensional Schrödinger $L^4$ estimate, and free spectral-measure bounds.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Exact Traces for Vector-Valued Morrey Spaces
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish an exact trace theorem for vector-valued time-Morrey spaces and complementary continuity theorems for time-BMO evolution classes. For a Banach couple $X_1\hookrightarrow X_0$, $1<p<\infty$ and $0<λ<1$, we prove that the trace of the class $u\in\mathcal M^{p,λ}(X_1)$, $u_t\in\mathcal M^{p,λ}(X_0)$ is exactly $(X_0,X_1)_{θ,\infty}$, where $θ=1-(1-λ)/p$. A constructive extension realizes every admissible trace, and counterexamples establish optimality of both the smoothness exponent and the weak fine index. Time-BMO control yields continuous finite-index interpolation traces and, under a mixed boundedness hypothesis, a logarithmic time modulus whose base-space logarithm is necessary. For the quadratic viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation on the torus, we characterize the bounded initial data generating Morrey-regular solutions by the exact Besov condition $u_0\in B_{2,\infty}^{2θ}$. The proof uses Hopf--Cole linearization and a direct composition argument, and requires no smallness assumption. Lacunary nonlinear solutions realize the sharp trace threshold. A forced Hamilton--Jacobi example exhibits genuinely logarithmic time regularity, and a forward--backward mean-field-game system illustrates initial and terminal trace compatibility. \par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Keywords:} Morrey spaces; trace spaces; real interpolation; Hamilton--Jacobi equations; bounded mean oscillation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A nonlocal transport problem describing pore growth
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study a nonlocal transport problem describing pore growth in a biological membrane exposed to a periodic electric potential, where the growth term is modified through the first moment of the solution $n_1(t)$. We show that for initial data $f_0$ with noncompact support it holds $n_1(t) \rightarrow \infty$ , whereas for $f_0$ with compact support the limit of $n_1$ depends sensitively on the data. For a broad class of initial data we additionally obtain $n_1 \sim t^{\frac{1}{2}}$. In the case of a constant external potential we further prove that solutions converge to the self-similar solution having the same tail behaviour as $f_0$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Local boundedness for solutions to parabolic double phase problems
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we investigate the local boundedness of weak solutions to parabolic double phase equations of type $$u_t-\mathrm{div}(|Du|^{p-2}Du+a(x,t)|Du|^{q-2}Du)=0\quad\text{in }Ω_T:=Ω\times(0,T),$$ where $0\leq a(\cdot)\in L^\infty(Ω_T)$ and $\frac{2n}{n+2}<p<q<p\left(\frac{n+2}{n}\right)$, so that both the degenerate range $p\geq 2$ and the singular range $p<2$ are covered. To this end, we derive the Caccioppoli inequality and recall a parabolic embedding theorem, which are then utilized in an iteration method.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Liouville theorem for plurisubharmonic functions with periodic complex Monge-Ampère measure
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study entire continuous plurisubharmonic solutions of the complex Monge-Ampère equation $(i\partial\bar\partial u)^n=2^n n!μ$ in $\mathbb{C}^n$, in the Bedford-Taylor sense, where $μ\not\equiv 0$ is a nonnegative locally finite Borel measure periodic with respect to a lattice of full real rank.
